articles.title: Marlins Open To Corner Infield/Outfield Addition
body: The Marlins have a wide array of potential targets as the offseason gets underway. Barry Jackson of The Miami Herald reports that the Fish are seeking at least one external addition to both the rotation and the bullpen. According to Jackson, they’re also open to bringing in an everyday position player at either a corner infield or outfield spot.

That leaves the front office with ample roster flexibility, a luxury of being well-positioned up the middle already. Miami has defensive stalwart Joe Mack behind the plate and a strong middle infield duo of Otto Lopez and Xavier Edwards. They’re well positioned long term in center field with Jakob Marsee as well, though they could look for a stopgap there because Marsee required postseason internal brace surgery. That came with a six-month recovery window that makes him doubtful for Opening Day if the season begins on time.

Miami was a league average offensive team in 2026. They ranked 18th in scoring, 23rd in home runs, and 16th in slugging percentage. They were in the top ten in batting average and on-base percentage but were a bit light in terms of true impact bats. It’s not surprising they’re open to an offensive acquisition in a corner, where most of their players have positional flexibility.

Kyle Stowers was a full-time first baseman in the second half. He has an outfield background and could move back there if the Fish brought in a first baseman. Javier Sanoja is the projected starter at third base. That looked like the offense’s biggest question mark for a while, but he finished the season on a tear.

articles.title: Mets To Add A.J. Ellis To Coaching Staff
body: The Mets are hiring former big league catcher A.J. Ellis as major league strategy coordinator, reports Will Sammon of The Athletic. He’ll be on Andy Green’s coaching staff.

Ellis logged parts of 11 seasons in the big leagues during his playing career. He spent the vast majority of that time as a backup with the Dodgers. Ellis was highly regarded as a game-caller behind the plate and forged a strong battery with Clayton Kershaw throughout the best seasons of Kershaw’s future Hall of Fame career.

The former 18th-round pick also played for the Phillies and Marlins before finishing his career with the Padres in 2018. That was Green’s penultimate season as San Diego’s manager. Ellis jumped right into a front office role with the Padres after that season. His special assistant role in San Diego is the extent of his post-playing experience, but Ellis received some attention from the White Sox during their managerial search in 2024. He’ll now reunite with Green as he makes the move into coaching.

Ellis is the second addition to the Mets’ staff, as they also tabbed Mariano Duncan for an unspecified role last month. They’re still looking to add another voice on the offensive side after removing director of hitting Jeff Albert from the coaching staff at season’s end.

articles.title: Angels Yet To Begin Interviewing GM Candidates While Awaiting Sale Approval
body: The Angels have yet to start interviewing candidates for their top position in baseball operations, interim general manager John Mozeliak tells reporters (including Jeff Fletcher of The Orange County Register). Mozeliak, who’s under contract through December, remains in charge of the front office as the offseason gets underway.

It’s a less than ideal spot that’s a product of the Angels’ pending sale. Arte Moreno agreed to sell the franchise to Stan Kroenke’s group (officially known as Kroenke Sports & Entertainment) on September 1 at a $4 billion franchise valuation. That’s awaiting official approval from the other 29 owners, however. The timing on that varies but frequently takes a few months. The most recently approved franchise sale (Padres) was agreed upon in mid-April and not finalized until August 17.

Moreno fired former GM Perry Minasian and tabbed Mozeliak on an interim basis on June 26. They gave Mozeliak the autonomy to trade controllable starter José Soriano to Toronto for a package led by shortstop prospect Arjun Nimmala. However, the ownership change seemingly ensured that Mozeliak would not hold the GM role for the long term. He told reporters a few weeks ago that he’s not a candidate for the full-time job and intended to step away once a new hire was in place. The Angels also moved on from skipper Kurt Suzuki.

articles.title: Mets Notes: Bichette, Sato, First Base
body: Back in August, the Mets were connected to Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato, who is now available via the posting system. This week, a report from Tim Britton and Will Sammon of The Athletic suggests that the club is less likely to make a push there now that infielder Bo Bichette has opted to stay in Queens.

Sato has put up big offensive numbers in his career in Nippon Professional Baseball. His future defensive home is more of a question but his primary position in NPB has been third base. Some scouts believe he would be a subpar defender at the hot corner if placed there right now. If that assessment is true, then his future team will need to either develop his skills at third or move him elsewhere. He has a decent amount of right field experience. He also could presumably move from third to first, as many players have done over the years.

For the Mets, it’s possible to fit him in there but it wouldn’t be perfect. Now that Bichette has opted in, he projects as the everyday third baseman next year. Per the report from Britton and Sammon, the Mets were satisfied with Bichette’s move from shortstop to third in 2026. In the outfield, the Mets project to have Juan Soto, A.J. Ewing and Carson Benge in three spots.

articles.title: Phillies Likely To Pursue Left-Handed Setup Man
body: The Phillies have a long to-do list this offseason, with needs in the outfield, the bullpen and at third base (among others). Regarding the bullpen, Matt Gelb of The Athletic writes that Philadelphia will be in the market to add a left-handed setup reliever to help bridge the gap to star closer Jhoan Duran.

It’s a sensible pursuit. The 28-year-old Duran is one of the game’s best relievers, and the Phils have some quietly solid right-handed options already in their high-leverage mix. Last offseason’s swap of veteran lefty Matt Strahm for Royals righty Jonathan Bowlan proved to be a heist after Bowlan delivered 56 1/3 innings of 3.36 ERA ball with a 31.9% strikeout rate, 6.6% walk rate and 47.8% ground-ball rate. He’s controlled for five more years. Flamethrowing young righty Alex McFarlane posted a 1.83 ERA in the minors before debuting with 19 innings of 2.84 ERA ball (25.3% strikeout rate, 8.9% walk rate, 45.3% grounder rate).

That gives the Phils a formidable trio of righties late in games, but the left-handed group is more lacking. Southpaw Tim Mayza already re-signed on a one-year deal worth $2.75MM, but the Phillies primarily used him in middle relief. Fellow lefty Tanner Banks is a non-tender candidate after posting an ugly 6.19 ERA in 36 1/3 innings. Banks had a strong 2025 showing, but he’s 35 and posted career-worst walk, ground-ball and home-run rates in 2026. Twenty-eight-year-old Kyle Backhus had nice numbers in Triple-A but barely kept his ERA south of 5.00 in 20 MLB frames. He has a 4.76 ERA overall in 45 1/3 major league innings.

articles.title: Tigers To Hire Kyle Hudson As First Base Coach
body: The Tigers are expected to add Kyle Hudson as their first base coach, per WEEI’s Rob Bradford. Hudson was most recently with the Red Sox as third base coach.

Detroit moved on from first base coach Anthony Sanders at the end of this season. He was only with the club for one year. Third base coach Joey Cora was let go midway through the season. He was replaced by Billy Boyer.

Hudson spent parts of four seasons in Boston. He first came aboard as the first base coach in 2023. He moved across the diamond the following season. Hudson was part of the mass firings near the end of April. After a slow start to the season, the Red Sox moved on from manager Alex Cora and most of his coaching staff. Hudson was replaced by Chad Epperson.

The Tigers have been among the least-active teams on the basepaths in recent seasons. They’ve ranked 24th or worse in stolen bases for five straight years. Those rankings could certainly be personnel-related. The 2027 lineup could feature more speed with a full season of Max Clark. Kevin McGonigle was also more active as a base stealer in the minors than as a rookie last year, so perhaps he improves on his 12 steals.

articles.title: Astros To Interview Albert Pujols, Morgan Ensberg For Managerial Job
body: The Astros’ search for a new manager has two more candidates. Cardinals legend Albert Pujols will receive an interview this week, as first reported by Mike Rodriguez of Rompiendo Sports. Former Astro Morgan Ensberg will also get an interview this week, per Brian McTaggart of MLB.com.

Both Pujols and Ensberg have connections to new Astros GM Randy Flores. Pujols and Flores overlapped for five seasons in St. Louis. Ensberg played with Flores in college at USC. Houston is also interviewing Rangers’ bench coach Luis Urueta and Yankees bench coach Brad Ausmus for the manager gig.

Pujols was frequently in the conversation for manager openings last winter. He seemed to have the Angels job in hand before talks broke down between the two sides. Pujols has previous experience managing in the Dominican League and most recently with the Dominican Republic national team. He was the club’s skipper for the 2026 World Baseball Classic. Team DR reached the semifinals, but came up short against Team USA.

Houston fans would have to adjust their attitude toward the former Cardinal if he gets the gig. Pujols was a nemesis of the Astros as a player when both teams were in the NL Central. He slugged 62 home runs against Houston, more than any other opponent. Pujols delivered an all-time playoff moment against the Astros in Game 5 of the NLCS with a three-run blast off closer Brad Lidge.

articles.title: Reds Announce Joe Torres As Pitching Coach
body: The Reds announced that Joe Torres has been hired as their new pitching coach. He has previously been serving as the assistant pitching coach with the Guardians. He will replace Derek Johnson, who was the previous pitching coach in Cincinnati.

Cincinnati hired Johnson in October of 2018 and he was still officially on the job in 2026. However, he took a personal leave of absence in June and was away from the club for the final months of the season. The Reds announced last month that Johnson would not be returning.

Reds manager Terry Francona was hired in October of 2024 and inherited Johnson. To fill the vacancy, Francona has turned to his old staff. Francona was the skipper in Cleveland from 2013 to 2023. Torres was in the organization for much of that span. He joined the big league staff as assistant pitching coach in January of 2022, replacing Ruben Niebla, who left to become pitching coach in San Diego. Torres was working in Cleveland’s minor league system for five years prior to that, so he and Francona surely crossed paths often.

It always tough to connect a club’s on-field results to one specific coach but the Guardians organization is one with a strong reputation for pitching development. In 2026, Gavin Williams seemingly emerged as a true ace. Parker Messick is a Rookie of the Year finalist after his breakout season. Cade Smith’s first year as a full-time closer resulted in 41 saves and a 1.95 earned run average.

articles.title: Nationals Release Zak Kent
body: The Nationals are releasing right-hander Zak Kent, per a team announcement. Kent was designated for assignment last week.

The 28-year-old Kent was bumped off the roster after Washington claimed right-hander Braxton Roxby off waivers from San Francisco. He apparently passed through waivers himself, and the Nationals chose to move on. Kent is now a free agent.

Kent spent most of the year in Washington’s organization, but it was a wild ride to get there. He was designated for assignment by the Guardians last winter. Kent was then claimed and DFAed by the Cardinals, Rangers, and Cardinals again. The Twins claimed and actually kept him for a bit. Kent pitched in two games for the Twins before being DFAed again. Washington scooped him up in early May.

The Nationals called on Kent whenever they needed a fresh arm in the bullpen. He had three separate stints with the big-league club. Kent posted a 5.68 ERA across 12 2/3 innings with Washington. He had similar struggles at Triple-A Rochester, recording an ERA up near 5.00 in 32 appearances.

Kent throws from an over-the-top arm angle at 52 degrees. Only 15 qualified righties had an arm angle above that number this season. It’s a prototype that the Nationals tried out frequently in 2026. Righties Clayton Beeter and Gus Varland, who took turns as Washington’s closer early in the season, both have arm angles above 50 degrees. They’d theoretically pair nicely with the lower slots of Brad Lord, Yovanny Cruz, and Jack Sinclair. It didn’t work out this season and the unit will likely look plenty different in 2027.

articles.title: David Bell Leaves Blue Jays’ Front Office
body: Blue Jays executive David Bell has left his position with the team, reports Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic. Bell served as assistant general manager and vice president of baseball operations for the past two seasons.

“I decided to step away and reassess where I can make the greatest impact, on and off the field,” Bell told The Athletic. “The Toronto Blue Jays are a first-class organization. I have a deep appreciation for the people I’ve worked with over the past two years.”

Shi Davidi of Sportsnet reports that the organization will look for someone to take over Bell’s duties. He adds that Bell was involved in player acquisitions and also oversaw the player development and performance departments.

Toronto still has two AGMs, Joe Sheehan and Michael Murov, operating under general manager Ross Atkins. The organization also has James Click (baseball strategy) and Jeremy Reesor (baseball operations) in vice president positions.

The gig with the Blue Jays was the first foray into the front office for Bell. Before coming to Toronto, he’d spent six seasons as the manager of the Reds. Cincinnati made the playoffs once in his half-dozen years with the club. He was fired at the tail end of the 2024 season. Bell had previously worked in various roles for the Cubs, Cardinals, and Giants.

articles.title: Athletics Hire Brewers’ Cam Castro As General Manager
body: 12:03 pm CT: The A’s have officially announced the hiring of Castro.

10:31 am CT: The Athletics are hiring Brewers senior vice president of player development and performance Cam Castro as their new general manager, reports Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic. He’ll serve as the No. 2 executive under newly hired president of baseball operations Taylor Smith.

Castro, who’d been with the Brewers organization since 2019, has an extensive background in pitching development. He worked at Driveline more than a decade ago and was the head baseball coach for Division-II Lake Erie College before being hired by Milwaukee as a minor league pitching coach. He quickly climbed the ladder in the Brewers organization, ascending to minor league pitching coordinator, then director of pitching development and eventually vice president of player development, before being promoted to his most recent title following the 2024 season.

Pitching development has been an Achilles heel for the A’s for more than a decade. They’ve cultivated an impressive core of largely homegrown bats; Nick Kurtz, Tyler Soderstrom, Jacob Wilson, Henry Bolte and Zack Gelof were all Athletics draftees. Catcher Shea Langeliers was a Braves pick but was traded to the A’s before ever making his big league debut. It’s a strong group of bats that give the soon-to-be Las Vegas A’s a nice foundation.

articles.title: Cardinals To Hire Joel McKeithan As Hitting Coach
body: The Cardinals are set to hire White Sox assistant hitting coach Joel McKeithan as their new hitting coach, Robert Murray of Fansided reports. He’ll take over for Brant Brown, who spent the past two seasons as hitting coach in St. Louis but was dismissed last month.

The 35-year-old McKeithan spent the past two seasons as an assistant hitting coach with the White Sox. He’d previously been both an assistant hitting coach and lead hitting coach with the Reds. McKeithan has also worked as a minor league hitting coach in both the Phillies and Tigers organizations.

White Sox hitters mashed 211 homers and walked at a 9.5% clip in 2026. Both marks were the fifth-best in baseball. On the whole, they posted a.236/.320/.406 batting line that was about 4% better than average, by measure of wRC+. The Cards hit.239/.313/.378 as a team, giving them the fifth-worst wRC+ (93) in the sport. They hit the seventh-fewest home runs in MLB (167) and tied with the Twins for the fifth-worst walk rate (8.3%). Obviously, any successes and failures of a team are attributable to far more than just one individual coach, but it’s still not a surprise to see the Cardinals draw their new top hitting instructor from an organization that had a more productive all-around year.

To this point, Brown has been the only coach dismissed from manager Oli Marmol’s staff. Third base coach Pop Warner and outfield/baserunning coach Jon Jay were on expiring contracts, but Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch reported last month that both are expected back for the 2027 season.

articles.title: Cubs Outright Tyler Austin
body: The Cubs sent first baseman Tyler Austin outright off their 40-man roster this week, according to the MLB.com transaction log. Chicago’s offseason roster count drops to 34.

Austin signed a $1.25MM contract last December. The righty hitter had spent the previous six seasons with the Yokohama DeNA BayStars in Japan. Austin mashed in his final two NPB seasons and impressed Cubs evaluators enough to secure a big league deal. He was expected to compete for a platoon role to complement Michael Busch.

Those plans were unfortunately scuttled by a right knee injury. Austin required a debridement surgery to repair the patellar tendon in late February. He neither played in Spring Training nor during the regular season. Austin, who’s best known for his early-career stint with the Yankees, hasn’t appeared in an MLB game since 2019. He’s a.219/.292/.451 hitter with 33 homers in 583 big league plate appearances.

Austin remains in the organization for now. He has the right to elect free agency, and it’s unclear if he intends to give things another go with the Cubs or attempt to find a guaranteed contract back in Japan.

Busch handled left-handed pitching well in 2026 (.243/.348/.422 in 204 plate appearances) and wound up starting all but four games. The Cubs probably aren’t going to devote an active roster spot to a short side platoon first baseman/designated hitter. They have a couple utility players, Matt Shaw and Pedro Ramírez, who can pick up the scattered start at the position if they’re not traded for pitching this winter.

articles.title: Neander: Rays Have “Every Intention Right Now” Of Holding Drew Rasmussen
body: The Rays’ biggest question this offseason is whether to trade ace Drew Rasmussen. Tampa Bay had an easy call to exercise his $20MM option after what’ll almost certainly be the righty’s second straight top 10 finish in Cy Young balloting. That doesn’t preclude the possibility of a trade, as Rasmussen is set to make the largest salary for any player in team history.

Trading Rasmussen as he enters his final year under contract would be a typical Rays move. Tampa Bay’s run to the third AL title in club history may point to them operating differently in this case. President of baseball operations Erik Neander told reporters on Tuesday that the team’s early-offseason plan is keep Rasmussen as their #1 starter for 2027 (link via Marc Topkin of The Tampa Bay Times).

“(It’s) not a declarative this, that, whatever, but I can sit here very confidently and say that every intention right now is thinking about ‘Ras’ anchoring our rotation and how to make this team better going into next year,” Neander said. At a different point in the media scrum, he said the team “(wants) to have ‘Ras” back. We’re going into this offseason when you were that close to where we were, it’s hard to think we’ll be closer if ‘Ras’ isn’t part of the team.”

articles.title: Luis Urueta To Interview For Astros’ Managerial Job
body: The Astros will interview Rangers’ bench coach Luis Urueta as part of their ongoing managerial search, reports Jon Morosi of The MLB Network. Yankees bench coach Brad Ausmus also received an official interview, reports Jon Heyman of The New York Post. Brian McTaggart of MLB.com reported last week that Ausmus was in Houston to speak with the club before they hired Randy Flores as their general manager on Friday.

Hiring a manager is the most immediate task for Flores, who’s running a baseball operations department for the first time. Owner Jim Crane told reporters during Monday’s introductory press conference that Flores would have “full authority” to lead the front office (link via Chandler Rome of The Athletic).

Crane has a reputation as one of the most hands-on owners in MLB. To that end, he acknowledged interviewing multiple managerial candidates before the team hired Flores. Crane was running baseball operations for a couple months with input from senior advisor Jeff Bagwell and assistant GMs Charles Cook, Connor Huff, and Gavin Dickey.

Ausmus played parts of 10 seasons with the Astros. He’s a longtime teammate of Bagwell’s, though his tenure ended before Crane purchased the franchise in 2011. Ausmus has had multiple interviews with the Astros over the years. He spoke with the team about their managerial vacancy in 2020 before they hired Dusty Baker. Three years later, he was reportedly among the finalists for the GM position that went to Dana Brown.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Houston Astros
body: The Astros won the American League West this year but mostly due to the historic weakness of the division. On the whole, it was a disappointing season and change is in the air. There will be a new front office leader and new manager for 2027. It’s possible the roster sees significant turnover as well.

Carlos Correa, SS: $60.5MM through 2028 (Twins still owe $30MM as part of trade; contract includes club/vesting options for 2029-2032) Yordan Alvarez, LF/DH: $52MM through 2028 Jose Altuve, 2B: $50MM through 2029 Josh Hader, LHP: $38MM through 2028 Tatsuya Imai, RHP: $36MM through 2028 (Imai declined post-2026 opt-out; can opt out after 2027) Cristian Javier, RHP: $21MM through 2027 Christian Walker, 1B: $20MM through 2027 Option Decisions

Tatsuya Imai, RHP: declined to opt out of two years and $36MM remaining Isaac Paredes, IF: club exercised $13.35MM option Ryan Weiss, RHP: team declined $5MM option in favor of $500K buyout 2027 financial commitments: $168.35MM Total future commitments: $261.35MM

Peter Lambert (5.069): $4.6MM Jeremy Peña (5.000): $13.1MM Hunter Brown (4.035): $6.8MM Yainer Diaz (4.035): $6.3MM Hayden Wesneski (3.170): $1.8MM Nick Allen (3.164): $1.8MM Bennett Sousa (3.156): $1.3MM Taylor Trammell (3.143): $1.5MM Ronel Blanco (3.100): $1.4MM Non-tender candidates: Sousa, Trammell, Blanco

articles.title: Marlins Release Bradley Blalock
body: The Marlins released right-hander Bradley Blalock, according to the MLB.com transaction tracker. Kevin Barral of Fish On First suggests that the 25-year-old is likely to pursue an overseas opportunity. Miami’s 40-man roster tally drops to 35.

Blalock spent one season in South Florida. The Marlins acquired him from the Rockies in January. Blalock made four MLB appearances in a mop-up role, allowing seven runs in 11 1/3 innings. He spent the rest of the season working as a starting pitcher with Triple-A Jacksonville. Blalock pitched 110 frames with a 5.56 ERA in the minors. He recorded roughly average strikeout (21.2%), walk (9.5%), and ground-ball (46.5%) marks.

A former 32nd round draft pick, Blalock has pitched parts of three seasons in MLB. He has allowed nearly eight earned runs per nine innings across 100 2/3 career frames. The 6’2″ righty also has an unimpressive 6.53 ERA at the Triple-A level, but some of that is driven by a nightmare season in the extremely hitter-friendly setting with the Rox’s affiliate in Albuquerque. Blalock throws seven pitches and averaged 96 mph with his fastball during his MLB work this year.

articles.title: Rangers President: 2027 Payroll To Be Similar To 2026
body: Rangers president of baseball operations Chris Young met this week with members of the media, including Evan Grant of The Dallas Morning News, to talk about various topics related to the club. He said the aim will be for the 2027 club to be competitive will running a “very similar” payroll to 2026.

According to the MLBTR Payroll Tracker, the Rangers had a cash/LRD payroll of $193MM this year, with a competitive balance tax number of $219MM. The club’s 2027 numbers are projected to be $175MM and $194MM, respectively, both about $20MM lower than in the season that just finished.

$20MM is a lot of money for a normal person but isn’t a ton of spending capacity for a major league club these days. The Rangers went 80-82 this year and have a lot of holes to fill. In a sense, they don’t need to improve too much, as it only took 81 wins for the Astros to take the A.L. West this year. But it seems safe to assume that was a historic low and it will take at least a win total in the mid-80s next year, if not higher.

articles.title: Rays’ Edwin Uceta Undergoes Shoulder Surgery
body: Rays right-hander Edwin Uceta underwent arthroscopic surgery on his right shoulder last month, president of baseball operations Erik Neander revealed in a session with the media earlier today (link via Marc Topkin of the Tampa Bay Times). Specifics aren’t clear, but Neander added that Uceta is expected to miss at least the first couple months of the 2027 season.

Uceta was a minor league pickup in the 2023-24 offseason who’d previously pitched with the Dodgers, D-backs, Mets and Cubs organizations. He came to the Rays with a career 5.80 ERA in 40 1/3 frames, but like so many other small-scale Rays pickups found a home in Tampa Bay. From 2024-25, Uceta pitched 117 2/3 innings with a 2.98 ERA. He fanned exactly one-third of his opponents, limited walks at a tidy 7.3% clip and induced some decidedly poor batted-ball metrics from opponents (88.1 mph average exit velocity, 34.8% hard-hit rate).

Before long, Uceta had found himself in a high-leverage role. He saved five games and tallied seven holds late in the’24 campaign, and he was one of manager Kevin Cash’s go-to setup arms in 2025 when he notched 21 holds (plus one rogue save). He looked locked into a setup role entering the 2026 campaign.

articles.title: Report: Orioles Open To Trade Offers On Majority Of Roster
body: The Orioles are going into the offseason with a very open mind, reports Andy Kostka of The Baltimore Banner. Per Kostka’s report, first baseman Pete Alonso is the only untouchable player on the roster. The O’s are open to offers on everyone else as they look to upgrade the rotation, the outfield and the catcher position.

It’s worth emphasizing that there’s a difference between actively trying to trade players and being open to offers, a distinction that Kostka clearly makes in his report. Still, it’s notable that the Baltimore front office is going into the offseason with the willingness to consider sweeping changes.

The openness is certainly understandable. The Orioles did a big tank job from 2018 to 2021, placing themselves as one of the worst clubs in baseball for that stretch in order to stockpile young talent. There was no draft lottery at that time, making that strategy more viable. They then won 101 games in 2023 with a young core featuring Gunnar Henderson, Kyle Bradish, Adley Rutschman and many others. It felt like a dynasty was brewing.

Instead, things have changed in more recent years, and not for the better. Many of the club’s planned core players have regressed or haven’t panned out. The team still snagged a Wild Card spot in 2024 but has finished below.500 in each of the past two seasons. After that slide, it seems the desire for change is there. Rutschman was surprisingly flipped to the Red Sox at the deadline. Perhaps more players who were once viewed as cornerstones in Baltimore will end up wearing different uniforms.

articles.title: Cubs Decline Javier Assad’s Option; Assad Remains Under Team Control
body: The Cubs declined their $3.3MM club option on righty Javier Assad yesterday, reports Jordan Bastian of MLB.com. He remains under club control as an arbitration-eligible player. The team didn’t formally announce the decision at any point.

Assad played the 2026 season on a one-year, $1.8MM deal that included a $3.3MM club option for 2027. He and the Cubs agreed to that deal last winter, buying out his first arb year and giving the team some cost certainty in the event that Assad had a big year. Instead, the righty split the season between Triple-A Iowa and Chicago, functioning primarily as a swingman when he was on the big league roster.

In 94 1/3 major league innings, Assad posted a 3.63 ERA. He did so with a 16.1% strikeout rate that was six percentage points shy of average but also a strong 7.1% walk rate. Assad picked up a pair of three-inning saves but otherwise didn’t log a save or hold. He was generally used as an opener and long reliever, operating most frequently in low- and medium-leverage settings.

The price tag on Assad’s club option came in well north of the $2.3MM figure he’s projected to earn in arbitration (via MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz). Given that discrepancy, it’s not a surprise to see the Cubs turn down that option. He’ll likely negotiate a new deal that locks in some money for 2027 but saves the Cubs $1MM or so, give or take. It’s a small bit of cost-savings but does have a compounding factor; since Assad’s 2027 salary will be lower, so too will any potential raise he’ll receive heading into the 2028 campaign — his final season of club control.

articles.title: Cardinals To Re-Sign Josh Fleming
body: Veteran lefty Josh Fleming is headed back to the Cardinals on a minor league deal, per Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. Fleming spent the final month of the season at Triple-A Memphis.

The Blue Jays brought Fleming in on a minor league deal last offseason. He didn’t break camp with the club, but was up by the second week of the season. Fleming was knocked around for four earned runs over three innings in his lone appearance with Toronto. He was designated for assignment, passed through waivers, and re-upped with the Blue Jays on a minor league deal.

Toronto cut Fleming in early July. He latched on with the Cubs, but that lasted just over a month. He finally found his way to the Cardinals organization for the final stretch of the season. After posting a low-3.00s ERA at Triple-A with the Blue Jays’ and Cubs’ affiliates, Fleming struggled with Memphis. He was tagged for 21 earned runs over 29 2/3 innings. Fleming gave up nine homers in six starts.

St. Louis didn’t have many proven options in the rotation entering the season, but the unit performed relatively well. It was also a remarkably durable group. Michael McGreevy, Kyle Leahy, Andre Pallante, and Matthew Liberatore each made 29+ starts. Dustin May also made 31 starts, but 10 of them came with Milwaukee after he was moved at the trade deadline. Quinn Mathews stepped into the rotation for the last two months of the year.

articles.title: Rockies Return RJ Petit To Tigers
body: The Rockies have returned 2025 Rule 5 pick RJ Petit to the Tigers, per a team announcement. The right-hander missed the entire 2026 campaign while recovering from Tommy John surgery.

Colorado took Petit with the top selection in last year’s Rule 5 draft. He was coming off a strong minor league season that saw him post a 2.44 ERA with a 29.5% strikeout rate between Double-A and Triple-A. Petit made three Spring Training appearances with the Rockies in 2026. He had TJ in March.

The 27-year-old Petit will head back to Detroit to continue recovering from the surgery. It’s unclear how much he’ll pitch this season, if at all. The injury came at a brutal time for a young arm seemingly on the brink of his MLB debut.

Petit sat in the mid-90s with his four-seamer and sinker during his stint in Toledo. He also threw a slider and changeup. Petit leaned heavily on the slider, throwing it more than 40% of the time. It averaged 83.7 mph with decent glove-side movement. FanGraphs has the slider as a 55-grade pitch.

articles.title: Red Sox Trade Eduardo Rivera To Cardinals
body: 11:17 am CT: The Red Sox have officially announced the trade.
10:34 am CT: The Red Sox are sending left-hander Eduardo Rivera to the Cardinals, reports Andrew Parker of SoxProspects.com. Boston will receive right-hander Juan Garcia in return.

Rivera was designated for assignment on Monday as part of Boston’s 40-man roster adjustments. He’s had multiple solid seasons in the minors, but struggled in his first taste of the big leagues this past year. The Red Sox ultimately ran out of space for him on the roster. Rivera will get a shot with a Cardinals squad that has less certainty in the bullpen, particularly from the left side.

Boston took Rivera in the 11th round of the 2021 draft. He operated as both a starter and reliever as he worked his way through the Red Sox system. The 23-year-old opened the 2026 campaign at Double-A. He allowed a run over two starts and earned the bump to Triple-A. Rivera compiled a 2.96 ERA across 45 2/3 frames at Worcester, with most of that work coming out of the bullpen.

Rivera was called upon in late April to eat some innings against the Yankees. He tossed 3 1/3 scoreless frames in his MLB debut. It wasn’t enough to keep him on the roster. Rivera wouldn’t get his next big-league chance until July. He fired 3 2/3 scoreless innings in his first start, a matchup against the Mets shortly before the All-Star break. Rivera was tagged for seven earned runs over three innings in his final two appearances. A lumbar strain ended his season in mid-August.

articles.title: Mariners Hire Jason Kanzler As Manager
body: 11:03 am CT: The Mariners have officially announced Kanzler as their new manager.

“Our goal in this process was finding a manager with the ability to challenge all of us to improve,” Dipoto said in a statement. “Jason has the mindset, expertise, communication skills, and intensity to help create a championship standard here in Seattle.”
10:41 am CT: The Mariners have landed on Jason Kanzler as their next skipper, reports Daniel Kramer of MLB.com. Kanzler will replace Dan Wilson.

This will be the first managerial position for Kanzler. He was a minor league hitting coach in the Astros system from 2019 through 2021. He was on the major league staff in 2022 and 2023. Kanzler has been the Cubs’ director of player development since 2024.
As Kramer notes, the 36-year-old Kanzler will be the second-youngest manager in the league. Blake Butera of the Nationals is the youngest at 34 years old.

“I am thrilled to join the Mariners organization and I’m looking forward to hitting the ground running,” Kanzler said in a statement. “This team has an immense amount of talent in all facets of the game, and my coaching staff and I are excited to access and unlock this team’s full potential.”

articles.title: Rangers Make Coaching, Front Office Changes
body: The Rangers are making some organizational adjustments after falling just short of a playoff spot this season. Assistant hitting coach Alex Cintrón will not return to the position, president of baseball operations Chris Young told reporters on Monday (h/t Shawn McFarland of the Dallas Morning News). Texas parted ways with assistant pitching coach Dave Bush.

Cintrón will remain with the team in an offensive-related role. Young made the decision sound more like something that came from Cintrón instead of the organization, with the former infielder trying “to balance what’s best for him at this point.”

After a nine-year playing career, Cintrón entered the coaching ranks. He’s spent the past decade in the dugout, mostly with the Astros. Houston hired him as an assistant in 2017. Cintrón served as first base coach and then hitting coach with the Astros through 2025. The Rangers hired him as an assistant to lead hitting coach Justin Viele this past season.

Bush has been with the team for three seasons. He was initially hired as director of pitching strategy in 2024. He’s been an assistant on the big-league staff the past two years. Bush worked under pitching coach Jordan Tiegs in 2026. Young said the club is not planning on hiring someone else for Bush’s role.

articles.title: Diamondbacks Outright Pavin Smith
body: The Diamondbacks sent first baseman Pavin Smith outright off the roster, according to the MiLB.com transaction tracker. That’ll drop their 40-man roster tally to 33.

Smith always seemed likely to lose his roster spot this offseason. Arizona already sent him through outright waivers around the All-Star Break. They called him back up in September in hope of finding a jolt against right-handed pitching. Smith managed a pinch-hit, walk-off home run to beat the Yankees on September 19 and had a big final two weeks. He had hit just.141/.236/.192 in 89 plate appearances before losing his MLB spot, though.

MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projected Smith for a $2.5MM arbitration salary. This functions as an early non-tender of the former #7 overall pick. Smith will almost certainly file for free agency in the next day or two. He’ll take a league average.242/.325/.398 career slash line to the open market. Arizona will be in the market for left-handed bats and will need to acquire at least one player to slot at first base or designated hitter.

Jake Bauers is the top free agent first baseman but is attached to a qualifying offer and likely out of Arizona’s price range. Ty France, Alec Bohm, Josh Bell, Nathaniel Lowe, Joc Pederson, Eugenio Suárez and George Springer are available as free agent first base/DH types. The trade market could feature Andrew Vaughn (especially if Bauers accepts the QO to stay in Milwaukee), Spencer Torkelson, Royce Lewis and Jake Burger.

articles.title: Evan Carter Unlikely To Be Ready For Opening Day, Rangers To Explore Center Field Market
body: Rangers center fielder Evan Carter underwent labrum surgery on his right hip last week, president of baseball operations Chris Young told reporters on Monday (link via Kennedi Landry of MLB.com). Young said that while Carter is expected to play for a good portion of the 2027 season, he’s not likely to be ready for Opening Day — presuming the season itself starts on time.

It’s yet another injury setback for Carter, who battled back issues early in his career. He had a relatively healthy’26 campaign in terms of avoiding the injured list, only missing two weeks in the middle of June with a right oblique strain. Carter easily established new career highs in games played (141) and plate appearances (455) but slogged through a miserable offensive season. He batted.194/.288/.315 with nine home runs.

Among hitters with 400+ PAs, only Cal Raleigh and Matt McLain had a lower batting average. Carter was fifth from the bottom in slugging and in the bottom 15 in on-base percentage despite a strong 10.3% walk rate. He struck out a quarter of the time and made a lot of weak contact. Carter also continued to struggle mightily in limited looks against left-handed pitching; he’s a.110 hitter and still doesn’t have an extra-base hit against a southpaw in his major league career (145 plate appearances).

articles.title: Parker Messick Earns PPI Pick For Guardians
body: The Baseball Writers Association of America announced the finalists for all the major awards on Monday night. The award winners will be revealed next week, but the finalists are the players who finished top three in the voting in some order.

Guardians left-hander Parker Messick is listed alongside Cam Schlittler and Dylan Cease among the finalists for the AL Cy Young award. As MLBTR contributor Ethan Hullihen observes, that ensures that Cleveland will receive a bonus pick after the first round in the 2027 draft. Messick met the eligibility for the Prospect Promotion Incentive, which means a top three Cy Young finish within his first three seasons nets Cleveland a pick.

For those unfamiliar with the PPI intricacies, that only applies to rookie-eligible players who appeared on at least two of the preseason Top 100 prospect lists at Baseball America, ESPN and MLB Pipeline. Messick made his MLB debut last August and remained rookie-eligible going into 2026. He appeared on the ESPN and Baseball America lists. The Guardians carried him on their roster for the entire’26 season, so he could’ve earned them the pick either by winning Rookie of the Year or with a top three Cy Young finish in any season between 2026-28.

A team can only receive one PPI pick per player. Messick is unsurprisingly also a finalist for AL Rookie of the Year, but that’s no longer relevant to Cleveland’s PPI situation. They would not receive a second bonus pick if Messick wins ROY, nor would they receive any additional picks for a top three Cy Young finish in 2027 or’28.

articles.title: Rockies Hire Ethan Katz As Pitching Coach
body: The Rockies announced they’ve hired Ethan Katz as their new pitching coach. Thomas Harding of MLB.com reported the news shortly before it was official. Harding also reports that former MLB infielder Andre Lipcius is joining the staff as game-planning coach, where he’ll replace retiring assistant bench coach Ronnie Gideon. The team has not yet confirmed the Lipcius hire.

Katz takes over for Alon Leichman, who was dismissed after one year in the role. He’ll have his work cut out for him in taking on Coors Field with arguably the least talented pitching staff in the majors. Colorado was last in ERA (5.59) and strikeout rate (17.5%) for a fifth straight season. The ballpark certainly plays into that, but it’s far from the biggest problem. No team had a lower strikeout rate on the road this year, while only the Reds had a higher ERA away from home.

The 43-year-old Katz is a former minor league pitcher who was drafted by the Rockies in 2005. He never advanced beyond A-ball as a player but has carved out a strong coaching career. He spent five years as the top pitching coach with the White Sox and worked as an assistant under lead pitching voice Josh Miller with the Astros this year. Houston moved on from Katz — along with numerous other coaches and manager Joe Espada — after a season in which they ranked 24th in ERA and 12th in strikeout percentage.

articles.title: Red Sox Designate Eduardo Rivera For Assignment
body: The Red Sox announced that reliever Eduardo Rivera has been designated for assignment. The club’s 40-man roster count is now at 40.

Rivera is a somewhat surprising final roster cut. He’s a 23-year-old left-hander with a 95 mph average fastball and promising slider. Rivera struck out 30% of opponents against an elevated 12.7% walk percentage across 55 2/3 innings in the minors this year. He pitched in four big league contests, working 10 innings of seven-run ball.

The 6’7″ southpaw finished the season on the injured list with a lumbar strain. Between the injury and the below-average control, the Red Sox are apparently content to move on. It’d be very surprising if Rivera weren’t acquired in a minor trade or claimed off waivers this week. He still has a pair of minor league options remaining and has the size and stuff to potentially pitch towards the back of a bullpen at some point. Boston has Aroldis Chapman, Erik Miller, Jovani Morán, Raymond Burgos, Alec Gamboa and Tyler Samaniego as lefty relief options on the offseason roster.

articles.title: Rockies Outright Four Players
body: The Rockies announced they’ve dropped four players from their 40-man roster: infielder Chad Stevens and right-handers Blake Adams, Eiberson Castellano and TJ Shook. All four have already cleared outright waivers. Stevens, Castellano and Shook have elected free agency. Adams has been assigned to Triple-A Albuquerque. The club’s 40-man count is now at 37.

Adams, 26, will remain in the organization and could get a non-roster invite to Spring Training. He’s a 2022 draftee (13th round) who doesn’t have the previous career outright or seven years in the minors to elect free agency. The Kansas State product was called up on August 24 and tossed one inning against the Nationals in his MLB debut. It didn’t go as he hoped, as Washington tagged him for five runs, including a Daylen Lile homer. The 26-year-old had a 6.29 ERA and 16.5% strikeout rate as a multi-inning reliever in the minors this year.

Shook was acquired in the minor league portion of last year’s Rule 5 draft. He earned his first MLB call in June and made five total appearances, allowing seven runs over 7 2/3 innings. Shook managed a solid 3.45 ERA across 57 1/3 frames with Albuquerque but is a fly-ball pitcher whose fastball sits in the 92-93 mph range.

articles.title: Giants Designate Reiver Sanmartin, Decline Option On Rowan Wick
body: The Giants announced Monday that they’ve designated left-handed reliever Reiver Sanmartin for assignment, dropping their 40-man roster to an even 40 players. San Francisco also declined its $800K option on righty Rowan Wick, who’ll receive a $100K buyout. Wick remains with the club for now as an arbitration-eligible player.

San Francisco acquired Sanmartin early last offseason, claiming him off waivers from Cincinnati. The southpaw suffered a hip injury in Spring Training and missed the first couple months. He was up and down from Triple-A the rest of the way, allowing a 4.22 ERA across 21 1/3 innings. He got ground-balls at a monster 63.8% clip but only managed a 17.2% strikeout rate.

As one might infer from those rate stats, Sanmartin leans most heavily on a sinker. He has a three-pitch mix but only sits around 92 mph with his fastball. Sanmartin had a career-low walk rate in 2026 (7.5%) yet struggled with his control during his time in Cincinnati. He’s also out of options and would need to break camp next year if he’s on a club’s 40-man roster. The Giants will trade or waive him in the next five days.

Wick, 34 later this week, missed the entire season rehabbing from Tommy John surgery. The Giants knew that’d be the case when they signed him to an $880K free agent deal last February. Wick hasn’t pitched in the majors since 2022. He worked 42 2/3 frames of 0.84 ERA ball with a 30.4% strikeout rate in Japan during the’25 season before his elbow gave out.

articles.title: Eight Players Receive Qualifying Offers
body: Eight players have received a $23.15MM qualifying offer, reports Joel Sherman of The New York Post. They are Randy Arozarena of the Mariners, Jake Bauers of the Brewers, David Bednar of the Yankees, Ryan Jeffers of the Twins, Brandon Lowe of the Pirates, Adrián Morejón of the Padres, Trevor Rogers of the Orioles and Seiya Suzuki of the Cubs.

As a refresher, teams are allowed to issue a one-year QO to an impending free agent as long as he spent the entire walk year with that club and has not previously received a QO in his career. The value is determined by averaging the salaries of the 125 top-paid players in the league. Players have until 3 pm Central on November 17 to decide whether to accept or reject. In the meantime, they are free to discuss contracts with other clubs, getting a sense of their market potential before making a decision.

If the player signs elsewhere, the club is then entitled to draft pick compensation. The player’s new club would be subject to penalties, certainly including draft pick forfeiture and potentially the forfeiture of international bonus pool space as well.

Most of the names are not surprising. Back in September, MLBTR took a look at the hitters and pitchers we expected to receive a QO. Rogers, Arozarena and Suzuki were characterized as locks. Jeffers and Lowe were also framed as likely recipients, with the slight hesitation due to the spending history of their respective clubs, rather than any lack of talent on the part of the players.

articles.title: Tigers Exercise Option On Drew Anderson, Decline Option On Kenley Jansen
body: The Tigers have picked up their $10MM option on swingman Drew Anderson, the club announced. They declined a $12MM option on closer Kenley Jansen in favor of a $2MM buyout.

Detroit also re-signed righty Jacob Waguespack to a one-year, $1.3MM guarantee. That deal contains an additional $200K in performance bonuses: $25K apiece at 45 and 50 innings pitched, and $50K each at 55, 60, and 65 frames. Waguespack, a client of The Team, was eligible to sign with Detroit within the five-day exclusive negotiation window for clubs to retain their own free agents.

Picking up Anderson’s option and re-signing Waguespack necessitated making four cuts from the 40-man roster. Detroit has placed pitchers Bailey Horn and Sawyer Gipson-Long on release waivers, designated reliever Yilber Díaz for assignment, and sent outfielder Corey Julks outright off the roster. Julks has already cleared waivers and elected free agency, per the team.

Anderson will enter camp competing for a rotation spot in his second season in Detroit. The Tigers signed him to a $7MM deal after a four-year run in Asia. He initially expected to compete for a rotation spot but was pushed to long relief by the subsequent Framber Valdez and Justin Verlander signings. He got out to a spotty start and never really pitched his way into a late inning role. Anderson got a handful of high-leverage assignments but also mixed in a decent amount of mop-up work.

articles.title: Blue Jays Decline Option On Myles Straw
body: The Blue Jays announced they’ve declined their $8MM club option on outfielder Myles Straw. He receives a $1.75MM buyout, which is paid by the Guardians as a condition of the 2025 trade that sent him to Toronto. Straw is now a free agent.

Toronto announced a few procedural moves as they got their 40-man roster in shape. José Berríos, Jake Bloss, Bowden Francis, Cody Ponce, Addison Barger, Anthony Santander and Jonatan Clase were all reinstated from the 60-day injured list. While the Jays didn’t officially announce an option decision regarding Berríos, it’s safe to assume he did not opt out of the final two years on his contract. Toronto outrighted right-hander CJ Van Eyk off their 40-man roster and announced that outfielder Rudy Martin Jr. elected free agency after being outrighted last week.

Straw has spent the last two seasons in Toronto. The Jays acquired him in what amounted to a salary dump, as the Guardians sent along international bonus pool space so Toronto could make a better offer to Roki Sasaki. The gambit didn’t work as hoped when Sasaki chose the Dodgers anyway, but Straw salvaged the deal from their perspective with a couple solid seasons as a depth outfielder. He batted.262/.313/.367 with stellar defensive grades for their pennant winning team in 2025. This past season wasn’t as productive, but Straw remained a viable fifth outfielder and a strong clubhouse presence.

articles.title: Mets Designate Kyren Paris, Christian Cairo For Assignment
body: The Mets announced that infielder Kyren Paris, who was claimed off waivers from the Angels a few days ago, has been signed to a major league contract for 2027 and designated for assignment. They announced that fellow infielder Christian Cairo has been designated for assignment as well. It was reported earlier today that Cairo, who was claimed off waivers in September, had also signed a big league deal.

Paris, who turns 25 next month, is a former second-round pick who has played parts of four big league seasons. He’s a good athlete with speed and raw power who’ll need to dramatically cut down on the strikeouts to even carve out a career as a bench player. The righty-swinging Paris owns a.147/.238/.272 slash line with seven home runs and 11 stolen bases across 263 career plate appearances. He has gone down on strikes in 38% of his trips to the plate.

New York is evidently intrigued enough by the tools and Paris’ minor league production. While he barely factored into the Halos’ big league plans this season, he’s coming off a.274/.384/.458 showing with 13 homers and 24 steals between Double-A and Triple-A. Paris has played mostly middle infield in his minor league career but has the speed to factor into the outfield mix as well.

Cairo spent the final couple weeks of the 2026 season in the organization after being claimed from the Phillies. He’s an all-glove utility infielder who hasn’t appeared in the majors yet. The 25-year-old is coming off a.230/.381/.300 showing with four homers and 25 stolen bases in Triple-A.

articles.title: Yankees Select Marco Luciano
body: The Yankees announced that they have added infielder/outfielder Marco Luciano to their 40-man roster. Luciano would have otherwise become a minor league free agent, so this allows the Yankees to keep him in the system for now.

Luciano, now 25, was once a big prospect in the Giants’ system. He didn’t click in the majors with that club and exhausted his final option season in 2025. That led to him riding the transaction carousel last offseason. He went to the Pirates, Orioles and Yankees via waiver claims. The Yankees were the ones to finally pass him through waivers unclaimed in February, allowing them to keep Luciano in the minors as non-roster depth.

He didn’t earn his way back to the majors during the 2026 season but had a good year on the farm. He got into 116 games, 28 at the Double-A level and 88 at Triple-A. He stepped to the plate 493 times in total. His 24.7% strikeout rate was a bit on the high side but he drew walks at a 13% clip and hit 27 home runs. He slashed.293/.387/.545 for a 143 wRC+. He got a bit of help from a.348 batting average on balls in play but it would have been a good season even with more neutral luck.

Defensively, he came up as a shortstop but the Giants become pessimistic about his prospects there and moved him to left field. The Yankees put him back on the dirt but mostly at second base. He played just one game at short and only seven in left field.

articles.title: Orioles Decline Club Option On Dietrich Enns
body: The Orioles announced that they have declined a $3.5MM club option on left-hander Dietrich Enns. He will receive a $125K buyout.

This was an obvious call for the Orioles, who received little contributions from Enns in 2026. After he missed almost all of April with a foot infection, he returned to make nine appearances in May. While Enns had a passable 3.94 ERA through his first 16 innings, it came with nearly as many walks (11) as strikeouts (13). The Orioles designated Enns for assignment and then outrighted him in late May, and they never summoned him back to their roster. He ended up throwing 54 1/3 innings of 5.80 ERA ball with Triple-A Norfolk.

Enns spent a year and change in the Baltimore organization, which acquired him from Detroit ahead of the 2025 trade deadline. He didn’t pitch well with the Tigers after returning from a three-year run in Asia, but he turned things around with the Orioles at first. In 28 2/3 frames down the stretch, Enns registered a 3.14 ERA with 34 strikeouts and 11 walks. The Orioles then kept him around last November for a guaranteed $2.625MM, but the 35-year-old is now back on the open market 12 months later.

Also a former Twin and Ray, Enns has notched a 3.86 ERA with decent strikeout (23.5%) and walk (8.7%) numbers in 88 2/3 major league innings. However, left-handed hitters have teed off on the southpaw for a.324/.374/.505 line. Enns has had far more success against righties, who have hit.223/.291/.341 against him.

articles.title: Red Sox Designate Zack Kelly For Assignment
body: The Red Sox are designating reliever Zack Kelly for assignment, reports Chris Cotillo of MassLive. Boston subsequently confirmed the move and designated left-hander Eduardo Rivera for assignment. Those transactions got their roster count down to 40.

Kelly has pitched parts of five seasons in Boston. The 31-year-old righty has a 4.04 earned run average over 131 1/3 career innings. He worked 16 frames of eight-run ball this past season, striking out 14 against seven walks. Kelly had a middling strikeout/walk profile in Triple-A as well and suffered a season-ending elbow injury in early July. Cotillo reported last month that he suffered a fracture, though he’s expected to resume throwing in a few weeks.

Kelly has shown the ability to be a productive middle reliever but has had a few elbow issues over the course of his career. He’s also out of options, limiting the roster flexibility going into 2027. The Sox will trade him or place him on waivers within the next five days. Kelly can elect minor league free agency even if he clears waivers, so this likely ends his time in the Boston organization.

articles.title: Astros Exercise Club Option On Isaac Paredes
body: The Astros announced they have exercised a $13.35MM club option for infielder Isaac Paredes. Chandler Rome of The Athletic was among those to relay the info.

There was never any doubt this option would be picked up. Paredes put together a terrific 2026 season, delivering a.262/.360/.447 batting line with 25 homers, 27 doubles and a triple. He walked at a healthy 10.8% clip and struck out in a career-low 13.4% of his plate appearances. Metrics like Defensive Runs Saved (-7) and Outs Above Average (-4) panned his defensive work at the hot corner, but he also showed some versatility by helping out for brief spells at first base (58 innings) and second base (25 innings).

Paredes hit well both at home and on the road, but his swing is practically tailor-made for Houston’s Daikin Park, where the short porch down the left field line dovetails with Paredes’ extreme fly-ball, pull-oriented approach. He belted 14 homers in 324 plate appearances in Houston compared to 11 in 335 trips to the plate on the road.

The Astros enter the 2026-27 offseason with the same crowded infield they faced last winter. Paredes, Carlos Correa, Jeremy Peña, Jose Altuve and Christian Walker give them five infielders for four spots. There’s no real DH time available — not with MVP candidate Yordan Alvarez standing in that spot as one of the game’s top all-around hitters (if not the top all-around hitter). Houston tried in the past to move Altuve to left field, but that experiment wound up producing even worse defensive results than Altuve has been registering at second base as he moves into his late 30s.

articles.title: Brewers Exercise Option On William Contreras; Decline Options On Senzatela, Sánchez
body: The Brewers announced they’ve picked up their $14.5MM option on catcher William Contreras. Milwaukee declined a $14MM option on reliever Antonio Senzatela and their end of an $8.5MM mutual option for backup catcher Gary Sánchez. The Brewers also officially announced the previously reported moves of issuing a qualifying offer to Jake Bauers, while Dustin May declined his half of a $20MM mutual option.

On top of the option decisions, the Brewers also did a bit of housecleaning at the back of the 40-man roster. Milwaukee lost outfielder Akil Baddoo on waivers to Pittsburgh while running relievers Bryse Wilson and Jared Koenig through waivers unclaimed. Koenig has already elected free agency, and Wilson will have the right to do the same.

There wasn’t much suspense with any of the option decisions. Contreras is coming off a World Series MVP win and would’ve been eligible for arbitration even if Milwaukee declined the option. His projected salary was right around the option price, and there’s no reason for the Brewers to take that to a hearing. They’ll surely get calls from other teams about his availability on the trade market as he enters his walk year.

However, the Brewers have enough short-term spending capacity to make a $23.15MM offer to Bauers and could trade the likes of Trevor Megill or Andrew Vaughn to trim salary from their arbitration class. While an offseason Contreras trade seemed plausible this past summer, it’s more difficult to envision coming off the franchise’s first title.

articles.title: Marlins Outright Patrick Monteverde
body: The Marlins announced that left-hander Patrick Monteverde has been sent outright to Triple-A Jacksonville. He has elected free agency, per Christina De Nicola of MLB.com.

Monteverde, a Marlin since they selected him in the eighth round of the 2021 draft, could be on the way to the second organization of his career this offseason. The 29-year-old made one appearance apiece with the Marlins in each of the past two seasons, but that is the extent of his major league experience. In 7 2/3 innings with the Fish, Monteverde was lit up for eight earned runs on 14 hits. He added six strikeouts against two walks.

While Monteverde hasn’t been much of a factor in the bigs, he has gotten extensive work at the minors’ highest level. He combined for 76 appearances and 49 starts with Triple-A Jacksonville over the past three years, but the soft-tossing Monteverde had trouble preventing runs during that stretch. He pitched to a 5.38 ERA with unspectacular strikeout and walk rates (18.9% and 8.6%, respectively) over 271 innings.

articles.title: Mariners Outright Five Players
body: The Mariners announced that five players have cleared players and been outrighted to Triple-A Tacoma. They are left-hander Josh Simpson, right-hander Troy Watson, as well as infielders Weston Wilson, Will Wilson and Patrick Wisdom. All five players are eligible for free agency and will presumably be on the open market shortly.

Today is a busy day for marginal transactions. The 60-day injured list is now gone, meaning injured players had to be added back to the 40-man roster. Also, two weeks from now, teams will give roster spots to prospects who would otherwise be eligible for the Rule 5 draft. With today’s moves, the Mariners have now gotten their 40-man count down to 39.

The five fellows who lost their spots were all minor players in the club’s disappointing 2026 season. Wisdom signed a minor league deal with Seattle last offseason. He was selected to the roster in April. However, he spent some time on the injured list and also got optioned to the minors a few times. He made 50 plate appearances but struck out in 42% of those while producing a.106/.160/.191 line. Wisdom has big power but the strikeouts were a problem even when he was at his peak. He’s now 35 years old and it’s been several years since he held down a regular big league job.

articles.title: Pirates Claim Akil Baddoo
body: The Pirates have claimed outfielder Akil Baddoo off waivers from the Brewers, according to announcements from both clubs. The Bucs have 40-man space and don’t need to make a corresponding move.

Baddoo, 28, didn’t play in the majors this year. He had a good rookie showing back in 2021 but struggled in subsequent seasons. The Brewers signed him to a major league deal ahead of the 2026 campaign. He suffered a left quad strain in spring training and began the season on the IL. When he was ready to come off the IL in May, he was optioned to Triple-A.

He ended up performing well in 64 games at that level. He hit 11 home runs and stole seven bases. His 23.3% strikeout rate was around average while his 12.2% walk rate was quite strong. He slashed.252/.342/.469 for a 113 wRC+ while spending time at all three outfield spots.

Baddoo exhausted his final option in 2026 and is now out of options. That will make it harder for him to hold a roster spot going forward. The Brewers bumped him off but the Bucs have scooped him up, at least for the moment.

The Pirates project to have Oneil Cruz and Bryan Reynolds in two outfield spots. Esmerlyn Valdéz, Jake Mangum, Jhostynxon García and others will be trying to earn playing time next to Cruz and Reynolds. Baddoo is now in that mix as well. If he holds his roster spot through the winter, he could compete for a role during spring training. If he is outrighted off the roster later in the offseason, he would have the right to elect free agency, both because he has a previous career outright and because he has at least three years of service time.

articles.title: Padres Select Luis Gutierrez
body: The Padres announced that they have selected the contract of left-hander Luis Gutierrez. They still have eight openings on their 40-man roster.

Gutierrez would have been eligible for minor league free agency had the Padres not made this move. They obviously didn’t want to risk losing the 23-year-old, who ranks as one of their 25 best prospects at MLB Pipeline (12th) and Baseball America (24th).

Gutierrez, a native of Venezuela, signed with the Padres for $750K in 2019. It took him until 2024 to reach Single-A ball, but he put together a breakout season at four different levels the next year. While leaning on an 82 mph slider and a 92 mph sinker as his top offerings, he posted a 3.31 ERA and a 47.4% ground-ball rate over 125 innings (65 in High A, 50 in Single A and five apiece in Double A and Triple A). This past season didn’t go nearly as well for Gutierrez, who missed around four months with shoulder problems. He wound up totaling 36 innings, including just seven at the Triple-A level, and recording a 4.50 ERA.

articles.title: Cubs Claim Eric Orze
body: The Cubs announced that they have claimed reliever Eric Orze off waivers from the Twins. Chicago now has 35 players on its 40-man roster.

Orze, whom the Mets drafted in the fifth round in 2020, had a two-appearance, 1 2/3-inning major league debut with the club in 2024 and then left in an offseason trade. After the Rays acquired Orze for outfielder Jose Siri, the right-hander emerged as an effective member of Tampa Bay’s bullpen in 2025. Across 41 2/3 innings, Orze pitched to an appealing 3.02 ERA. However, he did it despite pedestrian strikeout, walk and ground-ball numbers, and he benefited from an 81% strand rate.

Orze didn’t last long with the Rays, who dealt him to the Twins for pitching prospect Jacob Kisting last November. The move didn’t go as Minnesota hoped, evidenced by the fact that the team subjected Orze to waivers a year after acquiring him. Orze’s ERA skyrocketed to 5.66 ERA in 41 1/3 innings with the Twins, though an unusually low 59.7% strand rate didn’t help his cause. While the 29-year-old continued to post below-average strikeout, walk and grounder rates, ERA estimators such as FIP (3.34), xERA (4.13), SIERA (4.50) and xFIP (4.71) suggest he should have kept runs off the board at a more respectable clip.

articles.title: Astros Select Roddery Muñoz, César Salazar
body: The Astros announced that they have selected right-hander Roddery Muñoz and catcher César Salazar to their roster. They also announced their acquisition of right-hander Evan Reifert, a deal that was previously reported. Reifert has been added to the roster as well. Outfielder Jake Meyers has been outrighted off the roster and will elect free agency. It was reported earlier today that Meyers would be removed from Houston’s 40-man roster.

Houston took Muñoz from Cincinnati in the Rule 5 draft last year, and he held a roster spot with the Astros into the season. However, the team placed Muñoz on outright waivers after a 1 1/3-inning, five-run blowup in his third appearance of the year on April 3. Muñoz went unclaimed, and the Reds didn’t take him back, leaving him to finish the season with the Astros’ Triple-A affiliate. The 26-year-old put up quality production over 53 innings in Sugar Land, where he parlayed a 33.3% strikeout rate and a 53.3% ground-ball mark into a 3.06 ERA.

articles.title: Rays Exercise Club Option On Taylor Walls, Announce Five Additional Moves
body: The Rays exercised their $3.1MM club option on Gold Glove shortstop Taylor Walls, per a team announcement. Tampa Bay also added righty Alexander Alberto and outfielder Jack Suwinski to the 40-man roster.

Meanwhile, infielder Nick Madrigal and right-hander Jonathan Heasley went unclaimed on waivers. Madrigal rejected an outright assignment in favor of free agency, while Heasley is now slated to become a minor league free agent. The Rays also confirmed their previously reported trade of righty Evan Reifert to the Astros.

Barring an offseason trade, Walls will be back for a sixth full season in Tampa Bay. He’s been a defensive stalwart throughout his career and finally secured his first Gold Glove this past season after leading AL shortstops with 21 Defensive Runs Saved. Statcast’s Outs Above Average wasn’t nearly as bullish, grading Walls three runs below average, but that’s bizarrely been the case throughout his career. The Rays clearly believe DRS to be more accurate in this case, reflecting Walls’ value as a Gold Glove caliber defender.

They’ve been willing to live with a dearth of offense from the bottom of the order to keep Walls’ glove in the picture. He never hit above seventh in the lineup and batted just.222/.309/.298 with two homers (which incredibly came in consecutive at-bats in a game against the A’s on August 11) over 433 plate appearances. Walls is a career.200/.291/.298 hitter in nearly 2000 trips to the dish. He’s slated to hit free agency after next season.

articles.title: Nationals Designate José Tena For Assignment
body: The Nationals announced a series of roster moves today. Infielder José Tena has been designated for assignment. Left-hander PJ Poulin, Richard Lovelady and Ken Waldichuk have cleared waivers and elected free agency. Pitchers Paxton Schultz and Mitchell Parker have been claimed off waivers, Schultz by the Reds and Parker by the Braves. Those claims will be covered in more details in the links provided. Spencer Nusbaum of The Athletic reported the Tena news prior to the official announcement.

Roster maintenance is a key thing for all clubs this week. The injured list goes away at 4 pm Central today. November 17 is the deadline to add players who would otherwise be eligible for the Rule 5 draft. Those dual pressures will squeeze many guys to DFA limbo or the waiver wire or both.

Tena, 26 in March, was acquired from the Guardians in the 2024 deadline deal which sent Lane Thomas to Cleveland. Between those two clubs, Tena has appeared in 227 games and stepped to the plate 659 times, producing a lackluster.240/.303/.358 line. He provides defensive versatility, with experience at the three infield spots to the left of first base as well as the outfield corners, but he hasn’t been given especially strong grades anywhere.

articles.title: Giants Release Tristan Beck; Outright Joel Kuhnel, Seth Lonsway
body: The Giants announced a big match of roster moves today. Right-hander José Buttó has been claimed off waivers by the Rangers. Fellow righty Duncan Davitt was claimed off waivers by the Reds. Infielders Brett Harris and Shay Whitcomb were both claimed off waivers by the Phillies. Catcher Zach Morgan was claimed off waivers by the Orioles. Righty Tristan Beck has been placed on unconditional release waivers. Righty Joel Kuhnel and lefty Seth Lonsway were both outrighted to Triple-A Sacramento after clearing waivers. You can read more about the moves for Buttó, Davitt, Harris, Whitcomb and Morgan in other MLBTR posts.

The 30-year-old Beck’s release ends a long tenure with the Giants, who acquired him from the Braves in the teams’ Mark Melancon trade in July 2019. He debuted with the Giants in 2023 and pitched to a 3.92 ERA with a superb 5.9% walk rate across 33 appearances and 85 innings. Unfortunately, an arm aneurysm kept Beck out for almost all of 2024. While Beck returned that September to post a 1.69 ERA with a similar walk rate in 16 innings, he had far more trouble keeping runs off the board with the Giants from 2025-26. Over 75 2/3 frames, including 19 this year, he recorded a 4.76 ERA. Beck continued to limit walks during that stretch, as he issued free passes just 6.7% of the time, but he only fanned 15.9% of hitters.

articles.title: Orioles Make Four Waiver Claims; Leody Taveras Elects Free Agency
body: The Orioles announced a dizzying slew of roster moves ahead of the deadline to get 40-man rosters down to 40 players. Baltimore claimed right-hander Josh White off waivers from the Marlins and southpaw Philip Abner off waivers from the Mets. The O’s also claimed catcher Zach Morgan from the Giants and righty Chase Hampton from the Cardinals.

Meanwhile, outfielder Leody Taveras cleared waivers and rejected an outright assignment, instead opting for free agency. Baltimore also confirmed its previously reported outright of former top prospect Heston Kjerstad, while adding that righty Yosver Zulueta and catcher Yohel Pozo were outrighted to Triple-A Norfolk. All of Kjerstad, Zulueta and Pozo can become minor league free agents. [UPDATE: Kjerstad, Zulueta, and Pozo indeed elected free agency, as per the MiLB.com transaction log.]

White, 25, is a 2022 fifth rounder. He’s only pitched two-thirds of an inning in the majors, during which he was shelled for five runs due primarily to issuing four walks. He posted a 2.41 ERA in 56 Triple-A frames, however, fanning 27% of his opponents there. His 13.5% walk rate in Jacksonville shows that the command struggles in his lone MLB appearance were more than just debut day jitters. White sits 94.4 mph on his four-seamer and mixes in a curveball and slider he uses with equal frequency. He has a pair of minor league option years remaining.

articles.title: Phillies Claim Brett Harris, Shay Whitcomb
body: The Phillies announced that they have claimed infielders Brett Harris and Shay Whitcomb off waivers from the Giants. Additionally, catcher Garrett Stubbs, who was designated for assignment last week, elected free agency. That indicates he cleared waivers in recent days.

The Giants went into the offseason with a large amount of roster maintenance to do. They had a huge number of players on the 60-day injured list but the IL goes away five days after the World Series is done. That deadline is today at 4 pm Central. Free agency wasn’t going to help much as righty JT Brubaker was their only guy heading to the open market. As of a few days ago, they were projected to end up with a 40-man count of 56. That situation has led to various transactions this week as the Giants pare down.

The Phillies will benefit by adding some infield depth. Harris, 29 in June, isn’t really established in the big leagues yet. He has appeared in 89 games and stepped to the plate 258 times but has produced a lackluster.186/.293/.273 line.

Despite those numbers, Harris is clearly liked around the league. This is his fourth team this year. He began 2026 with the Athletics but was designated for assignment in June. He was traded to the Red Sox and later went to the Giants via the waiver wire. Now he has been claimed yet again.

articles.title: Rangers Claim José Buttó, Outright Michael Helman
body: The Rangers claimed righty José Buttó off waivers from the Giants and assigned infielder/outfielder Michael Helman outright to Triple-A Round Rock after he went unclaimed on waivers, per a team announcement.

Buttó had been on the Giants’ 60-day injured list, but with the club facing an extreme roster crunch, it elected to move on in the wake of a lost year. After throwing just two innings, Buttó underwent surgery on a blood clot in his pitching arm in mid-April and did not return. However, he is expected to go through a normal offseason and return for Spring Training, per San Francisco’s injury tracker at MLB.com.

Buttó debuted with the Mets in 2022 and became a regular in their bullpen for a couple of years. In his best season, 2024, he fired 74 innings of 2.55 ERA ball with a strong 26.9% strikeout rate. Buttó’s ability to generate strikeouts helped him overcome a 12.9% walk rate, which is right in line with his career average. He hasn’t replicated that success since, however, and the Mets ended up trading Buttó to the Giants in the teams’ Tyler Rogers deal ahead of the 2025 deadline. The sinkerballer recorded a career-best 48.1% ground-ball rate in 67 innings between the Mets and Giants that year, but a much lower strikeout rate (20.4%) helped lead to a less impressive 3.90 ERA.

The 28-year-old Buttó is out of minor league options, meaning he will end up back in limbo if he is unable to hold a roster spot with Texas. For now, though, he represents a potential option for a team whose relievers finished 23rd in ERA and strikeout-walk percentage in 2026.

articles.title: Mets Claim Pierson Ohl
body: The Mets have claimed right-hander Pierson Ohl off waivers from the Rockies, reports Chelsea Janes of SNY. Colorado has announced the move.

The Rockies cut Ohl from their 40-man roster less than a year after acquiring him in a January 2026 trade with the Twins. They didn’t end up getting any contributions from Ohl, who underwent Tommy John surgery in late February and missed the entire season. He began throwing in August in hopes of returning in 2027. If he does, it could be as a member of the Mets.

Now 27 years old, Ohl has spent most of his pro career with the Twins organization. They drafted him in the 14th round in 2021 and helped him develop into a decent prospect. When they selected Ohl’s contract in July 2025, he owned a microscopic 3.6% walk rate in the minors. He continued limiting walks during a 14-appearance, 30-inning major league debut that year, as he issued free passes at a 5.3% clip. While that accompanied an unspectacular strikeout rate (20.3%) and a high ERA (5.10), Ohl posted more encouraging underlying numbers. ERA estimators such as SIERA (3.87), xFIP (3.99), FIP (4.20) and xERA (4.78) all suggested he deserved a better fate.

After a lost year with Colorado, Ohl will attempt to establish himself with his third organization. He is joining the Mets with a full slate of options and a good track record at the lower levels, where he has typically leaned on a low-90s fastball and an 81 mph changeup. Most of Ohl’s minor league work has come in Double-A ball, where he has logged a 3.47 ERA in 228 innings.

articles.title: Reds Claim Duncan Davitt, Paxton Schultz
body: The Reds announced a pair of waiver claims Monday. Cincinnati claimed right-hander Duncan Davitt off waivers from the Giants and fellow righty Paxton Schultz off waivers from the Nationals. They’ll both go right onto the Reds’ 40-man roster, which had five vacancies as of this morning.

Davitt entered the professional ranks as an 18th-round pick of the Rays in 2022. They wound up sending him (as well as Curtis Mead and Ben Peoples) to the White Sox in 2025 in a pre-deadline trade for righty Adrian Houser. Davitt made his major league debut this past April, but he only logged two appearances before the White Sox shipped him to the Braves for catcher Joey Bart in early August. He changed hands yet again when the Giants claimed him off waivers from the Braves in early September. Between the White Sox and Giants, he combined for eight innings of eight-run, 10-hit ball and recorded five strikeouts against four walks.

The 27-year-old Davitt still has two minor league options left, which is a plus for the Reds, though he had difficulty at the lower levels in 2026.
