While mostly leaning on a 93 mph fastball and an 84 mph slider, he registered a 6.04 ERA with an above-average 24.0% strikeout rate and slightly below-average 9.3% walk rate. He tossed 69 1/3 Triple-A innings and 6 2/3 in Double-A ball.

articles.title: White Sox Claim Graham Pauley
body: The White Sox announced that they have claimed infielder Graham Pauley off waivers from the Marlins. The Sox also outrighted left-hander Ky Bush and outfielder Junior Pérez to Triple-A Charlotte.

It’s a busy time of year for transactions, particularly those involving fringe players. The injured list goes away at 4 pm Central time today, meaning several players will be retaking roster spots. November 17 is the deadline for clubs to give roster spots to players who would otherwise be eligible for the Rule 5 draft. The roster squeeze will push many players to the waiver wire.

Pauley, now 26, was originally drafted by the Padres. He was sent to the Marlins in the 2024 deadline trade which sent Tanner Scott and Bryan Hoeing to San Diego. Pauley has received some big league chances with both the Padres and Marlins but hasn’t yet done much to prove himself. He exhausted his final option season in 2026 and is now slated to be out of options going forward. That will make it harder for him to hold a roster spot.

The Marlins have nudged him off but the White Sox have grabbed him, at least for now. It’s possible he will end up back on the waiver wire later in the offseason. As mention, Pauley hasn’t done much to establish himself at the big league level. That’s particularly true offensively. In 370 plate appearances, he has a.209/.272/.364 batting line.

articles.title: Braves Claim Mitchell Parker
body: The Braves announced that they have claimed left-hander Mitchell Parker off waivers from the Nationals.

Parker, 27, was a fifth-round pick by the Nats in 2020. He had a solid big league debut in 2024, making 29 starts and pitching 151 innings with a 4.29 ERA, a 20.6% strikeout rate and a 6.7% walk rate. He sat 92-93 mph that season, didn’t miss many bats and gave up a fair bit of loud contact in the air, but it was a solid enough season that gave him the look of an optionable fourth or fifth starter for Washington for the next few years.

The 2025 follow-up to that rookie effort was a disaster, however. Parker set a new career-high with 164 2/3 innings pitched, but his ERA skyrocketed to 5.68 while his strikeout and walk rates swung wildly in the wrong direction (14.2 K%, 8.0 BB%). Parker’s glut of fly-balls came back to bite him, too, as he was rocked for 25 round-trippers.

In 2026, Parker worked out of the bullpen with even shakier results: 34 2/3 innings and a 6.58 ERA. His strikeout and walk rates inched back in the right direction but were still worse than average. The lefty’s velocity ticked up to an average of 93.6 mph while working in relief, but that was at best a nominal silver lining.

articles.title: Orioles Release Heston Kjerstad
body: Orioles outfielder Heston Kjerstad is heading to the free agent market after clearing outright waivers, Andy Kostka of the Baltimore Banner reports. The team previously designated him for assignment, per Matt Weyrich of the Baltimore Sun.

This ends a bitterly disappointing Baltimore tenure for Kjerstad, who has fallen well short of expectations since the team took him second overall in the 2020 draft. Kjerstad missed the 2021 season with myocarditis, delaying his major league debut until 2023. Since then, the lefty-swinging Kjerstad has batted a meek.217/.280/.359 (80 wRC+) with 10 home runs and below-average strikeout and walk rates of 29.1% and 5.4%, respectively, in 333 plate appearances.

Now 27 years old, Kjerstad has yet to get an extended look in the bigs in any season. He set career highs in games (54) and PA (167) in 2025, but even then, he only played a third of the campaign. Kjerstad mustered a paltry 57 wRC+ that year, as he hit just.192/.240/.327 with four homers, a 26.9 strikeout percentage and a 3.6% walk rate.

articles.title: Marlins To Claim Cameron Weston
body: The Marlins claimed righty Cameron Weston off waivers from the division-rival Mets, reports Will Sammon of The Athletic. New York had claimed Weston off waivers from the Orioles in early September. He spent the remainder of the season with the Mets’ top affiliate in Syracuse but didn’t pitch in a big league game as a Met.

Weston, whom the Orioles drafted in the eighth round in 2022, developed into a notable prospect with the organization. Both Baseball America (No. 13) and FanGraphs (14th) regarded him as one of the Orioles’ 15 best farmhands at the outset of the 2025 season. At that point, he owned a 3.09 ERA with a 28.3% strikeout rate and 7.2% walk rate in the minors. Weston ascended to the Triple-A level for the first time that year, but he posted a 4.59 ERA with far less impressive strikeout and walk numbers (22.0% and 11.7%, respectively) in 135 1/3 innings.

This past season went even worse for the 26-year-old Weston, who struggled to a 7.89 ERA with an 11.9% walk rate over 51 2/3 innings with Triple-A Norfolk. Weston made his major league debut with a scoreless inning against the Blue Jays on May 28, but that counts as his lone MLB appearance thus far. The Orioles cut him from their 40-man roster on Sept. 1. To Weston’s credit, he ended 2026 on a high note after the Mets claimed him. In 6 1/3 frames with Triple-A Syracuse, he gave up just one run on two hits and recorded 10 strikeouts against one walk.

articles.title: Cubs To Re-Sign Jacob Webb
body: The Cubs and right-hander Jacob Webb have agreed to a new contract, reports Robert Murray of FanSided. It’s a $2.5MM guarantee with a $2MM salary in 2027 and $4MM club option for 2028 which comes with a $500K buyout. Webb’s previous deal had a $2.5MM club option for 2027 with no buyout. The Cubs will bring him back and give him that same figure on the new deal while adding an extra year of potential club control. There are also incentives, per MLBTR’s Steve Adams. Webb will earn an extra $125K at 35, 45, 55 and 65 games pitched, giving him a chance to earn an extra $500K.

Webb, now 33, was a free agent last winter. The Cubs signed him to a one-year, $1.5MM deal with a $2.5MM club option and incentives. He went on to have a good season in the Chicago bullpen. He tossed 67 innings with a 3.36 earned run average. His 8.8% walk rate and 40.8% ground ball rate were both right around league-wide average while his 25.7% strikeout rate was a few ticks better than par. He racked up nine saves and nine holds in a volatile Cubs bullpen.

Despite pretty consistently solid results, the market has never been too excited about Webb. In 2024, he posted a 3.02 ERA for the Orioles and then was non-tendered despite MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz projecting a fairly modest $1.7MM salary for 2025. He signed with the Rangers for 2025 on a deal with a $1.25MM guarantee. He gave Texas 66 innings with a flat ERA of 3.00. His gift was another non-tender, despite a projected salary of just $2MM.

articles.title: Mariners To Claim Isaac Mattson
body: The Mariners have claimed right-hander Isaac Mattson off waivers from the Pirates, MLBTR has learned. Pittsburgh hadn’t designated him for assignment, so it seems they instead quietly placed him on outright waivers at some point in the past couple days. Seattle’s 40-man roster is now four players over capacity, so they’ll need to subtract four players at some point prior to today’s deadline to get back down to 40.

Mattson, 31, has pitched in each of the past three seasons with the Pirates. He was a particularly solid arm for them in 2025, when he tallied a dozen holds and notched a spectacular 2.45 ERA with a 22.7% strikeout rate and 9.6% walk rate.

Mattson’s results went the wrong direction in 2026. Mattson was roughed up for a 5.35 ERA, although a weighty.347 average on balls in play and 68% strand rate were both well out of line with his career norms. Mattson did give up far too much hard contact (92.1 mph average exit velocity, 52.1% hard-hit rate), so the bloated ERA can’t be attributed solely to poor fortune on balls in play, but there’s still reason to forecast some positive/favorable regression for the righty.

In three seasons with the Bucs, Mattson logged a 3.83 ERA and 20 holds in 91 2/3 innings. He sits 94.2 mph on a four-seamer he uses at a nearly 75% clip, mixing in a relatively rare slider and changeup in a three-pitch repertoire. He also had a curveball early in his career, when he debuted with the 2021 Orioles, but he shelved that pitch back in 2024.

articles.title: Astros To Designate Jake Meyers For Assignment
body: The Astros are designating outfielder Jake Meyers for assignment, reports Ari Alexander of 7News. He’d been arbitration-eligible and projected for a $3.6MM salary, per MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz. Houston has five days to trade Meyers or place him on waivers. Outright waivers would be a 48-hour process, so we’ll know the outcome of his DFA within a week’s time.

Meyers, 30, was the Astros’ primary center fielder from 2023-25. He’s a strong defender whose bat had some flashes of potential but wound up grading out below average over that three-year span. In that time, he hit.243/.310/.370 (93 wRC+) with a 22% strikeout rate and 7.4% walk rate.

The righty-swinging Meyers has slightly better-than-average numbers against southpaws in his career but has been 15% worse than average versus righties, by measure of wRC+. He’s played more than 3800 career innings in center and boasts outstanding marks: 22 Defensive Runs Saved, 43 Outs Above Average, 35 Fielding Run Value.

Injuries have dogged Meyers throughout his career. A shoulder injury suffered during the 2021 postseason required surgery to repair a torn labrum. That procedure limited him to 52 games the following season. He was healthy for the bulk of the next three seasons but did have some brief injury absences due to calf troubles.

articles.title: Mets To Claim Jack Anderson
body: The Mets are claiming righty Jack Anderson off waivers from the Twins, reports Anthony DiComo of MLB.com. There wasn’t any indication Anderson had been removed from the Minnesota roster but they evidently put him on waivers recently.

It’s a busy time of year for transactions, especially with fringe players. The injured list goes away today at 4pm Central, meaning players on the 60-day IL need to retake 40-man spots. Just over the horizon, on November 17, is the Rule 5 protection deadline. Most teams will be giving roster spots to several prospects. Those dates put pressure on players near the edges of 40-man rosters.

This is the second waiver claim of 2026 for Anderson. He began the year in the Red Sox’ system and made a brief major league debut with Boston in April, getting into three games. He was optioned back to the minors and then was put on waivers in July. The Twins claimed him and then shuttled him between Triple-A and the majors for the rest of the season.

Anderson’s big league track record is still minimal. He has allowed three earned runs in 12 1/3 innings over seven appearances. The interest from the Mets presumably comes from his arsenal and minor league work. During his time in the big leagues this year, his fastball averaged below 91 miles per hour but also featured a splitter, slider and curveball. In the minors, he has been used in a swing role. He logged 180 innings over 2025 and 2026 with a 4.75 ERA, 23.3% strikeout rate and 6.7% walk rate.

articles.title: Orioles To Turn Down Ryan Mountcastle’s Club Option
body: The Orioles are going to turn down the $7.5MM club option on first baseman Ryan Mountcastle, reports Matt Weyrich of The Baltimore Sun. Mountcastle will become a free agent for the first time in his career.

When Baltimore avoided arbitration with Mountcastle last winter, the sides agreed to add the club option for next year. But the Orioles are now moving on after the 29-year-old Mountcastle endured a lost season. He fractured his left foot in early April, and just as he was about to begin a Triple-A rehab assignment in late July, he suffered a serious oblique strain. Mountcastle didn’t play again, limiting him to eight games in what could go down as his final season with the Orioles. It was the second straight disappointing and injury-shortened year for Mountcastle, who hit.250/.286/.367 and registered a career-worst 82 wRC+ over 89 games and 357 plate appearances in 2025.

articles.title: Clay Holmes Declines Player Option
body: Right-hander Clay Holmes declined his $12MM player option with the Cubs, per an announcement from the MLBPA. He is now a free agent. Teammates Hunter Harvey and Caleb Thielbar also head to free agency after their mutual options weren’t exercised.

Chicago landed Holmes in a deadline deal that sent prospect Jefferson Rojas to the Mets. The Cubs also received outfielder Tyrone Taylor. Holmes was recovering from a fractured fibula at the time of the trade. He returned in early August and made nine starts down the stretch for Chicago. He pitched to a 4.25 ERA over 48 2/3 innings. Holmes did not appear in the Wild Card series.

The Mets signed Holmes to a three-year, $38MM deal heading into the 2025 season. He was making the transition back to the rotation after working as a reliever for the majority of his big-league career. Holmes delivered 165 2/3 innings of a mid-3.00s ERA in the first year of the contract. He faded down the stretch, which wasn’t overly surprising given the huge jump in innings.

Holmes entered 2026 as a firm member of what seemed to be a deep rotation. Injuries and poor performance quickly thinned out the group. Holmes had a stellar 1.86 ERA through eight starts before a Spencer Jones line drive broke his leg. He missed nearly three months with the injury, though it did impact his desirability at the trade deadline. Chicago added Holmes and Kevin Gausman to a rotation crushed by injuries all season. It was a worthwhile gamble, and Holmes was solid in August, but the wheels came off in September.

articles.title: Cubs To Decline Club Option On Colin Rea
body: The Cubs are not expected to pick up their option on right-hander Colin Rea, reports Jesse Rogers of ESPN. The veteran had a $7.5MM club option for 2027 with a $1MM buyout.

Rea put together a decent season in a swingman role. He compiled a 4.34 ERA across 137 innings. The righty made 19 starts and 15 relief appearances. Rea opened the year in a long relief role, but it didn’t last long. He was thrust into a starting gig by mid-April due to injuries in the rotation.

Chicago brought in reinforcements through the trade market over the summer. The additions of David Peterson, Kevin Gausman, and Clay Holmes eventually bumped Rea back to the bullpen. He served as a sparsely used long reliever over the final two months of the year. Rea made the Wild Card roster but did not pitch in the series.

The Cubs added Rea on a one-year, $5MM deal heading into the 2025 season. The agreement included a $6MM team option for 2026, with a $750K buyout. Instead of picking up the option for 2026, Chicago worked out a new deal with Rea that included a $5.5MM salary this past season plus the aforementioned 2027 option. That scenario could play out once again this time around, with the two sides coming up with a reworked agreement.

articles.title: Mets Sign Christian Cairo
body: The Mets have signed infielder Christian Cairo to a major league deal, per a team announcement. Cairo closed the season in New York’s system after joining the organization via waiver claim.
Anthony DiComo of MLB.com reports that it’s a one-year split contract. The exact terms of the deal are not yet known.

Cairo signed a minor league deal with the Phillies last offseason that included an upward mobility clause. He was added to the 40-man roster shortly before the season. Cairo did not reach the majors with Philly. He was designated for assignment in mid-September. The Mets claimed him and stashed him at Triple-A.

The 25-year-old Cairo had spent his entire pro career in the Guardians organization before last season. He showed solid speed and a good eye at the plate in the minors, but topped out at Triple-A with Cleveland. Cairo posted a.676 OPS in 128 games at Lehigh Valley. He had an impressive 90 walks to 76 strikeouts over 516 plate appearances. He also stole 25 bases for the third straight season.

Cairo has two minor league option years remaining. He has extensive experience at second base, third base, and shortstop. He’s also spent time at all three outfield spots in the minors. Cairo could work his way into a utility role for the Mets at some point in 2027, depending on how their bench shakes out this offseason.

articles.title: Details On The Astros’ GM Search
body: The Astros hired Randy Flores as their new general manager on Friday, as the longtime Cardinals assistant GM was the choice to succeed Dana Brown as the head of Houston’s front office. Flores was one of 10 known candidates linked to the Astros’ search, and MLB.com’s Brian McTaggart adds another name by reporting that the team spoke to Yankees bench coach Brad Ausmus about the GM vacancy the day before Flores was hired.

Ausmus has been the Yankees’ bench coach for the last three seasons and was the Athletics’ bench coach in 2022. The 57-year-old is best known for his two stints as a big league manager (with the Tigers from 2014-17 and with the Angels for the 2019 season) and his 18-year playing career. Ten of Ausmus’ 18 seasons were spent in Houston, where he was a teammate and friend of Jeff Bagwell, a senior advisor to the Astros’ baseball ops department and a known close confidant to owner Jim Crane.

In terms of front office experience, Ausmus worked as a special assistant to then-Angels GM Billy Eppler in 2018, and as a field executive for the Padres from 2011-13. He interviewed for the Astros’ GM job before Brown was hired, and Ausmus also spoke with the club about becoming their next manager in the wake of A.J. Hinch’s departure following the sign-stealing scandal, prior to Houston’s hiring of Dusty Baker.

articles.title: Nationals Acquire Nate Furman From Giants
body: The Nationals have acquired infielder Nate Furman from the Giants, ESPN’s Jeff Passan reports. Minor league left-hander Tony Neubeck is heading to San Francisco in return. The Nats announced that left-hander Richard Lovelady has been designated for assignment in the corresponding move.

The trade reduces the Giants’ list of 40-man roster players to 49, though obviously a lot of work is still to be done before tomorrow’s deadline for removing players from the 60-day injured list. San Francisco needs to be down to 40 players in less than 24 hours, so expect the team to announce more trades, outrights, releases, or players designated for assignment in the near future.

As per RosterResource, the Nationals also have 45 players on their 40-man, so Furman adds to an already crowded picture in D.C. even with Lovelady now in DFA limbo. It could be that the Nats simply didn’t want to pass up on a chance to land a player they found intriguing, especially if the Giants’ roster situation left Furman available for a pretty inexpensive price. This is the second player the Nats have acquired from the Giants in the last week, as Braxton Roxby was claimed on waivers on Thursday.

A fourth-round pick for the Guardians in the 2022 draft, Furman was dealt for the first time in 2024, as the player-to-be-named-later in the deadline deal that sent Alex Cobb from San Francisco to Cleveland. Furman made his Major League debut this season, hitting.125/.243/.125 in his first 39 plate appearances against big league pitching and appearing in 22 games for the Giants.

articles.title: Miguel Andujar, Lucas Giolito, Griffin Canning Enter Free Agency After Declined Mutual Options
body: The Padres announced that Miguel Andujar and right-handers Lucas Giolito and Griffin Canning are all now free agents. San Diego declined its end of mutual options with Giolito and Canning, while Andujar declined his end of a mutual option. Andujar will receive a $2.9MM buyout from his declined $8MM mutual option, Giolito’s $8MM mutual option came with a $1.5MM buyout, and Canning’s $5MM mutual option has a $1.8MM buyout.

Mutual options are rarely exercised by both sides, so there was no surprise in any of these decisions. Had Andujar picked up his end of the $8MM option, it is likely the Padres would’ve declined theirs, so Andujar might have just been expediting the process.

Andujar signed a one-year deal with the Padres last winter worth $4MM in guaranteed money ($1.5MM in salary and $2.5MM via the buyout). Over 254 plate appearances, Andujar hit.259/.303/.423 with five homers, but he spent over two months on the injured list after a wayward Lucas Erceg pitch fractured his right wrist. The injury ended Andujar’s regular season but he was able to return for the playoffs, going 0-for-3 with a walk in four pinch-hit appearances during San Diego’s postseason run.

articles.title: Cardinals Decline Ryne Stanek’s Club Option
body: The Cardinals have declined their $6MM club option on right-hander Ryne Stanek for the 2027 season, the St. Louis Post-Dispatch’s Derrick Goold reports. Stanek will instead take the $1MM buyout and enter free agency.

Stanek inked a one-year, $2.5MM deal last winter, so the righty will walk away with $3.5MM from his lone season in the Gateway City. He delivered a 4.02 ERA, 24.3% strikeout rate, and 12% walk rate over 62 2/3 innings, and his 70 appearances tied George Soriano for second on the team.

It was almost exactly a standard season for Stanek, with his numbers coming very close to the 3.87 ERA, 26.8K%, and 11.9BB% he has posted over 521 MLB innings with six different teams over parts of 10 seasons. At least in bottom-line results, Stanek’s 2026 was a step up from his previous two seasons, when he had a 5.09 ERA over 111 1/3 innings with the Mets and Mariners.

Stanek remains a very hard thrower, as his fastball averaged 98mph. He also showed batters something new, as Stanek decreased usage of his fastball from 57.1% in 2025 to 51.5% in 2026, while bumping up the use of a very effective slider.

Since Stanek turned 35 in July, his age may limit him to just one-year offers this winter, even though he appears to have plenty left in the tank. The Cardinals and other teams figure to show interest in a durable veteran who can cover innings can still deliver the velocity to fool younger batters.

articles.title: Mets Outright Four Players Off 40-Man Roster
body: The Mets have outrighted outfielder Cristian Pache, infielder Eric Wagaman, left-hander Philip Abner, and right-hander Cameron Weston off their 40-man roster, MLB.com’s Anthony DiComo reports. This brings New York’s 40-man roster down to 39 players, putting the team in better shape prior to tomorrow’s deadline for 40-man roster compliance.

Pache and Wagaman were the only members of the group to see any MLB action with the Mets in 2026, as Abner and Weston were both September waiver claims (from the Giants and Orioles, respectively). New York designated Pache for assignment three days ago, and since he has been outrighted in the past, he can and probably will elect free agency instead of accepting the outright assignment.

Pache signed a minors deal with the Amazins last winter, and was selected to the active roster just after the trade deadline. Of Pache’s 15 games with the Mets, he made only one start and was mostly used as a late-game defensive replacement, so he had only eight plate appearances. Pache has only a.514 OPS over his 618 career PA in the majors, and will likely again hit the open market in search of another team looking for speed and outfield depth.

articles.title: Red Sox Exercise Club Option On Garrett Whitlock
body: The Red Sox are exercising their $8.25MM club option on righty Garrett Whitlock, per Andrew Parker of SoxProspects.com. Whitlock will now officially be back in 2027 as the main bridge to closer Aroldis Chapman.

It was an easy call for the Sox to make. The 30-year-old Whitlock is coming off a second straight dominant season out of the Boston bullpen. After an internal brace procedure on his right elbow kept him out for most of 2024, Whitlock came back firing on all cylinders with a 2.25 earned run average in 72 innings in 2025. The righty’s 31.1% strikeout rate, 8.2% walk rate, and 45.1% ground ball rate were all better than average. Even more impressively, Whitlock allowed just two home runs all season, or 0.25 HR/9. That was the second-best mark in baseball among pitchers who threw at least 60 innings.

Whitlock was just as dominant this year in many respects. He lowered his ERA to 1.72 in 52 1/3 innings, and he struck out just under 30% of opponents. Although he didn’t get as many ground balls, he was quite stingy when it came to giving out free passes. Among pitchers with at least 50 innings of relief, Whitlock’s 4.5% walk rate was fourth-best, right behind Phillies closer Jhoan Duran (4.2%). FanGraphs values his 2025-26 work at 4.2 wins above replacement. That’s tied with Chapman and Twins/Blue Jays righty Louis Varland for fifth-best among qualified relievers.

articles.title: Padres Exercise Club Option On Kyle Hart; Yuki Matsui Declines To Opt Out
body: The Padres have some clarity on a couple of bullpen pieces. The team has picked up their $2.5MM club option on Kyle Hart, while left-hander Yuki Matsui has declined to exercise his opt-out clause, according to Kevin Acee of the San Diego Union-Tribune. Hart is now under control for 2027, while Matsui still has a $7MM player option for 2028.

Matsui is the more consequential of the two players. Since making his MLB debut with the Padres in 2024, he’s delivered 190 innings of relief with a solid 3.17 earned run average and above-average 25.1% strikeout rate. He’s also been durable, making just one trip to the 15-day injured list – a one-month stint early this year for a groin strain. Matsui has thrown at least 62 2/3 innings in each of his three seasons with the Padres and ranks 20th among qualified relievers since 2024 with the 190-inning total.

This year was an anomaly for Matsui in a few ways. For one thing, he lowered his ERA to an excellent 1.83, over two runs better than in 2025. He also cut back on the long ball after struggling in that area before, allowing less than one homer per nine, while recording a 26.2% strikeout rate. Despite working with below-average velocity, Matsui excelled at limiting hard contact. Statcast ranked him in the 90th percentile of average exit velocity (86.8 mph) and the 95th percentile of hard-hit rate (30.5%). Matsui’s 3.02 xERA and 4.17 SIERA weren’t quite as rosy, but on the surface, he was a solid reliever for San Diego.

articles.title: Yankees Part Ways With Omar Minaya, Brian Sabean
body: The Yankees are not renewing the contracts of Omar Minaya and Brian Sabean, according to The New York Post’s Jon Heyman. Both were serving as advisors to general manager Brian Cashman. The two executives are now free to look for jobs in other clubs’ front offices.

Minaya and Sabean were both hired by the Yankees in January 2023. Minaya held the title of senior advisor to baseball operations, while Sabean was more of a general advisor to Cashman. The soon-to-be 68-year-old Minaya has worked in baseball front offices for over four decades. He most prominently served as the general manager of the Expos from 2002-04, then as the Mets’ general manager for the 2005-10 seasons. Some highlights from the latter tenure include signing Pedro Martinez and Carlos Beltran as free agents, acquiring Johan Santana via trade, and drafting Matt Harvey in 2010.

Minaya was fired as GM in October 2010. He spent the following years working in the Padres’ baseball operations department and with the Players Association as an advisor to then-executive director Tony Clark. Minaya returned to the Mets in special assistant and ambassador roles before a brief stint as a consultant for MLB and finally, his time with the Yankees. It’s been eight years since Minaya served as a GM in any capacity, being part of the Mets’ interim committee in 2018 when Sandy Alderson took a leave of absence. Nonetheless, he comes with plenty of experience and should garner interest in an advisory role.

articles.title: Padres’ Wandy Peralta Exercises Player Option
body: Padres left-hander Wandy Peralta has exercised his $4.45MM player option, according to Jon Heyman of The New York Post. He will return as a member of San Diego’s bullpen for 2027.

This is the third straight offseason in which Peralta has chosen to remain with the Padres. His original four-year deal, signed in February 2024, included a $4.25MM player option for 2025 and $4.45MM player options for 2026 and’27. Compared to teammate Yuki Matsui, who is four years younger and just posted a sub-2.00 ERA (albeit with plenty of good luck), Peralta is more likely to have faced a pay cut if he tested the open market this time around. Instead, he’ll play out the final year of his current deal. Matsui has until 4:00pm CT tomorrow to decide whether to stick around for two years and $13.5MM.

The 35-year-old Peralta has been a solid reliever since the start of 2020. In 376 innings since then, he’s held opponents to a.669 OPS and a 3.26 earned run average. While Peralta typically posts below-average strikeout numbers, he thrives on a sinker-changeup combination and exceptional ground ball rates. From 2021-25, only 11 pitchers with at least 250 innings had a better ground ball rate than Peralta’s 56.8%.

articles.title: Braves Sign Vidal Bruján To Minor League Deal
body: The Braves have brought in infielder Vidal Bruján on a minor league pact, according to his transactions log at MiLB.com. He will report to Triple-A Gwinnett as a depth option.

The 28-year-old Bruján has played in 271 big league games for six clubs since debuting in 2021. He’s never shown much at the plate, taking 658 plate appearances and batting.197/.266/.272 with a 53 wRC+. His biggest sample of work came in 2024 with the Marlins. Bruján had a 74 wRC+ in 278 plate appearances that year, striking out and walking at better than average rates but showing nothing in the way of power.

Bruján’s deal with Atlanta is technically a reunion. The Braves claimed him off waivers from the Orioles in August 2025 and gave him 47 plate appearances down the stretch in a lost season. Bruján was designated for assignment in January, claimed off waivers by the Twins, then quickly flipped to the Mets in a cash deal. He appeared in nine games for New York in May and June but spent most of the season at Triple-A, posting a 113 wRC+ and chipping in 16 stolen bases.

The Braves figure to invite Bruján to Spring Training (whenever it ends up happening) as a non-roster player. Ozzie Albies will return at second base after his $7MM club option was exercised. RosterResource currently has Jim Jarvis as Atlanta’s starting shortstop. The team could try to re-sign Mauricio Dubon as a stopgap given Jarvis’ meager 57 wRC+ in his debut campaign.

articles.title: Angels Outright Sebastián Rivero; Sammy Peralta Elects Free Agency
body: Nov. 1: Peralta has indeed elected free agency, as announced by the club.

Oct. 29: The Angels announced Thursday that left-hander Sammy Peralta and catcher Sebastián Rivero both went unclaimed on waivers and were assigned outright to Triple-A Salt Lake. Both are eligible to elect free agency and will presumably do so.

The 28-year-old Peralta split the 2026 season between the Rockies and Halos, combining for 23 innings with a 6.65 earned run average. He fanned a respectable 20.5% of opponents against a solid 8% walk rate, leading to better reviews from metrics like SIERA (3.96). However, Peralta was quite homer-prone, plunked four of the 112 batters he faced, and was dinged for a brutal.417 average on balls in play, which did him no favors. He’s now pitched in parts of four major league seasons and carries a 5.64 ERA in 68 2/3 frames. The soft-tossing southpaw has averaged 89.1 mph on his four-seamer and 88.8 mph on his sinker during his brief major league stints.

Rivero, 27, took only 57 plate appearances for the Angels, hitting.245/.286/.283. He’s had brief stints as a backup catcher both with Kansas City and Anaheim, totaling 164 major league plate appearances with a.197/.247/.237 slash. He’s never hit much in the minors either, but Rivero is a quality defender who has found himself occasionally pressed into big league action despite being the third or fourth catcher on the depth chart with multiple organizations. Assuming both players do indeed become free agents, they’ll look to catch on as minor league depth with a new team in free agency.

articles.title: Rays Exercise Club Option On Drew Rasmussen
body: The Rays have exercised ace right-hander Drew Rasmussen’s club option for 2027, per a team announcement. Rasmussen is in line to earn $20MM next season.

This was a slam-dunk decision for the 2026 American League champions, who have seen Rasmussen blossom into one of the majors’ best starters over the past few years. Acquired from the Brewers in a May 2021 trade centering on shortstop Willy Adames, Rasmussen has logged a stellar 2.73 ERA in 133 appearances (111 starts) and 600 1/3 innings as a Ray. An internal brace procedure held him to 73 1/3 innings from 2023-24, but he has made 61 starts since then and continued to produce excellent results.

This past season, in which he earned his second straight All-Star nod, counts as the best of Rasmussen’s career. Across a personal-high 172 innings, the 31-year-old recorded a 2.67 ERA with above-average strikeout and walk rates of 26% and 4.8%, respectively. He ranked seventh in the majors in ERA and fWAR (5.0), while his walk rate was second among qualified starters. Teammate Nick Martinez finished first in that category.

articles.title: Orioles Make Multiple Roster Moves
body: The Orioles made several roster tweaks on Saturday. Right-handers Albert Suarez, Codi Heuer, and Colin Selby cleared waivers, per a team announcement. Suarez elected free agency. Heuer accepted an outright assignment to Triple-A. Selby was reinstated from the 60-day IL and sent to Norfolk with Heuer.

Suarez was a waiver wire mainstay this season. He was designated for assignment on five occasions. Each time, the veteran righty found his way back to the organization. Suarez was most recently selected to the big-league club during the final week of the regular season. He made one appearance, tossing four scoreless frames in relief to pick up a win over the Yankees.

Baltimore routinely leaned on Suarez whenever the club needed a fresh arm. He’d be added to the roster to save a tired bullpen, then bumped off whenever another player needed his spot. Suarez would inevitably pass through waivers and accept an outright assignment or re-up with the team on a new minor league deal. There’s a solid chance that happens again this time around. After spending five seasons in Asia, Suarez has been with the Orioles for the past three years.

Heuer came to Baltimore at the trade deadline. He was one of the final moves on deadline day, heading to the Orioles from Milwaukee in exchange for cash considerations. It was the second trade in two days for the righty. Heuer and Bo Naylor went to the Brewers in the deal that sent Blake Perkins and Craig Yoho to the Guardians.

articles.title: Rays Finalize Yandy Diaz’s Contract
body: The Rays have completed Yandy Diaz’s contract for 2027, per Marc Topkin of the Tampa Bay Times. The slugger had a $10MM club option for next season that turned into a guaranteed $13MM deal if he reached 500 plate appearances. Diaz comfortably reached that threshold, but needed to finish the season healthy to finalize the deal.

The 35-year-old Diaz provided another productive season atop Tampa Bay’s lineup. He hit.293 with 22 homers as the club’s primary DH. He led the AL with 180 hits. Diaz was at least 20% better than league average at the plate for the fifth consecutive season.

Diaz was a solid contributor on a Rays squad that represented the AL in the World Series. He recorded a.742 OPS across 59 playoff at-bats. Diaz was particularly important in the ALCS against the Guardians, hitting.333 with two home runs. His two-run shot in the eighth inning of Game 6 helped seal Tampa Bay’s series-clinching win.

The three-year, $24MM extension Diaz signed with the Rays heading into the 2023 season has worked out swimmingly for Tampa Bay. The cost has risen, and Diaz is in his mid-30s, but the numbers have been there. The Rays preemptively exercised their 2026 club option on Diaz before the 2025 season. The organization also tacked on the 2027 option at that time. Diaz made $12MM this past season. He’ll do one better on that figure for next year after reaching the vesting threshold.

articles.title: Astros To Acquire Evan Reifert
body: 9:05pm CT: The Rays will receive cash in the trade, per Marc Topkin of the Tampa Bay Times.
8:39pm CT: The Astros have acquired right-hander Evan Reifert in a deal with the Rays, per Robert Murray of FanSided.
Reifert is coming off a solid year at Triple-A, recording a 2.48 ERA across 46 appearances with Durham. He’ll now head to Houston in search of his first chance in the majors.

The 27-year-old Reifert has spent the majority of his pro career with the Rays. He was signed as an undrafted free agent by the Brewers in 2020. Milwaukee sent him to Tampa Bay after one season in a deal that netted infielder Mike Brosseau.

Reifert has routinely put up massive strikeout numbers in the minors, but it’s almost always come with an untenable walk rate. He did manage a 9.9% walk rate in 35 games at Double-A in 2024, to go with an excellent 40.4% strikeout rate. That was enough for the Nationals to select him with the fifth pick in the Rule 5 Draft. Reifert walked 12 in seven Spring Training games. Washington returned him to the Rays shortly before Opening Day.

Tampa Bay bumped Reifert to Triple-A for the first time in 2025. He recorded a 2.48 ERA over 29 innings. He’s posted nearly identical stat lines the past two years with the Bulls, including a strikeout rate around 39% and a walk rate just over 14%. The fact that he’s still missing bats at the highest minor league level is an encouraging sign. The control remains the issue and is likely what has held him back from getting a big-league look up to this point.

articles.title: Padres Decline Club Option On Nick Pivetta
body: 8:16pm CT: Acee notes in a follow-up post that there are questions about the health of Pivetta’s elbow. He added that declining the option was expected and the team and player could still work out a new deal.
7:24pm CT: The Padres have decided not to pick up right-hander Nick Pivetta’s team option, as first reported by Kevin Acee of the San Diego Union-Tribune. He’s now a free agent.

San Diego signed Pivetta to a four-year, $55MM contract heading into the 2025 season. The original stipulations of the deal gave the veteran righty opt-outs after 2026 and 2027. However, an extended injury absence this year changed the arrangement.

Since Pivetta spent more than 130 days on the injured list this year, the Padres were given a $14MM option for 2027. It’s not a massive price tag, but Pivetta’s injury history likely gave the club some hesitation. The decision doesn’t mean he won’t be back with the team, as the sides could work out a new agreement. President of baseball operations A.J. Preller hinted at the possibility a couple of weeks ago.

Pivetta made it through four appearances before hitting the IL in mid-April with a flexor strain. He had setbacks in his rehab process and didn’t make it back to the majors until early September. Pivetta was effective when available, pitching to a 2.86 ERA backed by a 3.18 xFIP and a 3.17 SIERA. He tossed 34 2/3 innings across eight starts. Pivetta added another 7 2/3 frames in the postseason.

articles.title: White Sox To Hire Matt Roffe As Scouting Director
body: The White Sox are set to hire Matt Roffe as their scouting director, Katie Woo and Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic report. The team is not expected to announce the move until next week, per Scott Merkin of MLB.com.

Roffe is heading to Chicago on the heels of winning the 2026 World Series as a member of the Brewers’ elite front office. The 30-year-old alumnus of Washington University (St. Louis) spent a half-decade in Milwaukee and worked in multiple positions, most recently as the club’s assistant director of domestic scouting. He took over that role in November 2025.

Roffe also has past experience as an analyst in Arizona’s front office, where he overlapped with current White Sox assistant general manager Josh Barfield from 2019-21. Barfield was the Diamondbacks’ director of player development before he became a top lieutenant for White Sox GM Chris Getz in 2023.

Getz is bringing in Roffe to replace former director of amateur scouting Mike Shirley, who resigned on Sept. 12. Shirley was a longtime White Sox employee who was at the helm of their amateur scouting department for seven years, but he resigned after the team placed him on administrative leave and investigated allegations of verbal harassment, as Brittany Ghiroli and Keith Law of The Athletic reported at the time. The White Sox spent first-round picks on Garrett Crochet, Colson Montgomery, Noah Schultz, Jacob Gonzalez, Hagen Smith, Billy Carlson and Roch Cholowsky during Shirley’s stint as their amateur scouting leader.

articles.title: Orioles Decline Club Option On Luis Robert Jr.
body: OCTOBER 31: The Orioles have declined Robert’s option, according to Alden González of ESPN.

OCTOBER 29: The Orioles are expected to decline their $20MM club option on outfielder Luis Robert Jr., reports Francys Romero of BeisbolFR. Robert will become a free agent and collect a $2MM buyout on his way out the door.

Robert, now 29, signed an extension with the White Sox back in 2020. That deal ran through 2025, with $20MM club options for 2026 and 2027, both of which came with $2MM buyouts. Robert hadn’t yet made his major league debut at the time that deal was signed but he would go on to flash some All-Star upside in subsequent years.

That was especially the case in 2023. He got into 145 games that year, hit 38 home runs and stole 20 bases. He slashed.264/.315/.542 for a 129 wRC+. FanGraphs credited him with five wins above replacement. He finished 12th in American League Most Valuable Player voting. The rest of the deal looked good and the club options looked like bargains.

A lot has changed since then. Robert battled injuries in the final two guaranteed years of his deal. He got into a total of 210 games over the 2024 and 2025 campaigns and produced a lackluster.223/.288/.372 line and 85 wRC+ in the process. The Sox picked up his 2026 option but then traded him to the Mets for Luisangel Acuña and Truman Pauley.

articles.title: Reds Decline Mutual Options For Eugenio Suárez, Pierce Johnson
body: The Reds have declined their 2027 mutual options for third baseman Eugenio Suárez and right-hander Pierce Johnson, the team announced. Both players are now free agents, leaving the Reds with five openings on their 40-man roster.

Neither decision comes as a surprise, especially considering it has been over a decade since both a team and a player triggered a mutual option. Suárez’s $16MM option did not come with a buyout. Meanwhile, the Reds chose to pay Johnson a $1MM buyout in lieu of the $8MM they would have owed him had both sides exercised the option.

Unless the 35-year-old Suárez sticks around on a new deal, this will wrap up his second stint in Cincinnati. The right-handed slugger previously played there from 2015-21, when he put together three seasons of at least 4.0 fWAR and two with 30-plus home runs. He also earned his first of two All-Star nods during that stretch.

The Reds first moved on from Suárez when they sent him (and outfielder Jesse Winker) to the Mariners in a blockbuster trade three weeks before the 2022 season opened. He then spent two seasons with Seattle before going to Arizona for one and a half. The Diamondbacks traded him back to the Mariners ahead of the 2025 deadline. Between the D-backs and pennant-contending Mariners last year, Suárez swatted 49 homers for the second time in his career and slashed.228/.298/.526. Despite a low batting average and on-base percentage, he put up a solidly above-average wRC+ of 125.

articles.title: Emilio Pagán Declines Player Option
body: Reliever Emilio Pagán has declined his $10MM player option with the Reds for 2027, Francys Romero of BeisbolFR reports. Unless he signs a new deal with the Reds by 4 p.m. CT on Nov. 2, the right-hander will head to the open market.

The 35-year-old Pagán, who has pitched for six teams since he debuted with the Mariners in 2017, spent the past three seasons in Cincinnati. He originally joined the club on a two-year, $16MM guarantee in December 2023, but the first season of the contract didn’t go particularly well. Pagán had separate stints on the injured list with triceps and lat issues, and he only delivered 38 innings of 4.50 ERA ball when healthy.

The past two years went far better for Pagán, who took over as the Reds’ closer in 2025. That year, he converted 32 of 38 save opportunities and recorded a stingy 2.88 ERA with quality strikeout and walk rates of 30.0% and 8.1%, respectively, over 68 2/3 frames. He was able to keep runs off the board despite inducing ground balls just 28.7% of the time. Pagán has walked that tightrope throughout his career, having logged a 29.3% ground-ball rate over 549 1/3 innings in the majors.

articles.title: Braves Hire Dana Brown For Scouting Advisor Role
body: The Braves are reuniting with Dana Brown as a senior advisor in their amateur scouting department, as per USA Today’s Bob Nightengale. It’s a homecoming for Brown, who worked as Atlanta’s VP of scouting from 2019-22 before he was hired as the Astros’ general manager.

Brown and Braves president of baseball operations Alex Anthopoulos have a long working relationship dating back to their days in Montreal, when Anthopoulos was Brown’s assistant when Brown was hired as the Expos’ director of amateur scouting in 2002. Brown continued in that role with the Expos/Nationals through the franchise’s move to Washington and until 2009, when Anthopoulos (now the Blue Jays’ GM) hired Brown for a special assistant’s role in Toronto. Once Anthopoulos was hired by the Braves following the 2017 season, Brown reunited with Anthopoulos once more within a couple of years.

The Astros’ hiring of Brown was a rare case of a team making a front office change right after a World Series title, as former GM James Click was let go after the playoff run due to clashes with owner Jim Crane (who is known for playing a direct role in baseball operations). While Brown didn’t capture a championship during his time in Houston, he also had a much better record than most GMs who are shown the door. Houston made the ALCS in 2023 and won two AL West titles in Brown’s three full seasons as GM, and the Astros even ended up winning the division again this year, albeit with an 81-81 record.

articles.title: Cubs Re-Sign Gabe Klobosits To Minor League Deal
body: The Cubs have signed right-hander Gabe Klobosits to a new minor league contract, 7 News’ Ari Alexander reports. Klobosits is back for his second year in the organization, after his minors deal last offseason resulted in a 3.51 ERA, 26.9% strikeout rate, and 13.8% walk rate over 33 1/3 innings with the Cubs’ Triple-A affiliate in Iowa.

This marked Klobosits’ first taste of affiliated baseball since 2023, as he spent the previous two years with independent league teams. The righty was a 36th-round pick for the Nationals in the 2017 draft, and he has pitched in parts of nine pro seasons with some notable interruptions — Klobosits missed most of 2018-19 due to Tommy John surgery, and he didn’t pitch at all in 2020 when the minor league season was canceled by the pandemic.

Klobosits’ tenure in Washington paid off with some playing time at the big league level, as the righty’s MLB resume consists of 11 1/3 innings of 5.56 ball for the Nats during the 2021 season. He then pitched in the minors with the A’s and Blue Jays over the next two years before turning to indy ball.

For his career, Klobosits has a 4.09 ERA, 23.18% strikeout rate, and 12.3% walk rate over 81 1/3 innings at the Triple-A level. He has worked almost exclusively as a reliever, apart from a few pseudo-starts as an opener. Klobosits’ shaky control and a two-month stint on the injured list in 2026 probably kept him from getting any looks even from a Chicago team desperate for healthy relievers, but the Cubs clearly liked enough of what they saw to bring the 31-year-old back into the fold.

articles.title: Two Players Elect Free Agency
body: Two players who saw regular-season action for the two World Series teams have elected minor league agency, according to the official MiLB.com transactions page. To qualify for minor league free agency, players must be outrighted off their teams’ 40-man rosters during the course of the season without being added back, and they must have either three years of MLB service time or multiple outright assignments over the course of their careers.

Dunn signed a minor league deal with the White Sox last winter, and was traded to the Rays in May. He was quickly added to the active roster as infield depth when Ben Williamson was placed on the IL, and Dunn had a.258 OPS in 12 plate appearances over nine games, appearing mostly as a late-game substitute. Tampa optioned Dunn back to Triple-A after that nine-game stint, and outrighted him off the 40-man in September.

Dunn has now played in parts of the last three MLB seasons, and has hit.197/.253/.275 over 157 PA in the Show with the Brewers and Rays. He can play all over the infield (and has played left field in the minors) and has some good base-stealing ability, so Dunn will try to parlay that skillset into another minor league contract this offseason. Dunn is out of minor league options, which will complicate his chances of sticking on a 40-man roster.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Los Angeles Angels
body: The Angels, amazingly, just had their first 100-loss season. That’s a low point for the franchise but there is optimism about the future because the 2027 club will have a new owner, a new front office leader and a new manager.

They haven’t had a winning record since 2015. Despite that long run of poor results, they have resisted rebuilding and prioritized short-term contention.

articles.title: Luis Severino To Exercise Player Option, Remain With A’s
body: Athletics right-hander Luis Severino will exercise his $22MM player option and forgo a return to the open market, as first reported by Mike Rodriguez of Rompiendo Sports. Severino will remain with the A’s in their final season in Sacramento before becoming a free agent in the 2027-28 offseason.

Although Severino previously expressed dissatisfaction with the facilities at Sutter Health Park, it’s no surprise that the veteran will stick around for the third and final year of his contract. Severino posted a 4.16 ERA over 12 starts and 62 2/3 innings before going on the 15-day injured list at the end of May with a strain of his shoulder capsule and subscapularis muscle. The injury proved to be season-ending, as Severino was able to resume throwing but didn’t get deep enough into his recovery process to even begin a minor league rehab assignment.

Between this shortened season and his so-so performance in 2025, Severino wouldn’t have made anywhere close to $22MM in free agency. Opting out of his deal also would’ve meant hitting the open market in offseason that is bound to be interrupted by a lockout, so it makes plenty of sense for Severino to take his guaranteed payday and focus entirely on returning to the mound in 2027 (Severino’s age-33 season).

articles.title: Astros Hire Randy Flores As General Manager
body: The Astros have hired Cardinals assistant GM/scouting director Randy Flores as their new general manager. The team announced the move on Friday evening.

“Randy has had a huge impact on the Cardinals over the last 10 seasons,” Houston owner Jim Crane said in the press release. “Throughout the entire interview process, we’ve been thoroughly impressed with Randy and with his background in scouting and player acquisition. We’re happy to welcome Randy and his family to the Astros and we can’t wait to get to work on bringing another championship to Houston.” Flores and Crane will meet with the media during an introductory press conference on Monday morning.

It’s a surprise turn of events. The Athletic reported on Thursday that Brewers assistant GM Matt Kleine had emerged as the frontrunner for the position. Chandler Rome of The Athletic reports that Houston offered the GM job to Kleine on Wednesday evening, hours before Milwaukee won its first World Series.

Although it’s unclear precisely what changed, The Athletic suggests that Kleine had been seeking the title ‘president of baseball operations’ earlier in the week. They write that the Milwaukee AGM never pulled his name out of the running, though it’s possible there was some kind of hangup in negotiations on title and/or salary.

articles.title: Clint Hurdle, Rockies Parting Ways
body: Clint Hurdle and the Rockies are parting ways, the baseball lifer announced on social media (link via Thomas Harding of MLB.com). Hurdle has been in the organization for the past five seasons, mostly in a special assistant role.

The 69-year-old Hurdle is better known for his first stint with the club. After playing parts of 10 seasons in the big leagues, he went into minor league managing in the late 1980s. Hurdle began coaching in the Colorado farm system in 1994, then worked his way onto the MLB staff as hitting coach. He was promoted to manager in 2002 and led the club for eight seasons, including their trip to the World Series in’07. The Rockies fired him in May’09 after a rough start to that season.

Hurdle spent a season as hitting coach in Texas before returning to the managerial ranks. He took the lead job with the Pirates in 2011. Hurdle led the club to three straight playoff appearances from 2013-15 (still the franchise’s only postseason berths since the Barry Bonds era) and won NL Manager of the Year honors in 2013. He managed parts of nine seasons with the Bucs but was fired at the tail end of the’19 campaign.

After a couple seasons out of baseball, Hurdle returned to Colorado in the special assistant capacity. He moved back onto the coaching staff in 2025, taking over as interim hitting coach and then interim bench coach when the Rox made various changes amidst a 119-loss season. He returned to the special assistant role for the’26 season, the first year under the new front office team of Paul DePodesta and Josh Byrnes.

articles.title: Kyle Higashioka, Jakob Junis To Become Free Agents
body: All three of the Rangers’ mutual options will be bought out, reports Shawn McFarland of The Dallas Morning News. ESPN’s Jesse Rogers first reported this afternoon that designated hitter Joc Pederson passed on his end of an $18.5MM option. Catcher Kyle Higashioka will receive a $1MM buyout in lieu of a $7MM salary; reliever Jakob Junis is paid a $1.25MM buyout on a $5MM option.

McFarland’s report doesn’t specify which side formally declined the Higashioka/Junis options, yet it’s safe to assume the team passed on both. Neither player was much of a factor down the stretch, and Texas is clearly working against payroll limitations.

Higashioka wraps up a two-year, $13.5MM free agent deal. He combined for a.233/.296/.391 slash line with 18 homers across 513 plate appearances. That’s perfectly serviceable for a part-time catcher. Higashioka has a solid reputation as a receiver but has been below average at throwing out baserunners. He didn’t play after July 20 due to a flexor strain in his forearm.

It’ll almost certainly be a one-year deal this time around, as Higashioka hits the market in advance of his age-37 season. The Phillies, Yankees, Diamondbacks, Cubs, Brewers, Marlins, Reds, Red Sox, Twins and Tigers could all be in the market for a backup catcher. Texas will also need to address the position. Elias Díaz is a free agent, leaving Danny Jansen and Logan O’Hoppe as an underwhelming catching tandem.

articles.title: Rangers To Select Aidan Curry
body: The Rangers are adding right-hander Aidan Curry to their 40-man roster, reports Joel Sherman of The New York Post. Curry signed as an undrafted free agent in 2020 and has appeared in parts of seven seasons in the minors. That meant he’d have qualified for minor league free agency on Monday if the Rangers didn’t select his contract.

Curry has a prototypical pitcher’s build at 6’5″ and 205 pounds. A product of a New York high school, he’s worked as a starter throughout his minor league career. The results have been mixed, but Curry has a five-pitch arsenal and has shown the ability to push his fastball into the mid-90s.

It has been a couple seasons since Baseball America ranked him among the top 30 prospects in a weak Texas farm system. Brendan Gawlowski of FanGraphs was a little more bullish, slotting him 25th in the organization back in April. Gawlowski’s report graded all five pitches at average or better but noted that lackluster control is likely to push him to the bullpen.

Texas has continued to give Curry developmental reps as a starter. He opened this year in High-A, played most of the season in Double-A, and made one start in mid-August at Triple-A Round Rock. Curry combined for a 4.93 earned run average across 104 innings. He struck out an impressive 29% of opponents against a concerning 12.4% walk rate that points to his likely future as a reliever. The Rangers have enough bullpen uncertainty that they could make that transition as soon as next spring, as Curry’s spot on the 40-man should have him under consideration for a midseason promotion.

articles.title: Michael Soroka Declines Mutual Option With D-Backs
body: Michael Soroka has officially declined his end of a $10MM mutual option with the Diamondbacks, reports Nick Piecoro of The Arizona Republic. He’ll be paid a $1MM buyout and return to free agency.

This was inevitable, as Soroka has put himself in position to do pretty well financially. The Diamondbacks picked him up on a $7.5MM deal last offseason. (He earned an additional $1.35MM in performance bonuses by starting 20 games.) He was initially slated to open the season in a swing role, but an Opening Day injured list stint for Merrill Kelly drew him into the starting five.

Soroka was one of Torey Lovullo’s more reliable starters and held a rotation spot all season. He pitched to a 3.41 earned run average across 116 innings. He led Arizona starters with a 24.1% strikeout rate while limiting his free passes to a 6% clip. Soroka tailed off a bit in the second half as he navigated injured list stints for a left glute strain and arm inflammation, yet it was mid-rotation production on a rate basis. This was also his highest workload since 2019.

The innings questions are going to keep Soroka from commanding a massive contract, but he’s very likely to secure a multi-year deal. He’s entering his age-29 season and has one of the better strikeout and walk profiles of the group of mid-tier free agent starters. Soroka has a chance at three years, with a two-year pact in the $10-12MM range feeling like a floor.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Tampa Bay Rays
body: The Rays posted the best record in the American League this season (98-64) and cemented their status as the Junior Circuit’s top team by toppling the Yankees and Guardians en route to the American League pennant. Tampa Bay ran into a Brewers buzzsaw in the World Series, however, falling four games to one to a dominant Milwaukee pitching staff. The Rays now face critical offseason decisions on some of their top players as they look to retool around an impressive young core and gear up for what they hope will be another deep October run in 2027.

Yandy Díaz, 1B/DH: $13MM through 2027 (Díaz reached vesting option threshold in August; contract becomes official once he passes a postseason physical) Steven Matz, LHP: $7.5MM through 2027 Option Decisions
