articles.title: Dodgers Notes: Ohtani, Klein, Coaching Staff
body: Shohei Ohtani will not require surgery on either the knee or biceps injuries that hampered him in the second half, Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman told reporters on Wednesday (link via Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic). He’s expected to be fully healthy for the start of Spring Training.

Friedman confirmed that Ohtani will return to a two-way role in 2027, as the four-time MVP suggested over the weekend. However, the front office leader declined to answer whether they believe Ohtani can sustain a full two-way workload for the entire season. He indicated the team hasn’t decided yet what kind of limitations Ohtani might face.

A physically hampered Ohtani was a liability for the Dodgers down the stretch and into the postseason. He missed a couple weeks in September due to the biceps issue and didn’t hit well while playing through the injury. Ohtani went nearly two months between his final regular season home run in mid-August and the three-run shot he hit in Game 4 of the NLCS, their eventual elimination game. He didn’t pitch after July 3 due to the left knee concern.

Ohtani was firing on all cylinders in the first half. He carried a.293/.403/.549 slash line with 22 home runs into the All-Star Break. He was also in the early-season Cy Young conversation with a 1.79 earned run average and 28% strikeout rate over his first 14 starts.

articles.title: A’s Considering Hiring GM Under Taylor Smith
body: The Athletics finalized the hiring of their new president of baseball operations, Taylor Smith, on Monday. At Smith’s introductory press conference, owner John Fisher suggested they could also hire a general manager to work as the #2 front office executive (link via Martín Gallegos of MLB.com).

That’s an increasingly common front office structure around MLB. The A’s had gone that route when Billy Beane and David Forst were the top two in the hierarchy. That changed at the end of the 2022 season when Beane transitioned to an advisory role and turned baseball operations autonomy to his longtime lieutenant. Forst ran the front office for three and a half seasons. Fisher made a change at the beginning of August when it became clear they were en route to a fifth straight losing season.

While many GM changes presage a move in the manager’s office, that’s not going to be the case with the A’s. In February 2025, the team signed Mark Kotsay to an extension that runs through the’28 campaign with a club option for’29. Smith expressed his excitement about working with the sixth-year skipper, saying Kotsay “seems like someone who is hungry for all the information (the front office) can get him, and I think it’ll be a great partnership.”

articles.title: Friedman: Dodgers Offseason “Business As Usual”
body: The Dodgers’ bid for a three-peat ended in decisive fashion, as they were swept by the Brewers one year after handing Milwaukee that same fate in the NLCS. As they turn their attention to 2027, president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman tells reporters (including Katie Woo of The Athletic) that this offseason will be “business as usual” from a financial perspective — at least pending the possibility for an overhaul to the sport’s economic structure in the next collective bargaining agreement.

No team has come close to the Dodgers’ spending in recent years. There’d been no real concern that they might slow down until reports emerged this summer that investments and loans made by insurance businesses owned by chairman Mark Walter were the subject of federal inquiries. Walter has sold off his interests in a few other sports franchises, most notably the Lakers. Dodgers CEO Stan Kasten said in no uncertain terms in August that Walter had no plans to sell the baseball franchise. Kasten also downplayed the idea that the non-baseball businesses could lead to a reduction in the team’s payroll, saying then that “the Dodgers stand on their own pretty well.”

Friedman’s comments strike the same chord. “We talked to Mark after we lost, and he was obviously really disappointed,” he told reporters on Wednesday. “But so much of his focus was on, OK, what can we do? What are our plans? What are our thoughts for the offseason? And our brains weren’t quite there yet, but so much of his focus was how do we put ourselves in the best position to win in’27?”

articles.title: Angels To Hire General Manager For 2027 Season
body: Angels interim general manager John Mozeliak informs Jeff Fletcher of the SoCal News Group that the club will be hiring a full-time general manager for the 2027 season, and that Mozeliak himself will not be that general manager. No one has been interviewed yet as the process is still in its early stages. Mozeliak will step aside when the new front office leader is hired, per Rhett Bollinger of MLB.com. “That is still to be determined, but I imagine I will help,” Mozeliak said when asked if he would be involved in the search, per Sam Blum of The Athletic.

In June, general manager Perry Minasian was fired, with Mozeliak taking over the front office as interim GM. Mozeliak had previously spent many years running the front office of the Cardinals. September brought the stunning news that longtime owner Arte Moreno would be selling the club to Stan Kroenke, owner of several other sports franchises, including the Los Angeles Rams of the NFL. That sale is expected to be finalized early in 2027.

The news of the sale came as the franchise was in transition in many ways. As mentioned, Mozeliak was running the front office on an interim basis. Kurt Suzuki managed the club in 2026 but on a one-year deal. At the deadline, the Angels made some future-focused moves but stopped short of a full rebuild. José Soriano and Jo Adell were flipped elsewhere but trade candidates Reid Detmers and Zach Neto stayed.

articles.title: Mitch Garver Retires
body: Catcher Mitch Garver has retired from playing, reports Ted Schwerzler of minnesotasportsfan.com. Garver played parts of ten major league seasons, suiting up for the Twins, Rangers and Mariners.

The Twins selected Garver in the ninth round of the 2013 draft out of the University of New Mexico. He hit well in the minors but there was skepticism about whether or not he had the defensive chops to stick at catcher. By the end of 2016, the Twins were optimistic enough that they gave him a 40-man roster spot to keep him out of the Rule 5 draft.

He made his debut in 2017 but didn’t hit much, slashing.196/.288/.348 with no home runs in 52 plate appearances. He showed more life the following season, hitting seven home runs and putting up a solid.268/.335/.414 line.

A true breakout arrived in 2019. Garver only played in 93 games and stepped to the plate just 359 times but that was still enough for him to launch 31 home runs as part of Minnesota’s “Bomba Squad”. That 2019 campaign is now famous for its juiced balls, with many home run records set across the league, but Garver’s huge.273/.365/.630 line was still 55% better than league average by measure of wRC+. Garver’s defense wasn’t lauded as highly as his offense, but considering catchers usually have lesser offensive production than other hitters, his big bat was a clear asset.

articles.title: Dalton Rushing To Undergo Elbow Surgery
body: Dodgers catcher Dalton Rushing will undergo elbow surgery today, reports Maddie Lee of the L.A. Times. He’s expected to undergo an internal brace procedure to repair the ulnar collateral ligament in his right elbow. That surgery would come with an approximate nine-month recovery window before Rushing can return to catching, though he’d be cleared to resume hitting well before that.

A nine-month window would see Rushing unable to catch until next July. Given Shohei Ohtani’s presence as the team’s designated hitter on days when he’s not pitching, that doesn’t leave Rushing with much of a path to playing time in the interim. Rushing has experience at first base and in left field, but it’s doubtful he’d be cleared to play either spot when he’s first given the green light to resume hitting.

Rushing, 26 in February, is the backup to Will Smith and also saw occasional time at first base and designated hitter in 2026. He first landed on the injured list due to a ligament tear in his elbow on the day of the trade deadline. He spent a month on the shelf before briefly returning, but he logged only eight hitless plate appearances through the remainder of the season and wasn’t on L.A.’s roster for either the National League Division Series or the National League Championship Series.

articles.title: Mariners Interested In Jason Kanzler For Managerial Vacancy
body: The Mariners are looking for a new manager after parting ways with Dan Wilson last month. A report from Patrick Mooney, Chandler Rome and Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic says that Jason Kanzler, Joe Espada and Rocco Baldelli are three of the candidates. Those aren’t the only three candidates in the mix but the report characterizes the search as being in an advanced stage. Espada and Baldelli have been connected to the job in previous reporting.

Kanzler, now 36, was drafted by the Twins in 2013. He topped out at the High-A level in 2015. He then became a teacher but also did some coaching in the Cape Cod League. Prior to the 2019 season, he got a job in the minor league system of the Astros as hitting coordinator. He got promoted to the big league staff for the 2022 campaign with the vague title of major league coach. He was made assistant hitting coach for the 2023 season. In January of 2024, the Cubs hired Kanzler as director of player development.

It would be a bit of an unorthodox move for the Mariners to pick Kanzler. He is quite young and doesn’t have a ton of experience, whereas Espada and Baldelli have both been managers before. Espada just wrapped up a three-year run in the Astros dugout. Baldelli managed the Twins from 2019 to 2025. The Dodgers hired him in December as a special assistant to president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman.

articles.title: Angels Decline 2027 Option On Manager Kurt Suzuki
body: Kurt Suzuki’s tenure as Angels’ skipper will last only one season. The team announced Wednesday that it has declined a 2027 club option on Suzuki and will commence a search for a new manager and coaching staff. Suzuki has been offered a role to remain with the organization as a special assistant, interim general manager John Mozeliak announced in a prepared statement.

“Kurt has earned tremendous respect in our clubhouse, and I’ve seen firsthand how much he cares about our players,” Mozeliak said in his statement within today’s release. “I do not believe our record this year was a true reflection of his abilities as a manager. I’m pleased we were able to offer Kurt a role to stay on as a special assistant, where his knowledge of our players and his perspective would continue to be valuable to the organization. I would also like to thank the entire coaching staff for their professionalism and hard work throughout a very difficult season. We value their expertise and have offered some members of the staff positions within the organization.”

articles.title: Yankees To Extend GM Brian Cashman
body: Yankees general manager Brian Cashman told reporters this morning that he’s agreed to a new contract. The final details aren’t official, but Cashman said the deal is in place.

With manager Aaron Boone also returning next season, the Yankees will run it back with both their on-field leader and their head man in the front office. New York earned the top AL Wild Card spot and cruised past Boston in the Wild Card round. The club was swept in the ALDS by the Rays, the eventual AL pennant winner.

Cashman is the longest-tenured front office leader in the game. He’s been the Yankees’ GM since 1998. His most recent contract ran from 2023 through this season. Given his longevity in the organization and the success over the years, a contract extension doesn’t come as much of a surprise. New York’s lack of interest in extensions is likely the main reason the deal didn’t come together until the conclusion of the previous contract.

The Yankees have been knocked out in the divisional round in each of the past two seasons. They’ve lost to the AL’s World Series representative both times. Owner Hal Steinbrenner did not place blame on Boone or Cashman for the team coming up short, instead citing a lack of offense. “I don’t think you can pin the season and the unacceptable end to it on Aaron [Boone],” Steinbrenner told reporters (h/t Greg Joyce of the New York Post). “I don’t think you can pin it on [Brian Cashman].”

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: San Diego Padres
body: The Padres find themselves in a familiar spot. They just wrapped another season that was good but not good enough. They have a decent roster but a huge chunk of the payroll is tied up in the core while the rotation has a number of holes.

Manny Machado, 3B: $280MM through 2033 (including $35MM of signing bonus still owed) Fernando Tatis Jr., IF/OF: $266MM through 2034 Xander Bogaerts, SS: $175MM through 2033 Jackson Merrill, OF: $135MM through 2034 (including $6MM of signing bonus still owed) Michael King, RHP: $66MM through 2028 (including $8MM of signing bonus still owed) Jake Cronenworth, IF/OF: $48MM through 2030 Joe Musgrove, RHP: $20MM through 2027 Yuki Matsui, LHP: $13.5MM through 2028 (Matsui may opt out after 2026 or 2027) Sung-Mun Song, IF: $12MM through 2029 (including remaining signing bonus and buyout on 2030 mutual option; can opt out after 2028) Wandy Peralta, LHP: $4.45MM player option for 2027 Option Decisions

Michael King, RHP: $28MM player option with $5MM buyout; deal also has $30MM player option for 2028 Nick Pivetta, RHP: $14MM club option (deal also includes $18MM player option for 2028) Yuki Matsui, LHP: may opt out of remaining two years and $13.5MM; can also opt out after 2027 Miguel Andujar, IF/OF: $8MM mutual option with $2.9MM buyout Lucas Giolito, RHP: $8MM mutual option with $1.5MM buyout Griffin Canning, RHP: $5MM mutual option with $1.8MM buyout Wandy Peralta, LHP: $4.45MM player option for 2027 Kyle Hart, LHP: $2.5MM club option with $200K buyout Additional Commitments

articles.title: Ben Sestanovich, Scott Sharp Candidates For Astros’ GM Job
body: Royals senior vice president Scott Sharp and Braves assistant general manager Ben Sestanovich are candidates for the Astros’ general manager position, reports Chandler Rome of The Athletic. They join a trio of known candidates whom Bob Nightengale of USA Today and Rome reported to be on the radar this afternoon: Matt Kleine, Josh Barfield and Randy Flores.

Sharp, 54, has spent the last two decades with Kansas City. He climbed to assistant general manager and eventually a senior vice president role under baseball operations president J.J. Picollo. He has worked in various facets of baseball operations with the Royals and frequently garnered attention from other teams for a role running a front office. Sharp has interviewed with at least the Mets, Giants and Rockies in recent years.

Sestanovich is a Harvard product who pitched for the Crimson in 2011. He worked in the Padres’ player development after graduation, then took an assistant GM role under Alex Anthopoulos with Atlanta in 2019. He’s one of five AGMs in the Braves’ front office.

Rome reported this afternoon that the Astros could have their GM hire in place before the end of the World Series. They’ll also need to settle on a new manager after moving on from Joe Espada at the end of the season.

In other hiring news, Rome reported that Houston is hiring Spencer Medick as their director of pitching. He’ll work in a non-uniform capacity to oversee the team’s pitching development. Medick had been the pitching coach for the Yankees’ Triple-A affiliate in Scranton/Wilkes-Barre.

articles.title: Astros Have Spoken To Josh Barfield, Randy Flores About GM Vacancy
body: The Astros’ general manager search has been underway for two months but could soon draw to a close. Chandler Rome of The Athletic reports that Houston could hire a new general manager before the completion of the World Series. Rome lists White Sox assistant general manager Josh Barfield, Cardinals assistant general manager Randy Flores and (as already reported earlier today) Brewers assistant general manager Matt Kleine as three candidates still in the running. That’s not necessarily an exhaustive list; Rome notes that in-house assistant GM Connor Huff has a particularly good relationship with owner Jim Crane, for instance.

Both Barfield, 43, and Flores, 51, are former big leaguers. Barfield was an infielder and fourth-round pick of the Padres. He debuted with San Diego in 2006 and had a big rookie showing but was unable to replicate that in parts of three subsequent seasons. He concluded his major league playing career with a.264/.295/.375 batting line in 1075 plate appearances.

Upon retiring, Barfield hooked on as a scout in the Diamondbacks organization. He held that role for several years before being elevated to Arizona’s assistant director of player development and, eventually, director of player development in 2019.

The White Sox hired Barfield as an assistant general manager in 2023, and he’s been in their front office since, helping to oversee the remarkable turnaround enjoyed by the South Siders in 2026. He’s had a hand in every facet of their baseball operations, ranging from player acquisition to scouting to player development and roster management.

articles.title: Aaron Boone To Return As Yankees’ Manager In 2027
body: The Yankees will be standing pat in the dugout, as the Bergen Record’s Pete Caldera reports that Aaron Boone will be returning for his tenth season as the team’s manager. Boone was already under contract for 2027, which will be the final season of the two-year, $10.5MM extension he signed in February 2025.

There wasn’t too much suspense about Boone’s job security, and it wouldn’t even be a surprise if the Yankees extended him again this offseason so he could avoid “lame-duck status” as a manager in the final year of his contract. Boone’s first contract with the team was a three-year deal with a club option for the 2021 season, and the Yankees let that deal fully run out before a new three-year pact with another club option year (for 2025) was signed in October 2021. New York exercised that 2025 option in the aftermath of the Yankees’ trip to the 2024 World Series, with Boone’s current deal coming soon afterwards.

Boone has a 790-565 record during his managerial tenure, with winning records in all nine seasons. The Bronx Bombers have won three AL East titles and made the playoffs eight times under Boone, with that 2024 pennant marking their deepest postseason run. Boone ranks seventh all-time in both wins and total games amongst Yankees managers.

articles.title: The Rangers’ Roster Bind
body: The Rangers should be at a crossroads offseason. Texas failed to take advantage of an historically weak division, finishing 80-82 to come up two wins short of a playoff berth. They missed the postseason for a third consecutive year and have been a league average team since their 2023 World Series. That’s a clear letdown for a team that has a lot of money tied up on players in their mid-late 30s.

According to Baseball Reference, Texas had the fifth-highest average age in MLB on both the position player (29.3) and pitching (30.3) sides. The Braves were the only other team in the top five in both areas. It’s an aging roster that hasn’t been good enough for three seasons, mostly struggling with the same inability to score runs.

Ownership has also hamstrung the front office recently. They’ve pulled back spending in the wake of the team’s collapsed local TV contract. Texas should’ve been motivated to add at the 2026 trade deadline with the AL West wide open. They instead declined to take on payroll and traded for a middle reliever (Chase Silseth) and a change of scenery third catcher (Logan O’Hoppe).

articles.title: Trade Candidate: Ketel Marte
body: Only Ketel Marte knows if he’s a truly a trade candidate or not, as the ball is in the second baseman’s court when it comes to approving a deal. Marte gained 10-and-5 status back in April, so after accumulating 10 years of MLB service time and spending the last five years with one team, the Diamondbacks second baseman now has full no-trade protection. Marte’s veto power over any potential trade adds yet another wrinkle to what has become an increasingly strained relationship between the D’Backs and the three-time All-Star.

The tension stems from Marte’s tendency to miss games without informing the team, which manager Torey Lovullo said in August has happened in each of the last four seasons. Reports of this situation first surfaced in August 2025, about a month after Marte was briefly placed on Arizona’s restricted list after the All-Star break, ostensibly to spend time dealing with the aftermath of a burglary at his home in the Dominican Republic. John Gambadoro of 98.7 Arizona Sports reported that Marte was actually on vacation in the D.R. and was willing to miss a couple of games after the break.

articles.title: Josh Bell Keeps Getting It Done
body: After spending his first five seasons in Pittsburgh, Josh Bell has played for six teams over the last half-dozen years. He’s been a frequent trade deadline mover since leaving the Pirates. He’ll never rank at the top of any free agent lists, but he’s come through with each new team.

The Twins signed Bell to a one-year, $7MM deal last winter. He was coming off a solid 22-homer season as the primary DH for the Nationals. Bell stepped into a similar role in Minnesota. He slashed.255/.319/.419 across 631 plate appearances. The switch-hitter drove in 96 runs, his highest mark since 2019. He ranked fifth in the American League in RBI.

Bell finished the 2026 campaign with a 106 wRC+. That’s exactly what he posted in 2025. He’s had a wRC+ between 102 and 106 in each of the past four seasons. The highs were certainly higher earlier in his career. Bell hit 37 homers and earned an All-Star nod in 2019. He won a Silver Slugger award at DH in 2022. But the consistency is admirable, especially in a market that hasn’t offered much reliability recently.

Aside from the offensive output, Bell has also been remarkably durable. He’s played 140+ games in every year of his career, excluding his 2016 rookie campaign (when he was promoted in July) and the shortened 2020 season. Bell hasn’t been on the injured list since 2021.

articles.title: Athletics Hire Taylor Smith As President Of Baseball Ops
body: The Athletics have a new lead executive. Taylor Smith is taking over as president of baseball operations, per a team announcement. Smith most recently served as an assistant general manager with the Red Sox.

After a wide-ranging search, the A’s have found a replacement for longtime general manager David Forst. The club moved on from Forst in August. Phillies exec Sam Fuld and Cubs assistant GM Jared Banner were in the running for the role. Fuld ended up staying in Philly, while Banner just took the Orioles’ general manager job. The A’s were also connected to former Astros GM James Click and former Nationals POBO Mike Rizzo. Smith’s colleague, fellow Boston AGM Mike Groopman, also received an interview.

The 31-year-old Smith emerged as the favorite for the gig late last week. Cardinals assistant GM Rob Cerfolio was also one of the finalists. A’s assistant GM Dan Feinstein finished out the season in place of Forst, but was not among the candidates for the full-time position.

“I couldn’t be more excited about Taylor as our president of baseball operations,” owner John Fisher said in a statement, relayed by Martin Gallegos of MLB.com. “He is one of the brightest minds in the game today. We conducted a very thorough search for our new baseball leadership, and Taylor stood out for his acute understanding of the game, especially in the areas of measuring player performance and player development.”

articles.title: What Went Wrong For Framber Valdez?
body: The Tigers handed Framber Valdez the third-largest deal among free-agent starters last winter. The lefty received a three-year, $115MM commitment. He was brought in to form an elite southpaw tandem with two-time reigning AL Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal.

Valdez’s debut campaign in Detroit didn’t go so well. His 4.03 ERA was his worst mark since becoming a full-time starter in 2020. Valdez had a career-low 17.8% strikeout rate, while his walk rate ticked up to its highest point since 2021. He was far from the only reason the Tigers fell short of the postseason, but he failed to provide much-needed stability to a rotation that needed another reliable workhorse.

The first red flag for Valdez is a 56.3% groundball rate. It’s more of a beige flag. That’s a tremendous number for just about anyone (league average was 44.1% in 2026), but it’s not what we’ve come to expect from the lefty. Valdez has coaxed grounders at a 61.5% clip for his career. The 56.3% mark in 2026 was his second-lowest as a big leaguer, behind only 2023. Valdez saw a bump in strikeouts that season, which adjusted his profile a bit.

Getting groundballs at a league-leading clip helps Valdez balance out his hard contact issues. He routinely ranks in the bottom 10th percentile in hard-hit rate and average exit velocity. Well-struck grounders aren’t going to do damage at nearly the level of line drives and fly balls. Valdez’s WHIP is typically higher than other aces, but his ERA tends to land in the low-to-mid 3.00s range with this approach.

articles.title: Yankees Had Past Interest In Jeremiah Estrada
body: As part of a piece about how the Yankees could rebuild their bullpen this offseason, the New York Post’s Joel Sherman writes that “the Yankees have long eyed” Padres right-hander Jeremiah Estrada. It isn’t specified when or even if the Yankees might’ve engaged San Diego in any trade talks about the reliever, though Estrada was reportedly discussed by the Big Apple’s other team when the Mets tried to line up a deal with the Padres last winter.

Estrada celebrates his 28th birthday in a couple of weeks, and the right-hander has now completed his third successful season out of the Friars’ bullpen. The 2026 campaign came with a lot of health issues, however, as Estrada was limited to 31 regular-season innings due to three trips to the injured list. Estrada missed time with elbow tendinitis, knee inflammation, and a shoulder impingement, and the last of those injuries ended his season in late August and kept him out of the Padres’ playoff run.

The impact of all these injuries could be measured in a bit of a dropoff in performance from Estrada’s 2024-25 seasons. The reliever had a 3.22 ERA/2.47 SIERA over 134 innings in those seasons, as well as a shaky nine percent walk rate but an elite 36.3% strikeout rate. In 2026, Estrada’s ERA and SIERA were both 3.48 ERA, his K% dropped to a still-excellent 30.2%, and his walks spiked upward to a 12.7% rate. His average fastball velocity also lost two miles, going from 97.9mph in 2025 to 95.9mph this year.

articles.title: Trade Candidate: Shea Langeliers
body: It’s a little difficult to gauge what the Athletics will do this winter since the team has yet to hire a full-time president of baseball operations or general manager since David Forst was let go back on August 7. Beyond this front office uncertainty, the expectation that the A’s will continue to trade players as they get too expensive shouldn’t be written in stone, given how the team has been (in the last two years) spending money to extend core players and splurge on Luis Severino’s free agent deal.

With all of this in mind, it wouldn’t be a shock to see Shea Langeliers in another team’s uniform on Opening Day. Langeliers is projected to earn an $8.7MM salary in his second of three arbitration years, and he is on pace to hit free agency after the 2028 campaign. The Athletics discussed an extension with Langeliers last spring but talks didn’t appear to go anywhere, and it’s also worth wondering if a Scott Boras client like Langeliers is simply more likely than not to forego an extension and test the open market.

The two remaining years of control over Langeliers give the A’s plenty of potential time to work out a new deal, and decrease the urgency to trade Langeliers now (rather than next winter or even at next summer’s trade deadline). Langeliers missed a little under seven weeks of the 2026 season due to a torn right meniscus and was used only as a DH once he returned in September, so this might not be the sell-high peak of Langeliers’ trade value if some teams prefer to see him catch again before committing to a big trade package.

articles.title: Ben Rortvedt Elects Free Agency
body: Catcher Ben Rortvedt has chosen to become a minor league free agent, according to his MLB.com profile page. This was the expected outcome after Rortvedt was outrighted off the Dodgers’ 40-man roster in September, as that outright assignment (without being selected again to the active roster) plus Rortvedt’s three-plus years of career MLB service time qualified him for minor league free agency.

Rortvedt earned a World Series ring for his 18 regular-season games and four playoff games with the 2025 Dodgers, and a rather circuitous route took him back to Los Angeles at this year’s trade deadline. A series of waiver claims saw Rortvedt go from the Dodgers to the Reds in November, back to the Dodgers in early February, then to the Mets in mid-February. New York designated Rortvedt for assignment prior to Opening Day and he accepted the outright to Triple-A, where the catcher played until the Dodgers re-acquired Rortvedt yet again on deadline day.

Injuries to both Will Smith and Dalton Rushing prompted L.A. to trade for both Rortvedt and another ex-Dodger in Hunter Feduccia at the deadline, in order to bolster the catching depth chart. Rortvedt ended up playing in 16 games for Los Angeles in August, posting the easy-to-remember batting line of.185/.185/.185 over 28 plate appearances.

articles.title: The Blue Jays’ Unexpected Deadline Sparkplug
body: The Blue Jays’ 5-1 loss to the Cardinals on August 2 dropped Toronto to 52-60, the kind of record that usually would’ve made a team a clear seller heading into the next day’s trade deadline. For the Jays, however, the situation wasn’t quite so simple. The Blue Jays came within two outs of winning the 2025 World Series and headed into 2026 still in full win-now mode, so the front office was loath to wave the white flag on the playoff race. And, despite their mediocre record, the Jays were still in the wild card hunt, 4.5 games back of the Guardians for the final AL wild card slot.

Toronto’s response was to both buy and sell at the deadline. Some controllable players (i.e. Jose Soriano, Spencer Arrighetti, Josh Smith) were added to help the team both make a push this season and for the future. Arrighetti was acquired from the Astros in a one-for-one swap for Daulton Varsho, who was one of several impending free agents the Jays sent elsewhere. Besides Varsho, the Blue Jays also parted ways with Jeff Hoffman and Kevin Gausman, with the latter sent to the Cubs for prospects Brett Bateman and Ty Southisene.

The wild card pursuit fell short, as the Blue Jays ended up 79-83 and in last place in the AL East. None of Soriano, Arrighetti, Smith, or rental pickup Jameson Taillon played well, but instead it was a much less-established name who ended up boosting the Jays’ lineup. Bateman had never played in a big league game prior to the trade, yet the rookie ended up hitting.329/.402/.424 with two homers in his first 181 plate appearances in a Blue Jays uniform.

articles.title: Poll: Does Paul Skenes Just Need To Fix His Changeup?
body: It’s obvious that Paul Skenes did not have the follow-up campaign one would have expected of a Cy Young winner. After holding opponents to a 1.97 ERA last year, that figure nearly doubled to 3.82 in 2026. Skenes still came out above average by strikeout rate (28.1%) and walk rate (6.9%), and ERA estimators like xERA (3.28) and SIERA (3.34) were a bit kinder to him than the surface-level ERA. For what it’s worth, FanGraphs valued Skenes at 4.2 wins above replacement, ranking 12th-highest among qualified starters this year. Nonetheless, it was a clear drop-off for Skenes by his lofty standards.

As MLBTR’s Charlie Wright wrote in August, Skenes’ stuff looked mostly the same this year. Apart from ditching his cutter, the righty’s four-seam fastball, splitter, sinker, slider, and changeup usage were all within 3.5% of their 2025 levels. The four-seamer remained his most common offering and averaged 96.8 mph – a 1.4 mph decrease from last year, but still well above league average. Curiously, the most drastic change in Skenes’ pitch mix was a sharp decline in the effectiveness of his changeup.

articles.title: Preller Discusses Ethan Salas, Padres’ Catchers
body: Highly touted prospect Ethan Salas made his major league debut for the Padres last month, batting.256/.275/.462 in a limited sample of 40 plate appearances. He remains a consensus Top 100 prospect in the sport and figures to play a prominent role behind the dish in 2027. Understandably, the 20-year-old Salas will still need to earn his playing time, as president of baseball operations A.J. Preller implied during the team’s end-of-season presser that Salas will be competing with Luis Campusano and Freddy Fermin.

“I don’t think anybody’s going to be guaranteed anything,” Preller told reporters, including the San Diego Union-Tribune’s Jeff Sanders. “I think it’s going to be, for Ethan, for example, a competition-type situation for him.” It’s unsurprising that Salas will still need to prove himself given Preller’s other remarks from the presser, in which he reiterated the Padres’ goal of competing for a championship in 2027.

Salas batted.296/.374/.448 in 404 plate appearances between Double-A and Triple-A this year. He managed the strike zone well, walking at an 11.6% clip and only striking out 14.3% of the time. It remains to be seen how those will translate in a longer run against major league pitching, but the hope is obviously that Salas can be an above-average hitter for years to come. The same is true of his defense, which MLB Pipeline and other evaluators consider advanced beyond Salas’ years.

articles.title: Phillies To Reduce J.T. Realmuto’s Catching Workload
body: J.T. Realmuto has long been one of the league’s most durable catchers, and that has continued into his mid-30s. He leads the Majors with 613 games started behind the plate since 2022. That includes 122 games started this year, which bests the Brewers’ William Contreras by one game for tops at the position. At the same time, Realmuto will turn 36 in Spring Training, and the Phillies may need to manage his workload more carefully after a down season in 2026. Speaking at the team’s year-end press conference on Thursday, president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski told reporters, including Cole Weintraub of NBC Sports Philadelphia, that Realmuto will not be catching as frequently in 2027.

“I said, ‘I don’t know if I can accomplish this, but I don’t want you to hear about it from the press conference,” Dombrowski said of his conversation with Realmuto. “’My goal is to try to reduce the number of games you catch.’” Per Dombrowski, Realmuto physically feels fine but is open to having more days off behind the plate, perhaps by slotting in more at first base.

articles.title: Yankees Have Shown Past Interest In Jacob Young
body: The Yankees have shown past interest in Nationals center fielder Jacob Young, writes Joel Sherman of The New York Post. It’s unclear whether the two sides engaged in formal talks or if it was just due diligence on the Yankees’ part, though the Nationals were known to be exploring a trade of Young back in January.

The 27-year-old Young just completed his fourth big league season. Since debuting for the Nats in 2023, he’s taken 1,477 trips to the plate and batted.248/.312/.339 with an 82 wRC+. Young doesn’t hit for power, having just 15 home runs and a.091 isolated slugging percentage in his career. Instead, he’s a speed and defense guy. Young has stolen 79 bases in 104 opportunities, good for a 76% success rate that’s right around league average.

He’s also accrued +22 Defensive Runs Saved and a staggering +49 Outs Above Average as a center fielder. The latter ranks second among center fielders with at least 1,000 innings since the start of 2023. The only player ahead of Young is the Cubs’ Pete Crow-Armstrong, who’s been worth +60 OAA.

This year showed a more well-rounded version of Young, albeit one who is still a below average hitter. In 471 plate appearances, he hit.252/.318/.390 with a 7.0% walk rate and a 16.6% strikeout rate. Young’s 95 wRC+ put him five points below league average production, but that’s still the best mark of his career. Statcast also credited him with 96th-percentile range as a center fielder, while DRS (-3) wasn’t as kind as in prior seasons, but still considered him passable.

articles.title: Pirates Re-Sign Kyler Fedko To Minors Deal
body: The Pirates have agreed to re-sign outfielder Kyler Fedko to a two-year minor league deal, per Colin Beazley of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. Fedko underwent knee surgery in August to repair a torn ACL, MCL, and LCL, so he’ll be rehabbing for a good portion of the 2027 season.

The 27-year-old Fedko debuted with the Twins this year after spending parts of six seasons working through the minor leagues. He spent about a month in the Majors starting in mid-June, appearing in 14 games and taking 19 trips to the plate. Fedko walked twice and got his first RBI on a sacrifice fly, though he did not record his first big league hit. The Twins optioned him to Triple-A St. Paul on July 10th. He batted.274/.362/.545 at that level with a 128 wRC+ until the aforementioned triple knee injury ended Fedko’s season in early August. Minnesota released him on September 1st, and the Pirates picked him up three days later.

The two-year deal gives Fedko some continuity as he continues his rehab. Meanwhile, the Pirates get a no-risk depth outfielder to stash in the minors for the 2028 season (late 2027 if Fedko progresses quickly). This year was Fedko’s second at the Triple-A level. In 2025, he took 187 plate appearances for St. Paul after being promoted from Double-A in August. He batted.268/.353/.476 with a 115 wRC+, striking out at around average rates and showing penchants for power, speed, and getting on base. The latter three remained on display this year. Fedko knocked 17 home runs, stole ten bases, and walked at an 11.1% clip in 75 games for St. Paul before the injury.

articles.title: Tigers Sign Nick Raquet To Minors Contract
body: The Tigers have signed left-hander Nick Raquet to a two-year minor league contract, according to 7 News’ Ari Alexander. Raquet became a free agent after he was released by the Orioles in early September.

The length of the deal reflects Raquet’s health situation, as Alexander reports that the southpaw recently underwent a Tommy John surgery. Raquet will therefore miss all of 2027 rehabbing from the procedure, so this two-year pact gives him some security to recuperate under a team’s umbrella, with the Tigers having an eye towards using Raquet when he’s healthy in 2028.

A third-round pick for the Nationals in the 2017 draft, Raquet stepped away from baseball entirely in 2020 once the minor league season was canceled by the pandemic. Raquet instead went back to college at William & Mary to complete a business degree, and even took a job as an enterprise risk consultant with Ernst & Young. He returned to play independent ball in 2023 and then signed a minors deal with the Cardinals prior to the 2024 season.

His two years in the St. Louis organization led to Raquet making his MLB debut in September 2025, as he tossed two scoreless innings over two appearances. The Cardinals designated Raquet for assignment last April and then dealt him to the Orioles, and the lefty had a 7.36 ERA over four games and 3 2/3 innings in a Baltimore uniform. Amidst the sporadic usage on the big league roster, Raquet spent most of his time at Triple-A Norfolk before his elbow problem both ended his season in August and led to this much longer absence.

articles.title: NL West Notes: Giants, Itoh, Taira, Vesia, Hernandez, R-Rod, Rockies
body: The Giants are among the big league teams who have scouted Hiromi Itoh and Kaima Taira, Susan Slusser of the San Francisco Chronicle reports. The Japanese right-handers are expected to be posted for MLB clubs this offseason, even though the impending lockout will sure interrupt their 45-day posting window unless a deal is reached between the time of posting (potentially early November) and the lockout-induced transactions freeze on December 1.

At least 15 MLB teams were thought to be scouting Taira and Itoh is also drawing plenty of interest, so it isn’t surprising to see the Giants on this list. Either righty would make a good fit on a Giants team in need of rotation help, and while Taira doesn’t have a long track record as a starter, he could conceivably transition to a role in San Francisco’s leaky bullpen if things didn’t work out as a starting pitcher. Despite the team’s increased NPB scouting presence, Slusser notes that “the Giants haven’t fared well in their pursuit of Japanese players in recent years,” with such targets as Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Roki Sasaki ending up with the arch-rival Dodgers.

articles.title: Five Players Elect Free Agency
body: Five more players who played in MLB this year have elected minor league free agency, according to the transaction tracker at MiLB.com. These players were all outrighted off teams’ 40-man rosters and have played seven-plus seasons in the minors, so the elections are mostly formalities.

The Mets acquired Bruján from Minnesota in a cash trade over the offseason. The out-of-options infielder failed to break camp and cleared waivers on Opening Day. New York called him up in early May while Francisco Lindor was injured. Bruján spent six weeks on the active roster but only started three games, going 1-11 in 13 plate appearances. The former top prospect batted.278/.385/.421 over 258 plate appearances with Triple-A Syracuse.

Mastrobuoni missed the first two months of the season due to a right calf strain. The Mariners waived him in June, called him up briefly in July, then sent him through waivers again. He batted.192 in 13 MLB games and hit.245/.338/.375 over 222 trips to the plate with Triple-A Tacoma.

Vázquez, a 27-year-old shortstop, spent virtually the entire season with Triple-A Norfolk. He had a mediocre.226/.271/.371 batting line in 52 games around a few injuries. Vázquez got a two-day stint on Baltimore’s big league roster in late August, making a lone appearance as a pinch-runner and scoring the game-winning run against the Cardinals.

articles.title: Poll: What’s Next For Tarik Skubal?
body: As the two-time defending World Series champions, the Dodgers were already considered juggernauts before they acquired superstar left-hander Tarik Skubal from the Tigers ahead of the Aug. 3 trade deadline. Although Skubal is unsigned past this season, the Dodgers parted with three prospects for the the back-to-back American League Cy Young winner in hopes he would make them borderline unbeatable in the playoffs.

With Skubal in tow, the Dodgers went on to finish with 100 wins, take the NL West for the fifth straight year and clinch a first-round bye in the postseason. Skubal helped the Dodgers dispatch the Braves in the NLDS, but their season and their bid to become the first National League team to win three World Series in a row came crashing down in the NLCS.

The small-market Brewers, whose cash payroll is almost $200MM lower than the deep-pocketed Dodgers’, outscored L.A. 21-11 en route to a four-game sweep. It wasn’t necessarily surprising that the Brewers won the series, as they entered the postseason off a major league-best 103-win campaign. In a pre-series poll, 59% of MLBTR readers picked the Brew Crew to prevail. However, it came as a shock that a Dodgers team with a star-studded lineup and rotation (Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow) didn’t put up a better fight.

articles.title: The Phillies’ Many Infield Questions
body: The Phillies reshuffled their infield at the trade deadline, moving three players to new positions to accommodate Luis Arraez. They kicked Bryson Stott over to third base, Alec Bohm across the diamond to first, and Bryce Harper to right field. Shortstop Trea Turner was the only constant on the dirt.

It was an overhaul for a two-month rental that unfortunately didn’t work out. Arraez’s numbers dropped in Philly and he suffered a left ankle sprain that kept him off the Wild Card Series roster. Philadelphia ended up moving Stott back to the keystone and playing Edmundo Sosa at third base in their first-round loss in Atlanta.

The group could look a lot different in 2027. Arraez, Bohm and Sosa will all hit free agency. President of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski said on Thursday he expected Harper to move back to the primary first base role, though he could see occasional outfield work (link via Todd Zolecki of MLB.com). Dombrowski added that the team hopes to use Kyle Schwarber a little more frequently at first base as well, which would allow skipper Don Mattingly to give Harper more semi-rest days at designated hitter.

Turner will remain the starting shortstop to start 2027 — though the Phils made it clear that’s not guaranteed to remain the case all season (link via The Associated Press). “From a defensive perspective, we were very clear. He knows he has to be better at shortstop,” Dombrowski said. “I told him it’s really mandatory that it’s like that. … You cannot play shortstop like you did defensively in’26 going to’27.”

articles.title: Taylor Smith In Lead For A’s GM Job?
body: The Athletics have been in the market for a new front office leader since they parted with longtime general manager David Forst on Aug. 7. The A’s have since identified several candidates to succeed Forst, but if they had their way, Phillies president of business operations Sam Fuld would have taken the reins. Fuld, a former A’s outfielder, rejected an offer to become their president of baseball operations last week.

While the Athletics haven’t hired anyone since Fuld turned them down, Red Sox senior vice president and assistant general manager Taylor Smith may be emerging as the frontrunner for the A’s GM position. The team is seemingly “focused on” Smith, Jon Heyman of the New York Post writes.

Smith, who interviewed with the A’s nearly a month ago, began his career as an analyst in the Rays’ research and development department in 2018. He rose to director of predictive modeling before the Red Sox poached him from their AL East rivals two years ago. Smith is now one of four AGMs in Boston, which also has Raquel Ferreira, Eddie Romero and Michael Groopman underneath chief baseball officer Craig Breslow.

articles.title: Tigers To Hire Martín Maldonado As Quality Control Coach
body: Former major league catcher Martín Maldonado has lined up his next job in baseball. Maldonado will serve as the Tigers’ quality control coach, Chandler Rome and Cody Stavenhagen of The Athletic report.

This will reunite Maldonado with Tigers manager A.J. Hinch and former teammate Framber Valdez. Maldonado played for the Hinch-led Astros for parts of the 2018 and’19 seasons, and he was with Valdez in Houston through 2023. As Rome and Stavenhagen note, Valdez has thrown more innings to Maldonado than any other backstop. Maldonado caught the left-hander for the Astros’ World Series-clinching victory over the Phillies in 2022 and was behind the plate for Valdez’s no-hitter in 2023. The Tigers brought in Valdez on a three-year, $115MM contract in free agency last winter, but he fell short of expectations with a 4.03 ERA and similar underlying numbers over 174 innings.

Maldonado, a defensive specialist who suited up for seven MLB teams and won a Gold Glove during his 15-year career, announced his retirement last October. The 40-year-old did not spend any time away from the game, though, as he served as a special assistant with the Braves this season. Maldonado will now take over a position that Billy Boyer previously held in Detroit. The Tigers created the opening last July when they shifted Boyer to third base coach to replace Joey Cora.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Atlanta Braves
body: The Braves won the NL East and defeated the Phillies in the wild card round before falling to the Dodgers in the NLDS. It was a nice return to form for the Braves after their injury-marred 76-86 season in 2025, but Atlanta will need to fill some roster holes and perhaps address some broader concerns in order to be championship contenders next year.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Chicago White Sox
body: The White Sox became the first team ever to follow three consecutive 100-loss seasons with a playoff berth. They knocked out the Astros for their first series win in two decades in the Wild Card Series. It was an excellent season relative to expectations, though they surely feel they squandered an opportunity by failing to close out the Guardians after taking a 2-0 lead in the ALDS. How aggressive are ownership and the front office going to be to supplement a talented position player core?

articles.title: Miguel Rojas Announces Retirement
body: Tonight marked the final game of Miguel Rojas’ career. The two-time World Series winner and 2025 postseason hero told reporters that he’s retiring after the Dodgers were eliminated by the Brewers on Thursday evening (link via Alden González of ESPN).

The news doesn’t come as a huge surprise. Rojas announced last fall that he intended to retire at the end of the’26 campaign. He later left open the possibility of sticking around for one more year but continued to maintain that retirement was the likeliest outcome. Rojas played the final four seasons of his career in Los Angeles and is expected to jump right into a player development role with the Dodgers — an agreement the sides reached when he re-signed on a $5.5MM free agent contract last December.

Rojas only played for the Dodgers and Marlins at the MLB level during a career that spanned parts of 13 seasons. He actually began his professional playing days with the Reds, however, signing with Cincinnati as an amateur out of Venezuela in 2006. Rojas played parts of seven seasons in the Reds’ system, making it to Triple-A before qualifying for minor league free agency. He signed a minor league deal with the Dodgers going into 2013 and reached the big leagues with L.A. one year later.

articles.title: Braves Select Brett Wisely
body: The Braves added infielder Brett Wisely to their 40-man roster, according to the MLB.com transaction tracker. Atlanta sent outfielder DaShawn Keirsey Jr. outright off the roster in a corresponding move, suggesting they quietly placed him on waivers this week. The tracker also indicates that Luke Williams officially elected free agency, a formality after he cleared outright waivers yesterday.

This is the second minor 40-man move that Atlanta has made since being eliminated from the postseason. As with last week’s decision to select reliever Danny Young, this is motivated by minor league free agency. Wisely is a 2019 draftee who has played parts of eight minor league seasons. Players with seven-plus years of minor league experience can elect free agency at the beginning of the offseason if they’re not on the 40-man.

Atlanta isn’t committing to carrying Wisely on the roster all winter. There’s a decent chance he’ll be pushed out by a bigger move at some point during the offseason. If he clears waivers, he’d have the right to elect free agency in that scenario. The Braves delay that by putting him on the 40-man for now, as they’d apparently rather let Keirsey hit the market to start the offseason.

articles.title: AL Central Notes: Caminero, Melton, White Sox, Holderman
body: The ALCS matchup between the Guardians and Rays has put the spotlight back on one of the most infamous trades in Cleveland baseball history — the November 2021 swap that sent Junior Caminero to Tampa Bay in exchange for right-hander Tobias Myers, who never threw a big league pitch in a Guards uniform. Myers was dealt to the Giants in July 2022, and Myers’ emergence as a quality reliever with the Brewers in 2024 was an added blow for the Guards, who “couldn’t believe they lost the trade twice,” according to The Athletic’s Zack Meisel and Will Sammon.

In their look back at how the seemingly minor Caminero-for-Myers swap developed, Meisel/Sammon noted that the Rays discussed Xzavion Curry and three other prospects (none of whom are still with the Guardians) before finally settling on Caminero. The future All-Star was then a lightly-regarded 18-year-old prospect who had signed with Cleveland out of the Dominican Republic in 2019. Rays scout Eduardo Sanchez was given particular credit for being high on Caminero’s attitude and maturity, and other Tampa evaluators liked what they saw in Caminero’s swing and hitting potential. The end result was a steal for the Rays, and the Guardians can only hope that this trade doesn’t continue to haunt them by swinging a pennant in Tampa’s direction.
As the Guardians take a 2-1 lead in the ALCS, here’s more from around the AL Central…

articles.title: Preller, Stammen Discuss Padres’ Offseason, Rotation, Injuries
body: Padres president of baseball operations A.J. Preller and manager Craig Stammen held an end-of-season wrap-up session yesterday, with the San Diego Union-Tribune’s Kevin Acee, MLB.com’s AJ Cassavell, and The Athletic’s Dennis Lin among the reporters on the video call. As has been the case during most of Preller’s tenure, he reiterated that the organization is committed to delivering “a championship product to the city of San Diego,” and taking the “few more steps we need to take” in winning the Padres’ first World Series.

Beyond adding the final touches to the 91-win roster, however, the Padres first need to figure out how to keep some of that core intact, given how many key contributors are slated for free agency. In particular, most of the starting rotation — Michael King (if he opts out as expected), Robbie Ray, Casey Mize, Walker Buehler — is hitting the open market, plus Nick Pivetta could join this group if the Padres decline their $14MM club option on Pivetta’s services.

Exercising that option would be a logical move for a team in such need of starting pitching, though Pivetta logged only 42 1/3 total innings in the 2026 regular season and playoffs due to a flexor strain that sidelined him for the majority of the year. The extended nature of the injury altered Pivetta’s contract, turning his $14MM player option for 2027 into a club option for the Padres.

articles.title: Rockies Fire Pitching Coach Alon Leichman
body: The Rockies have parted ways with pitching coach Alon Leichman, according to The Athletic’s Ken Rosenthal and Keith Law. Leichman held the position for just one season, as the Rox only hired the 37-year-old last December.

On paper, the quick hook isn’t necessarily a surprise given that Colorado’s pitching staff finished last in baseball in ERA (5.59), SIERA (4.58), strikeout rate (17.5%), WHIP (1.52), and opponents’ batting average (.283), plus last or close to last in multiple other categories. As is the case with any coaching firing, however, it is fair to wonder how much of the blame can be played on a coach for the shortcomings of a roster that was clearly lacking in pitching talent. In the Rockies’ case specifically, the team has spent its entire history trying to figure out how to develop and maintain quality pitching in the thin air of Coors Field.

Nobody expected Leichman to turn this around in a single year, but president of baseball operations Paul DePodesta may have planted some hints about the firing when speaking to reporters last week. The starters’ pre-game preparation under Leichman may have been an issue, as DePodesta pointed specifically to the fact that Colorado’s “run differential was worse in innings one and two than innings three and beyond combined. There were way too many games where we just got into a hole within the first two innings.”

articles.title: Reds Avoid Arbitration With Oswaldo Cabrera
body: The Reds announced that they have agreed to a one-year, Major League contract with utilityman Oswaldo Cabrera. The signing allows the two sides to avoid salary arbitration, and MLB.com’s Mark Sheldon reports that Cabrera will earn $1MM in guaranteed salary plus up to $200K in bonuses related to plate appearances.

There was some thought that Cabrera could be a non-tender candidate given his lack of career production at the big league level. However, the Reds only added Cabrera to the organization on a waiver claim on September 18, so Cincinnati might’ve always had an eye towards retaining the 27-year-old heading into the offseason. Cabrera’s modest salary is an easy fit even in the Reds’ limited budget, and the team now has some experienced depth in place.

As a rookie with the Yankees in 2022, Cabrera hit.247/.312/.429 in his first 171 plate appearances as a big leaguer, good for a 110 wRC+. This remains the high point of his offensive production, as Cabrera has since batted.230/.289/.326 over 803 PA with New York and Cincinnati. Working as a part-time bench piece in the Bronx, Cabrera’s career was interrupted in May 2025 by an ugly ankle injury that required a season-ending surgery. He made it back for the start of the 2026 minor league season and hit.288/.345/.444 over 524 PA for Scranton/Wilkes-Barre, and Cabrera also made it into seven total MLB games with the Yankees and Reds.

articles.title: Two Players Elect Minor League Free Agency
body: A pair of players from NL East teams have elected minor league free agency, according to the MiLB.com transactions page. The details…

Henry played in 20 games with the Marlins in 2021-22, which remains the catcher’s only on-field action in the majors. The 2026 season saw Henry return to a big league roster but without any in-game action, as the Phillies selected his minor league contract in July but then optioned him back to Triple-A four days later. The 29-year-old backstop is a journeyman who has played for five different organizations during his pro career, with two separate stints for the Brewers (his original club) and the Phillies. Henry has a respectable.253/.324/.402 slash line over 1121 career plate appearances at the Triple-A level, and he hit.186/.314/.209 over his 51 Major League PA for Miami.

articles.title: Phillies Re-Sign Tim Mayza, Hire Carlos Mendoza As Third Base Coach
body: 10:50am: Mayza will earn $2.75MM next season, according to Gelb. That’s a raise over the $1.75MM salary he collected this year.

9:38am: The Phillies made a couple of notable moves on Thursday morning, president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski announced. In addition to re-signing left-handed reliever Tim Mayza to a one-year deal, the Phillies hired former Mets manager Carlos Mendoza as their third base and infield coach (via Matt Gelb of The Athletic).

Mayza debuted with the Blue Jays in 2017 and was a regular in their bullpen until they released him in July 2024. After brief runs with the Yankees and Pirates, he joined the Phillies off waivers from Pittsburgh in August 2025. Mayza only threw 7 1/3 innings with the Phillies last year, but they brought him back on a minor league pact. The 34-year-old ended up earning a spot in their Opening Day relief corps and enjoying one of the most productive seasons of his career.

articles.title: Phillies Reached Out To Chase Utley, Raul Ibanez In Managerial Search
body: The Phillies put an end to their managerial search when they promoted interim skipper Don Mattingly to the full-time role on Wednesday. They showed interest in ex-Red Sox manager Alex Cora during the process, but he wasn’t the only outside candidate on their radar. President of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski formally requested permission to contact Dodgers employees Chase Utley and Raul Ibanez about the job, Jayson Stark of The Athletic reports. The two former Phillies “politely declined,” according to Stark.

Utley, who is in his first year as a special assistant to Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman, ranks as one of the greatest Phillies of all-time. During a run that lasted from 2003-15, the former second baseman racked up 62.0 bWAR – trailing only legendary third baseman Mike Schmidt among Phillies hitters – and earned six All-Star nods. Utley also helped lead the Phillies to a pair of National League pennants and a World Series title (2008). He spent the last three-plus years of his career with the Dodgers, who acquired him in a 2015 swap, and became a Phillies Wall of Fame member this August.

Asked about the Phillies’ interest in reuniting with him as a manager, the 47-year-old Utley told Stark: “Regardless if that (Phillies report) is true or not … considering where I’m currently at with my family, that commitment (to a job like managing) is not really realistic at the moment.”

articles.title: Phillies Sign Don Mattingly To Two-Year Deal
body: Don Mattingly is the Phillies “interim” manager no more, as the team announced today that he’ll shed that interim label and be named the new full-time skipper. President of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski said in a press release that Mattingly has signed a two-year deal covering the 2027-28 seasons.

Mattingly relieved former manager Rob Thomson near the end of April. Philadelphia was 10 games under.500 when the club parted with Thomson. Mattingly led the team to a Wild Card berth. The Phillies went 79-55 after he took over.

There were rumblings last week that Mattingly could stick as manager after the Phillies were denied again by Alex Cora. He’d been their first choice to replace Thomson after being fired by the Red Sox in April. Cora said no at the time and maintained that he didn’t want the gig when pursued after the season ended. He’s reportedly not interested in managing at all next season and instead plans to take the downtime with his family.

Mattingly was going to be with the Phillies in some fashion for 2027. He signed a two-year deal to be the bench coach heading into this season. The Athletic’s Matt Gelb and Jayson Stark had previously reported that Mattingly could move to a front-office advisor position if he wasn’t given the manager gig. He’d be working closely with his son, Preston, who has been the Phillies’ general manager since 2024.

articles.title: Braves Outright Luke Williams
body: The Braves sent utility player Luke Williams through outright waivers, according to the MLB.com transaction log. Atlanta designated him for assignment last week when they added Danny Young to the roster to keep him out of minor league free agency this offseason.

Williams hasn’t technically elected free agency, according to the tracker, but it’s a formality that he’ll do so. He has played more than seven seasons in the minors and would hit the market as a minor league free agent either way. There’s a decent chance it’s a precursor to another non-roster contract with Atlanta, with whom Williams has spent the past three seasons.

The Braves kept the 30-year-old in the minors for virtually the entire season. He was on the big league roster for two days in April while Michael Harris II was on paternity leave. Williams hit just.218/.311/.367 across 363 plate appearances with Triple-A Gwinnett. He stole 37 bases in 40 tries, however, so the Braves added him to their Wild Card Series roster in case they needed a pinch-runner. The situation never came up against the Phillies, and Atlanta swapped him out for the five-game Division Series when they went from 11 to 13 pitchers.

articles.title: White Sox To Pursue Starting Pitching
body: White Sox general manager Chris Getz spoke with members of the media today, including James Fegan of the Chicago Sun Times, after the club was recently eliminated by the Guardians. Looking ahead to 2027, Getz said the Sox will pursue starting pitching this offseason.

It’s not a surprising declaration. Though the Sox had a good season, the rotation was not a strength. The club’s starters logged a total of 674 2/3 innings, the fewest of the 30 teams in the league. Their 4.60 earned run average was better than just four other clubs. Chicago deployed a pitching chaos strategy in the postseason, with few traditional starts.

The use of openers clouds those splits a bit but the general overview lines up with a deeper dive. Sean Burke, Davis Martin, Anthony Kay and Erick Fedde were the club’s biggest innings eaters this year. Fedde is headed to free agency. Kay had a serviceable 4.44 ERA with a subpar 18.2% strikeout rate. Martin had a 3.95 ERA but in uneven fashion. His ERA was at 2.00 through the end of May but was 5.63 after that. Burke was similar but less extreme. He had a 2.99 ERA through his start on August 11 but a 4.66 ERA in his final seven outings.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Detroit Tigers
body: The Tigers never recovered from an atrocious May. They wound up dealing the two-time defending Cy Young winner at the deadline but didn’t orchestrate any kind of rebuild. They’ll look to reload this offseason and improve upon a 76-86 finish, yet it’s going to take a lot of work on the pitching staff and some shuffling in the bottom half of the lineup.

articles.title: Phillies Not Retaining Kevin Long, Bobby Dickerson
body: 7:00pm: Matt Gelb of The Athletic confirmed the coaching decisions. His report notes that Long was signed through 2028 as part of an extension he signed after 2025. Gelb reports that Long is expected to get interest from several other clubs. He floats the Mets as a possibility, noting that Long has a good relationship with Juan Soto from their time together with the Nationals.

There will also be a change at third base coach. When Mattingly took over for Thomson, third base coach Dusty Wathan replaced Mattingly as bench coach. Anthony Contreras was called up from his role as Triple-A manager to be the new third base coach. Contreras will stay with the team but in a different role, per Gelb.
6:30pm: The Phillies will be moving on from hitting coach Kevin Long and infield coach Bobby Dickerson, reports Jim Salisbury of NBC Sports Philadelphia.

Long, 59, was hired as the club’s hitting coach going into the 2022 season. He previously held that title with the Yankees, Mets and Nationals. His first season in Washington, 2018, was Bryce Harper’s last before hitting free agency and signing with Philadelphia. The Phils were rebuilding at that time, missing the playoffs in each season from 2012 to 2021. In that latter campaign, the team-wide batting line was.240/.318/.408, leading to a 94 wRC+.

The first season under Long was a success. The Phils hit.253/.317/.422 in 2022 for a wRC+ of 107. They made a run to the World Series, though they lost to the Astros. After that one year in Philadelphia, Long was signed to an extension of unknown length.

articles.title: Twins Hire Brian Reith As Pitching Coach
body: The Twins announced Wednesday that they’ve named Brian Reith their new pitching coach, replacing Pete Maki, whose contract wasn’t renewed at season’s end. Reith has spent the past five seasons as the pitching coach with the Rays’ Triple-A affiliate in Durham, and he pitched in parts of three major league seasons with the Reds from 2001-04. Minnesota also elevated Ben Myers, who’s been on the training staff with their top affiliate in St. Paul, to the major league staff as an assistant athletic trainer.

Before his half-decade run in Durham, Reith coached in the low levels of Tampa Bay’s system. The 48-year-old was a sixth-round pick by the Yankees back in 1996 but was traded to the Reds four years later as part of the trade that brought two-time All-Star pitcher Denny Neagle to the Bronx. Reith wound up pitching 127 2/3 innings with the Reds across parts of three seasons.

Although Reith never found much success in the majors as a pitcher, he comes to the Twins from one of the game’s most highly regarded organizations in terms of player development. Reith has actually coached three pitchers on the Twins’ 40-man roster — Taj Bradley, Eric Orze and (more briefly) Joe Ryan — during that trio’s time in the Rays system.

articles.title: Will The Cardinals Trade A Catcher This Offseason?
body: The Cardinals’ catching depth has intrigued other teams for over a calendar year. Although St. Louis has yet to trade from that area of organizational strength, that’ll again surely be a point of discussion for the front office.

St. Louis has four catchers on the 40-man roster: Leo Bernal, Iván Herrera, Jimmy Crooks and Pedro Pagés. Top prospect Rainiel Rodriguez won’t need an offseason roster spot but has mashed his way to Double-A. There’s a chance he earns an MLB look next season at age 20. He’ll at the very least play his way to Triple-A and be on the radar for a 2028 promotion.

If Rodriguez were to make his debut next season, he’d likely be the second rookie catcher on the active roster. Bernal, who turns 23 in February, figures to break camp for the first time in his career. The Cardinals brought up the Panama native with September roster expansion. Bernal started 22 of the final 24 games, drawing 15 assignments behind the plate with seven more between first base and designated hitter. He made a strong first impression, batting.284 with five homers. Bernal scuffled a bit defensively, committing six errors, but most scouting reports feel he’ll be serviceable behind the plate.

articles.title: Diamondbacks Pursued Luis García Jr. At Trade Deadline
body: The Nationals were shopping first baseman Luis García Jr. at the deadline and eventually traded him to the Yankees. Joel Sherman of The New York Post reports that the Diamondbacks were the runners-up for García. Sherman then speculates about the Yankees now dealing García to Arizona for a reliever such as Juan Morillo.

It’s not surprising that the Diamondbacks were involved. They were in the Wild Card race in the National League but were getting subpar production from both the first base position and the designated hitter spot. But in the end, they got outfielder Lars Nootbaar and didn’t properly address those two spots. The Yanks needed a lineup jolt with both Aaron Judge and Giancarlo Stanton on the injured list. They sent Yovanny Cruz, Jake Bird, Jack Cebert and Ben Grable to Washington to seal the deal.

Arizona continued to get limp production from first base and DH and just missed the playoffs. Those spots are still wide open going into 2027 and stand out as clear areas for the Snakes to improve before next season. Pavin Smith, Adrian Del Castillo, Tyler Locklear and Tim Tawa are still on the roster but no one in that group looks like a clear answer.

Smith has had some success in the past but he hit.183/.262/.294 in 2026. He made $2.25MM and will be due a modest raise in arbitration. The club may decide not to tender him a contract. Del Castillo hit.193/.246/.309 this year. Locklear hit well in 2026 but in a tiny sample of 15 games. His career line in the majors is.190/.275/.310. Tawa had a respectable season but should be bouncing around the diamond as a utility guy.

articles.title: Cardinals Open To Short-Term Addition At Third Base
body: The Cardinals enter the offseason with set names at several spots around the diamond. Masyn Winn and JJ Wetherholt have the middle infield covered. Alec Burleson is locked in at first base. Jordan Walker will reprise his role in right field. They’re deep in catching talent with each of Leo Bernal, Pedro Pagés and Iván Herrera on the roster — to say nothing of top prospect Rainiel Rodriguez. Granted, Herrera is more of a DH option at this point, but he has enough bat to take regular reps there. Joshua Báez will probably get another look in left field, even with his strikeout troubles, after he hit a combined 41 homers between Triple-A and the majors.

Third base is very much up in the air, however. Nolan Gorman was the most frequent option at the hot corner this season but has yet to establish himself in the majors thanks to his own swing-and-miss tendencies. He’s only in line for a small raise in arbitration, but he’s a clear non-tender or change-of-scenery trade candidate. The Gorman question looms as the Cardinals consider their offseason trajectory, but Derrick Goold of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch reports that the Cards are open to bringing in a short-term solution at the hot corner to help bridge the gap to prospect Jesús Báez.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Arizona Diamondbacks
body: The D-Backs were in Wild Card contention until the final game of the season, but they ultimately fell short of a playoff berth for a third straight year. They’re probably working with a tighter budget this winter and have a handful of glaring needs on the pitching staff and in the back half of the lineup.

articles.title: Derek Law Elects Free Agency
body: Veteran reliever Derek Law is a free agent, per his MiLB.com transaction tracker. The Diamondbacks designated the right-hander for assignment in mid-September. He passed through waivers and was outrighted to Triple-A. Law is now back on the open market.

Arizona added Law on a minor league deal in January. He was recovering from flexor tendon surgery at the time and wasn’t ready for the start of the regular season. A setback during his rehab assignment pushed Law’s Diamondbacks debut to late August. He allowed a run in his first outing with the club, then ripped off six scoreless appearances.

The 36-year-old Law doesn’t miss many bats, but he throws strikes and keeps the ball in the yard. The righty put together 90 innings of a 2.60 ERA with the Nationals in 2024. He was set to be a key member of the bullpen last season until arm injuries ruined his campaign.

While Law did a nice job keeping runs off the board with Arizona, his velocity was noticeably down. He sat at a career-low 93.2 mph with his fastball. The heater averaged 95.1 mph with Washington. Law’s cutter, typically his primary pitch, was also down about two ticks.

The Diamondbacks were hit hard by injuries in the bullpen. Closer Justin Martinez was sidelined until mid-August. Lefties A.J. Puk and Andrew Saalfrank missed the entire season. Fill-in closer Paul Sewald was DFAed after allowing a dozen homers in 39 innings.

articles.title: The Tigers’ Under-The-Radar Option Decision
body: Option decisions are among the first pieces of offseason business. Any club and player option provisions must be decided upon within five days of the end of the World Series. The vast majority of those will be formalities, obvious decisions in either direction based on the player’s walk year performance. That said, every year brings a handful of borderline calls.

The Tigers have two upcoming club option decisions — both on pitchers who’d be due eight-figure salaries. Kenley Jansen is a future Hall of Fame closer; Drew Anderson is a journeyman who pitched in Japan and Korea during a five-year odyssey between MLB stints. Detroit has a net $10MM call on both pitchers. Despite their wildly different career arcs, it’s Anderson who stands a better chance of getting a second season in Detroit.

Anderson signed a one-year, $7MM contract last December. The deal included a $10MM option for next season with no buyout. Anderson initially expected to compete for a rotation spot but was pushed to long relief by the subsequent Framber Valdez and Justin Verlander signings. He got out to a spotty start and never really pitched his way into a late inning role. Anderson got a handful of high-leverage assignments but also mixed in a decent amount of mop-up work.

body: In perhaps the most underwhelming division race in history, the Astros won the AL West with an 81-81 record, while the Rangers finished a game (and a head-to-head tiebreaker) behind at 80-82. While technically not far away from being a playoff team, Texas clearly still has a lot of holes to fill in order to become more than a quasi-contender, and it remains to be seen how much money is available to address those needs.
