articles.title: Reviewing The Rays, Angels, And Reds Three-Team Trade
body: The three-team deal that sent Josh Lowe to the Angels and Gavin Lux to the Rays over the winter was intriguing, if not season-altering. Los Angeles picked up an everyday outfielder to replace Taylor Ward, who was traded to the Orioles. Tampa Bay landed a Brandon Lowe replacement after sending the second baseman to Pittsburgh.

And then there’s Cincinnati. The Reds got off the $5.525MM owed to Lux in his final year of arbitration. They also picked up reliever Brock Burke from the Angels. It seemed like a fine bit of business, but not a move that would have a major impact on the season. The trade turned out to be a big win for Cincinnati, and pretty convincingly so.

Burke had a decent run with the Rangers after moving to the bullpen in 2022. He struggled in 2024 and was designated for assignment midway through the year. The Angels picked him up for the final six weeks of the season. Burke made the club in 2025 and put up a solid 3.36 ERA over 69 games. He had a year of team control remaining when he was sent to Cincinnati.

The 30-year-old Burke was tremendous in his lone season with the Reds. He delivered a 2.30 ERA across 74 1/3 innings. Burke’s 77 appearances led the National League. He was the club’s top left-handed option with Caleb Ferguson opening the year on the IL, and manager Terry Francona leaned on him early and often.

articles.title: Marlins To Name Dillon Lawson Hitting Coach
body: The Marlins have settled on former Yankees hitting coach and former Red Sox assistant hitting coach Dillon Lawson as their next hitting coach, reports Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald. Lawson joined the Marlins organization as a roving hitting coach this past summer, following his April dismissal in Boston.

Miami moved on from hitting coach Pedro Guerrero following the season after its offense turned in a middle-of-the-pack performance. There were some obvious breakouts — Otto Lopez, Liam Hicks, Javier Sanoja — but several young Marlins hitters trended the wrong direction. Kyle Stowers and Jakob Marsee saw their offensive output take a step back, though injuries probably contributed to both (to an extent). Young hitters like Owen Caissie, Agustin Ramirez, Joe Mack and Connor Norby all hit at below-average levels; Norby wound up being traded to the Rockies prior to the deadline and saw his bat take off in his new environs. (Hicks, traded to the Rays at the deadline, hit well with both clubs).

Marlins hitters posted a collective.249/.326/.400 batting line this season — effectively right in line with the league-average.244/.318/.400. The team ranked 18th in runs scored (715), seventh in batting average, tied for fifth in on-base percentage and tied for 16th in slugging percentage. Their 9% walk rate ranked 13th, while their 21.8% strikeout rate tied for 14th. Those marks, again, were right in line with the respective league averages of 8.9% and 22.1%.

articles.title: Alex Anthopoulos Discusses Braves’ Free Agents, Rotation, Profar
body: The NL East champion Braves saw their season ended on Wednesday when the Dodgers eliminated Atlanta from the NLDS in four games. The team’s wrap-up press conference took place today, as Braves president of baseball operations Alex Anthopoulos met with the media (including the Athletic’s Jesus Cano and MLB.com’s Mark Bowman) to touch on several topics.

Reuniting with some impending free agents is a possibility, with Anthopoulos saying that the team will speak with all of its free agents before the market officially opens five days after the World Series. Anthopoulos praised the work of Tyler Mahle and Mauricio Dubon in particular, and the PBO noted that he is “very comfortable with” Dubon as a shortstop.

This is notable given that shortstop is perhaps Atlanta’s most glaring area of need, as both Dubon and Ha-Seong Kim are free agents. Kim is unlikely to be re-signed given his extreme struggles in 2026, but Dubon (acquired in a trade with the Astros last November) ended up appearing in 153 games for the Braves, hitting.276/.321/.399 with 12 home runs over 619 plate appearances.

articles.title: Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Undergoes Laser Eye Surgery
body: Blue Jays first baseman Vladimir Guerrero Jr. recently underwent laser eye surgery, as announced on Instagram by the Laser Eye Center of Miami and confirmed by Sportsnet’s Ben Nicholson-Smith. It’s unclear exactly when the surgery occurred, as the Center’s post was made during a post-op visit, though in any case it shouldn’t affect Guerrero’s offseason work.

The 27-year-old Guerrero had a trying season this year, the first of his 14-year, $500MM extension which he signed in April 2025. In 144 games, Guerrero batted.260/.332/.356 with just nine home runs and a 95 wRC+, putting him a few points below league average. The most concerning trend was the drop in his power. Guerrero’s.356 slugging percentage and.096 ISO were both career lows. His hard-hit rate fell from 50.7% in 2025 to a (still above-average) 44.3% in 2026. The same was true of Guerrero’s average exit velocity, which sat at 92.0 mph last year and declined to 90.3 mph this year.

articles.title: AL Central Notes: Vargas, Tigers Staff, Royals Ballpark
body: White Sox third baseman Miguel Vargas has been a major part of the club’s turnaround this season. The former top prospect, along with newcomer Munetaka Murakami, fueled an offense that ranked fifth in scoring during the regular season. Vargas has set career highs in virtually every offensive category.

The breakthrough season almost didn’t happen. Vargas told Scott Merkin of MLB.com this week that he considered leaving baseball after the 2024 campaign. It’s a topic he touched on earlier this season, but he expanded on it in the recent interview with MLB.com.
“I got to the last couple of weeks of that year, I sit with my dad and we actually … it wasn’t the first time talking about not playing,” Vargas said. “It’s just a hard moment.”

Vargas was dealt from the Dodgers to the White Sox at the 2024 trade deadline. He never found his footing in Los Angeles. Vargas hit just.104 in 42 games with Chicago to close the year. He compiled 237 plate appearances of a brutal 47 wRC+ between the two teams.

“It was so easy to stop playing, but I don’t have an answer to what I wanted to do,” Vargas said. “This is what I have done my whole life. I don’t know how to do anything else. So, I think that was the scary part. This is what I’ve done my whole life. This is what I want to continue to do.”

The 2025 season was a step forward. Vargas notched a respectable.717 OPS as an everyday player for the first time. He took a leap this year, launching 33 home runs and driving in 106. Vargas ranked 16th among all qualified hitters with a 134 wRC+. He even chipped in 22 stolen bases.

articles.title: Sam Fuld Declines Offer To Become A’s President Of Baseball Operations
body: Phillies president of business operations Sam Fuld has declined the Athletics’ offer to become the team’s new president of baseball operations, ESPN’s Jeff Passan reports. Fuld’s name surfaced in connection to the A’s job earlier this week, but Fuld has now taken himself out of the running and will stay in Philadelphia.

Nine names have been linked to the A’s job, though Passan (in another post) echoes an earlier report from The Athletic’s Patrick Mooney and Ken Rosenthal stating that Cardinals assistant general manager Rob Cerfolio is expected to stay in St. Louis rather than pursue the top job in Sacramento. Passan describes both Cerfolio and Red Sox assistant GM Taylor Smith as finalists in the search, and it is unclear how many other names were on the Athletics’ short list besides Fuld.

Fuld spent the last of his eight Major League seasons with the Athletics in 2015, and after retiring from playing in 2017, he joined the Phillies organization in November 2017. Beginning as a player information coordinator, Fuld served in that role until he was promoted to the role of general manager in December 2020. This put Fuld behind only PBO Dave Dombrowski on the Phils’ decision-making depth chart, though an interesting twist occurred in 2024 when Fuld took a leave of absence to pursue an MBA at Wharton. Fuld returned as Philadelphia’s president of business operations this year after attaining his degree, and Preston Mattingly has been the GM under Dombrowski over the last two years.

articles.title: Diamondbacks To Retain Hitting Coach Joe Mather
body: There were questions about manager Torey Lovullo’s future after the Diamondbacks’ season ended, but they put those to bed when they gave him a two-year deal on Oct. 1. While the D-backs parted with pitching coach Brian Kaplan five days later, Lovullo’s staff will have the same hitting coach in 2027. Joe Mather will return for a sixth season, John Gambadoro of Arizona Sports reports (via Alex Weiner of Arizona Sports).

Mather, a former outfielder who played in the majors from 2008-12, became a minor league coach for the Diamondbacks in 2015. He left the organization to become the Reds’ assistant hitting coach ahead of the 2020 season. After two years in Cincinnati, he returned to Arizona in his current position. Although the Diamondbacks have only made the playoffs once since then (their NL pennant-winning season in 2023), they have scored the majors’ fifth-most runs during Mather’s tenure.

articles.title: Corey Seager Undergoes Elbow Surgery
body: Rangers president of baseball operations Chris Young told reporters last week that shortstop Corey Seager was dealing with a bone spur in his right elbow. Minor surgery was on the table, and it appears Seager went that route. Jeff Wilson of DLLS Sports first pointed out an Instagram post from Seager’s wife, Madisyn, mentioning the procedure. Kennedi Landry of MLB.com, among others, has since reported the surgery happened on Tuesday.

It’s unclear exactly how long Seager was playing through the elbow injury, though Young mentioned it was multiple months. Seager had two separate IL stints for back inflammation and also spent time on the seven-day concussion IL. He didn’t miss time specifically for the elbow.

Seager was available for the final two months of the regular season. He certainly didn’t let the elbow injury slow him down at the plate. The five-time All-Star slashed.269/.332/.472 with 10 homers after coming off the IL at the end of July. His strikeout rate, which had been unusually high in the first half, dropped to a more typical 20.3%.

Injuries have hindered Seager over the past few seasons. After reaching 663 plate appearances in his first year with the Rangers (2022), that number has gone down in each of the subsequent campaigns. Seager has played in 102 games in each of the past two years.

articles.title: Reviewing The Athletics’ Young Hitters
body: The Athletics were hampered by several major injuries to an up-and-coming lineup this season. Nick Kurtz, Brent Rooker, Shea Langeliers, and Tyler Soderstrom all missed significant time. An offense that ranked 12th in scoring in 2025 slipped to 20th in 2026.

The absences in the middle of the order opened up playing time for a handful of inexperienced bats. The A’s got a good look at several players who could contribute in 2027, even when everyone is healthy. Here’s a look at each young hitter and where they might fit in the plans for next season.

Bolte repeated Triple-A to begin the year, but quickly proved too talented for the level. He slashed.348/.418/.658 with a dozen homers and 17 steals across 37 games with Las Vegas. Bolte was promoted for his big-league debut in mid-May. He got off to an uninspiring start, carrying a.690 OPS into the All-Star Break.

The former second-round pick took off over the final two months of the season. Bolte hit.307 with eight homers and nine steals from August on. He scored 37 runs in 52 games as a reliable table setter in the leadoff spot. Bolte sprinted through the finish line of his rookie season with a.945 OPS in September.

Bolte wasn’t just a major contributor with the bat. He also posted 5 Defensive Runs Saved in center field. The strong debut campaign, and particularly the sizzling stretch to close the season, likely earned Bolte the Opening Day gig in center field next year.

articles.title: Pirates Promote Justin Newman To Director Of Amateur Scouting
body: When he met with reporters in late September, Pirates general manager Ben Cherington revealed that he planned to hire a full-time scouting director. Two weeks later, Cherington accomplished his goal. The Pirates have promoted Justin Newman to director of amateur scouting, Colin Beazley of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports.

Newman, a University of Rochester alumnus, has worked in various positions with the Pirates since he joined their front office in 2017. He had been their director of player analysis since 2025. Newman’s main focus has been on the draft in recent years, according to Beazley. In his new position, the 31-year-old will replace Justin Horowitz, who left last October to become the Nationals’ assistant GM.

Horowitz was only with the Pirates for the 2024 and’25 drafts, but they appear to have struck gold in both years. The Pirates used their first-round picks on shortstop Konnor Griffin (ninth overall) and right-hander Seth Hernandez (sixth) when Horowitz was in the organization. Griffin was so highly regarded as a prospect that he scored a nine-year, $140MM extension last April. He went on to impress as a 20-year-old rookie. Hernandez, also 20, is on the shortlist of the best pitching prospects in baseball.

Between Horowitz’s exit and Newman’s promotion, Pittsburgh relied on assistant GM Kevan Graves to oversee its draft in 2026. With Graves at the helm, the team used the fifth overall selection on former LSU outfielder Derek Curiel. Graves also led the hiring process for the director of amateur scouting job, per Beazley.

articles.title: Paul DePodesta Discusses Rockies’ Pitching Struggles
body: If you want to take a glass-half-full approach with the long-struggling Rockies, they won 15 more games in 2026 than they did last year. If you want to take a glass-half-empty approach, they went 6-18 in September and clinched the majors’ worst record (58-104) for the second straight season. Colorado has lost triple-digit games four years in a row, and the team hasn’t come close to going.500 or better since a 91-72 effort in 2018. The Rockies’ ace that year was left-hander Kyle Freeland, who overcame hitter-friendly Coors Field to finish fourth in National League Cy Young voting.
[RELATED: Rockies Offseason Outlook]

While Freeland is still a Rockie to this day, he has not approached the success he had eight years ago. He was good for 202 1/3 innings of 2.85 ERA ball then, but the soft-tossing 33-year-old just wrapped up a season in which he posted a 6.65 ERA in 135 1/3 frames. Freeland was a major part of a staff that ranked last in the sport in ERA (5.59), and the Rockies’ run prevention issues weren’t limited to Coors Field. They had a better road ERA (5.35; it was 5.83 at home), but they still came in second to last in that category.

Meanwhile, although the Rockies’ offense tied for last in the league in wRC+ (91), only six teams scored more runs. It’s clear pitching was the main culprit for yet another rough season. President of baseball operations Paul DePodesta acknowledged as much at his end-of-season press conference on Tuesday, as Kyle Newman of the Denver Post relays.

articles.title: Three Players Elect Minor League Free Agency
body: A trio of former big leaguers reached the open market earlier this week. They head to free agency in search of another opportunity in the majors next season. These free agent decisions come from the MiLB.com transactions page.

Lawrence spent his first four seasons as a member of the Rockies, with whom he pitched to a 5.43 ERA over 194 innings and 182 appearances. The right-hander joined the Pirates via waivers ahead of the 2025 season, and though elbow issues limited him to 17 innings, the results were excellent. Lawrence posted a microscopic 0.51 ERA with strikeout, walk and ground-ball rates of 33.3%, 11.6% and 47.2%, respectively. The Pirates may have thought they had a gem on their hands then, but the wheels fell off for Lawrence this season. The 31-year-old pitched poorly enough for the Pirates to designate him for assignment in late May and then trade him to the Twins for cash considerations. Lawrence only lasted a few weeks with Minnesota, which designated him June 21. The Nationals claimed Lawrence, but they wound up outrighting him a month later.

All told, the sinkerballer threw 34 1/3 frames among the three teams and was lit up for a 7.34 ERA. The rest of Lawrence’s numbers from last year also sharply declined, as he fanned hitters at a 24.3% clip, walked them at a 15.8% rate and induced grounders 42.4% of the time.

articles.title: Jakob Marsee, Tyler Zuber To Undergo Elbow Surgery
body: Marlins outfielder Jakob Marsee and right-hander Tyler Zuber had visits with Dr. Keith Meister at the end of the season. Those appointments don’t usually end well, and that’s the case this time around. The Marlins shared that Marsee and Zuber are both slated for elbow surgery on Monday, relays Kevin Barral of Fish On First.

Marsee is looking at a six-month absence. He’ll have an internal brace procedure to repair the UCL in his throwing arm. As a position player, his recovery timeline will be shorter, but he’ll still be hard-pressed to return in time for Opening Day.

There was no indication during the season that Marsee was dealing with an injury. President of baseball operations told reporters in his end-of-season press conference that Marsee’s left elbow was barking down the stretch. Bendix added that Marsee “was banged up all season with a lot of different things.” The elbow issue certainly didn’t affect his performance. September was Marsee’s best month of the year, as he posted a.985 OPS with three homers and two steals.

Marsee delivered a respectable campaign in his first full season in the majors. He posted a perfectly league-average 100 wRC+ with a decent mix of power and speed. Marsee reached base at a solid.348 clip and spent a decent chunk of the year atop Miami’s lineup. The glove was a mixed bag. Marsee finished with -9 Defensive Runs Saved, but 9 Outs Above Average. Statcast gave him positive marks for range but a negative score for his arm. The elbow soreness could’ve played a factor there.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Minnesota Twins
body: By some measures, the Twins’ season was a pleasant surprise. Minnesota was in contention for much of the first half and even operated as buyers at the deadline. On the other hand, their dalliance with contention stemmed more from an almost unfathomably mediocre American League, where most of the league was at least nominally in contention through the first several months. By season’s end, the Twins were sitting on a 77-85 record that was more or less in line with preseason expectations after 2025’s deadline teardown and a pretty quiet offseason. There are already signs that this winter, however, will be more active.

Byron Buxton, OF: $30MM through 2028 (up to $10.5MM in annual incentives based on plate appearances and MVP voting) Pablo López, RHP: $21.5MM through 2027 Victor Caratini, C: $10MM through 2027 (includes $3.5MM buyout of 2028 mutual option) Jeff Hoffman, RHP: $7.25MM through 2027 (Blue Jays paying $3.75MM of Hoffman’s $11MM salary) Other Financial Commitments

$20MM owed to Astros ($10MM in 2027, $10MM in 2028) as part of 2025 Carlos Correa trade $25K buyout on 2027 mutual option for Justin Topa (released in May) Total 2027 commitments: $60.275MM Total long-term commitments: $88.775MM through 2028

Joe Ryan, RHP: $13MM mutual option with $100K buyout (remains arbitration-eligible if option declined) Josh Bell, 1B/DH: $10MM mutual option with $1.25MM buyout Arbitration-Eligible Players (service time in parentheses; salary projections via MLBTR contributor Matt Swartz)

articles.title: Matt Kleine, Rob Cerfolio Candidates In Athletics’ GM Search
body: The Athletics are looking for a new front office leader. According to reporting from Patrick Mooney and Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic, Brewers assistant general manager Matt Kleine is on the list of candidates, though it’s not specified if he has interviewed for the gig. The report mentions that Cardinals assistant general manager Rob Cerfolio has interviewed with the A’s but he is expected that he will stay with his current club. Per the report, he is more likely to be promoted to general manager with the Cards, working under president of baseball operations Chaim Bloom.

Kleine was been with the Brewers for many years, first getting hired to work in the scouting department in 2007. He was promoted to assistant general manager in November of 2023, working under president of baseball operations Matt Arnold.

The Brewers have a reputation for being one of the most savvy teams, putting together winning ball clubs annually despite running low payrolls. They have made the postseason in eight of the past nine seasons and had the best record in the majors in 2026. Kleine has already been connected to the Astros’ front office search and is apparently on the radar of the A’s as well.

articles.title: How Did Eduardo Rodriguez Do That?
body: Left-hander Eduardo Rodriguez posted an ERA over 5.00 in his first two seasons with the Diamondbacks. His four-year, $80MM contract looked like an albatross halfway through the deal. And then out of nowhere, Rodriguez emerged as one of the unlikeliest aces in the league.

The 33-year-old Rodriguez put together one of his most effective campaigns as a big leaguer in 2026. He ranked 5th in the National League with a 2.89 ERA. The four guys ahead of him are the top NL Cy Young candidates (Jacob Misiorowski, Chris Sale, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Jesus Luzardo).

Similar to his Red Sox days, Rodriguez limited hard contact at an above average clip. He ranked in the 89th percentile in hard-hit rate and in the 83rd percentile in average exit velocity. These were skills he’d shown before, just not in recent seasons. The main difference these days is that the strikeouts have dried up. Rodriguez posted a career-low 18.1% strikeout rate. He had the fourth-lowest called+swinging-strike rate among qualified pitchers.

The reliance on soft contact, combined with a subpar groundball rate and minimal punchouts, made Rodriguez’s performance look suspect. The ERA estimators certainly didn’t buy it. He finished with a 4.27 xERA, a 4.44 xFIP, and a 4.62 SIERA. Those marks are right in line with his numbers from 2025, including an identical xFIP.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Toronto Blue Jays
body: The reigning American League champions couldn’t even manage a winning record in 2026, as the Blue Jays fell to 79-83 and last place in the AL East. The Jays were set back by a ton of injuries, but beyond just hoping for improved health, the club needs to fix a lackluster offense.

Vladimir Guerrero Jr., 1B: $450MM through 2039 Dylan Cease, SP: $165MM through 2032 Andres Gimenez, SS: $71.5MM through 2029 (includes $2.5MM buyout of $23MM club option for 2030) Anthony Santander, OF/DH: $49MM through 2029 (includes $5MM buyout of $15MM club option for 2030; Santander has opt-out after 2027 season that Jays can override by increasing salary and exercising 2030 option) Kazuma Okamoto, 3B: $48MM through 2029 Jose Berrios, SP: $48MM through 2028 (Berrios can opt out of contract after 2026 season) Alejandro Kirk, C: $44.5MM through 2030 Tyler Rogers, RP: $25MM through 2028 (includes $1MM buyout of $9MM club option for 2029; club option can vest at $12MM based on appearance thresholds and health) Cody Ponce, SP: $22MM through 2028 Yariel Rodriguez, RP: $12MM through 2028 (includes $6MM player option for 2028; Blue Jays have $10.3MM club option if Rodriguez declines) Other Financial Commitments
$3.75MM to Twins to cover portion of Jeff Hoffman’s 2027 salary 2027 guarantees: $188.375MM Total future commitments: $935MM

articles.title: Taylor Rogers Plans To Pitch In 2027
body: With his 11th MLB season now in the books, Taylor Rogers intends to make it an even dozen in what will be his age-36 season. The Minnesota Star Tribune’s Bobby Nightengale writes that Rogers would ideally like either another season with the Twins, or to sign with the Blue Jays to reunite with his twin brother Tyler in Toronto’s bullpen.

After spending the first six years of his career with Minnesota, Rogers pitched for five different teams over the 2022-25 seasons before returning to the Twin Cities on a one-year, $2MM free agent deal last winter. Rogers posted a 4.33 ERA and a similar 4.58 SIERA over 60 1/3 innings, with below-average walk (11.2%) and strikeout (19.6%) rates. Both the strikeout rate and Rogers’ 34.6% grounder rates were the lowest of his career.

On the plus side, Rogers’ 28% hard-hit ball rate was not just the best of his career, but also in the 98th percentile of all pitchers in 2026. A.331 BABIP meant that Rogers didn’t receive as much benefit one might expect from inducing all that soft contact. Rogers’ 6% homer rate was also a career best, as the southpaw allowed only five home runs in his 60 1/3 frames. As one might expect, Rogers was much more effective against left-handed batters (.696 OPS) than against righties (.860 OPS), but he faced both types of hitters in almost equal measure, as Rogers’ chief role was to cover lower-leverage situations.

articles.title: The Playoffs Are Revealing The Future White Sox Rotation
body: The terms “starter” and “reliever” don’t mean much to the White Sox. The club has consistently employed openers and bulk pitchers in lieu of typical starters this season. The postseason has been no different. Sean Burke made a somewhat normal start in the clincher against the Astros, but two quasi-starters came in after him (Anthony Kay, Erick Fedde). The other two games have followed the more typical all-hands-on-deck blueprint.

Fedde and Sean Newcomb are pending free agents. The rest of the hodgepodge pitching staff will be back next season. The group of potential starters includes Davis Martin, David Sandlin, and Noah Schultz, along with the aforementioned Burke. Trade deadline acquisition Luis Castillo will also be back in 2027. He hit the IL in the final week of the regular season, which helped the club avoid a decision on his status for the playoff roster.

The White Sox beat the Guardians in Game 1 of the ALDS. Their season is far from over, but they’re already getting hints about how the rotation could shake out next season. Two young arms are making a name for themselves on the biggest stage.

Grant Taylor just had his longest outing of the season. He pitched the final four innings to secure the save in Cleveland. The righty struck out six and allowed just two baserunners in a dominant performance.

articles.title: The Pirates Nailed The Brandon Lowe Trade
body: The Astros went into last offseason in search of rotation depth. The Rays were looking to offload a cumbersome contract (by their standards). Enter the Pirates, who seized the opportunity and came away with a tremendous trade haul.

Pittsburgh landed second baseman Brandon Lowe, left-hander Mason Montgomery, and outfielder Jake Mangum in the three-team deal. The club sent right-hander Mike Burrows to Houston. The Astros routed a pair of prospects (outfielder Jacob Melton, righty Anderson Brito) to the Rays.

While all three players acquired in the swap made an impact for Pittsburgh, Lowe was the headliner. He smashed 35 home runs as a critical piece in a lineup that has lacked thump in recent years. Lowe finished with an.824 OPS, his best mark since his breakout 2021 season.

The Pirates finished sixth in scoring this season. They flirted with the top spot at times over the summer, but faded late as injuries to key bats thinned out the lineup. It was a huge turnaround after the club finished dead last in runs per game in 2025. Pittsburgh had finished in the bottom 10 in scoring every season since 2018. Even that year, the team ranked 20th. It’s been an inept offense for quite some time.

articles.title: Six Players Elect Minor League Free Agency
body: Six known players have elected minor league free agency in the past three days. While Major League free agents hit the open market five days after the end of the World Series, these eligible minor leaguers finished the season on outright assignments, so they’re able to get a head start on free agency. For further reference, these free agent decisions are all listed on the official MLB.com or MiLB.com transactions pages.

The 33-year-old Alexander got recalled and optioned three separate times early in the season and eventually spent most of it with Triple-A Sugar Land. He had a 5.26 ERA in 87 1/3 innings there with a middling 18.5% strikeout rate. He did throw six scoreless innings for Houston on May 19th, but he allowed 19 earned runs in his other 12 1/3 innings this year. The Astros designated him for assignment in late September. Alexander has a 47.5% ground ball rate in parts of three seasons in the Majors, so he’ll latch on somewhere as a depth option.

Formerly a staple of the Nationals’ bullpen, Rainey only tossed seven big league frames for the Tigers this year. He pitched 47 2/3 innings for Triple-A Toledo and was serviceable there, posting a 3.40 ERA with a 32.7% strikeout rate. Walks have been a problem throughout his career, and this year was no exception, as Rainey gave out free passes at a 14.1% clip in Toledo. Detroit designated him for assignment on August 31st and outrighted him two days later.

articles.title: Guardians, White Sox Announce ALDS Rosters
body: For the first time in the two franchises’ mutual 126 seasons of existence, the White Sox and Guardians will meet in the postseason. Hagen Smith starts (or, more accurately, opens) for Chicago against Guards starter Parker Messick in Game 1 of the ALDS this afternoon in Cleveland, and both clubs have now officially released their series rosters.

The Pale Hose made just one change to the 26-man roster that swept the Astros in the AL Wild Card Series, as righty Tyler Davis joins the roster in place of Huascar Brazoban. After starter Sean Burke was removed after four innings in Game 2, Brazoban was the first reliever out of the pen, but he retired only one of three batters faced. Anthony Kay replaced Brazoban and issued a walk but got out of the jam, preserving Chicago’s 4-3 lead. Brazoban was acquired by the Mets at the trade deadline, but posted a 4.40 ERA over 14 1/3 innings for the Sox and also spent close to a month on the injured list due to a left lat strain.

The five-year MLB veteran will be replaced by Davis, one of many rookies who have contributed to the upstart Sox roster. It’s a nice birthday present for Davis, who turns 28 years old today. Davis made his MLB debut on April 25, and he posted a 3.66 ERA, 21.1% strikeout rate, and 12.5% walk rate over 32 innings out of Chicago’s bullpen. The Sox never used Davis against Cleveland in the regular season, so the rookie represents a potential fresh challenge to Guardians hitters.

articles.title: Jose Urquidy Remains Free Agent
body: 5:00pm: Multiple sources, including Antonio Puesán, now report that Urquidy has not signed a deal with the Pirates. It appears it was a mistake in the MLB.com transaction logs. Urquidy remains a free agent.

4:40pm: Veteran righty Jose Urquidy cleared waivers and elected free agency on Wednesday. He didn’t have to wait long to find a new gig. Urquidy is headed back to the Pirates on a minor league deal, per his MLB.com transactions tracker.

The 31-year-old Urquidy first joined Pittsburgh last offseason. He reached a $1.5MM major league agreement with the club and opened the year as the Pirates’ long reliever. Urquidy was sent down just three weeks into the season. He was knocked around for six earned runs in 6 1/3 innings.

Pittsburgh designated Urquidy for assignment in late July. He was soon traded to the White Sox. The righty pitched decently in six games with Chicago, but was DFAed again in mid-September. The Phillies scooped him up to provide some length over the final two weeks of the season. After two appearances, Philadelphia DFAed Urquidy last week.

Urquidy posted a 4.95 ERA across 36 1/3 innings in the big leagues. While the results weren’t great, the workload is significant. Injuries limited Urquidy to just 34 1/3 innings between the minors and majors over the previous two years. He tossed 95 2/3 frames in 20 minor league starts this season, giving him 132 innings for the year. It’s the most he’s thrown since tossing a career-high 164 1/3 innings with the Astros in 2022.

articles.title: Mariners Claim Michael Toglia
body: The Mariners have claimed first baseman Michael Toglia off waivers from the Reds, per a team announcement. It wasn’t previously reported that Cincinnati had placed Toglia on waivers. He’d been on the 60-day IL since early September after dislocating his shoulder.

Cincinnati added Toglia on a minor league deal over the winter after Colorado dropped him from the 40-man roster. He had a nice season in Louisville, slashing.273/.373/.547 with 22 dingers in only 402 trips to the plate before being selected to the big league roster in mid-August. It was a short stay on the active roster, however, as Toglia appeared in only 10 games and took just 28 plate appearances before suffering his shoulder injury, which required season-ending surgery.

The 6’5″, 225-pound Toglia is a switch-hitting former first-round pick who was a well-regarded prospect in the Rockies organization but has never made enough contact to sustain a role in the majors. He did log a career-high 458 plate appearances and belt 25 homers back in 2024, but a 32.1% strikeout rate undercut that power and left him with a.218/.311/.456 batting line (99 wRC+). He followed that with a brutal.190/.258/.353 showing in 337 plate appearances the next season, during which his strikeout rate soared north of 39%. That led the Rockies to designate him for assignment and non-tender him last November.

articles.title: Reds Announce Coaching Updates
body: The Reds head into the offseason with multiple roles to fill on the coaching staff under manager Terry Francona. The club confirmed pitching coach Derek Johnson won’t be back next season. Cincinnati also dismissed assistant hitting coach Will Remillard, president of baseball operations Nick Krall and general manager Brad Meador told reporters, including Charlie Goldsmith of Fox 19 Now.

Remillard has been on the big-league staff for the past two seasons. He’d been a minor league coach in the Cubs’ organization since 2019 before joining the Reds. Remillard worked under hitting coach /director of hitting Chris Valaika in Cincinnati. Remillard, Valaika, and assistant hitting coach Alex Pelaez were all hired heading into the 2025 season with Francona taking over as skipper.

Elly De La Cruz put together his most complete offensive season in 2026. His costar, Sal Stewart, is a strong candidate to win NL Rookie of the Year. Outside of De La Cruz and Stewart, the Reds struggled mightily on offense. Cincinnati scored the 4th-fewest runs this season. The club ranked dead last in wRC+.

Meador said the organization is looking for a coach with more experience to help the offense. The lineup is projected to look largely the same next season, barring any major offseason additions. Third baseman Eugenio Suarez has a $16MM mutual option for 2027 that the Reds are unlikely to pick up. Catcher Tyler Stephenson is a free agent. Krall said they’d keep in touch with him. The rest of the group will return next year.

articles.title: Byron Buxton Ready For 2027, Twins Not Planning To Trade Him
body: Twins outfielder Byron Buxton battled hip injuries for most of his 2026 campaign. The issue finally led to surgery in September. Buxton is progressing well in his recovery and is on track to be healthy for the 2027 season, per Dan Hayes of The Athletic.
Buxton had arthroscopic right hip surgery on September 18. He’ll continue to rehab the injury through December, and then turn his attention toward preparing for next season.

“I’m just trying to make sure I do everything I’m supposed to,” Buxton said, relayed by Hayes. “It’s been good. I feel better. It’s good to be able to feel a little bit better since then. I’m moving around a little bit, so that’s progress, for sure.”

While he didn’t go on the IL until July, Buxton dealt with nagging hip pain as early as May. He played through the injury and put up a monster first half. Buxton posted a.926 OPS in June, including eight home runs. He aggravated the hip injury on a stolen base attempt against the Yankees on July 5 and went on the IL. The ailment was initially described as a hip strain.

Buxton returned shortly after the All-Star Break, but only made it through seven games. He was pulled from a matchup against the Athletics and went right back on the IL. This time, the injury was termed a hip impingement. Buxton made it through 11 games in August before going on the IL a third and final time.

articles.title: Krall Discusses Reds’ Position Player Needs
body: The Reds enter the offseason looking to rebound from a last place finish in the NL Central. They have deficiencies in virtually every part of the roster but will certainly need to improve an offense that ranked at the bottom of the National League in scoring.

President of baseball operations Nick Krall and general manager Brad Meador met with reporters (including Charlie Goldsmith of Fox 19 Now) to address the priorities on the position player side. Krall noted the team’s deficiencies at the bottom of the roster, where the Reds gave 100+ plate appearances to seven players who had an OPS below.650: Ke’Bryan Hayes, TJ Friedl, Edwin Arroyo, Noelvi Marte, Jose Trevino, Matt McLain and Will Benson. Friedl and Benson have been dropped from the roster.

Trevino and Hayes are signed for next season. McLain is into his arbitration window. Marte and Arroyo are both pre-arbitration and have minor league options remaining. They both finished the season in Triple-A. Krall didn’t pull any punches on Marte’s performance, in particular. “Noelvi Marte was bad. We should have sent him down earlier than we did,” he said. The former top prospect batted.189/.229/.321 in 63 big league contests and was optioned for the second time in the middle of August.
[Related: Reds Offseason Outlook]

articles.title: Royals Outright Luke Little
body: The Royals assigned left-hander Luke Little outright to Triple-A Omaha, according to the MLB.com transaction tracker. The log indicates that Kansas City technically designated him for assignment on Monday, though the team never announced the move.

Kansas City claimed Little off waivers from the Cubs at the beginning of August. He spent the rest of the season in Omaha on an optional assignment. Little was bombed for 21 runs (19 earned) across 11 1/3 frames with the Storm Chasers. He put far too many hitters aboard, walking 12 and hitting four while throwing three wild pitches. Little had also walked almost a batter per inning with the Cubs’ top affiliate earlier in the season. He finished the season with a 7.28 ERA and an untenable 18% walk percentage in 44 Triple-A appearances.

Little has above-average velocity and cuts an imposing on-mound presence at 6’8″ and 220 pounds. He has yet to sync his mechanics enough to consistently find the strike zone. Little has managed a 2.97 ERA across 36 1/3 career big league frames, yet it’s required him to work around a near-18% walk rate. The free passes have led to more runs in the minor leagues. Little has a 4.62 ERA over parts of four Triple-A campaigns.

This is the first career outright assignment for Little, but he has played parts of seven seasons in the minors. That’ll give him the right to elect minor league free agency at the beginning of the offseason. He’ll be out of options next season and is likely to be limited to non-roster invites to camp.

articles.title: Reds Outright Ivan Johnson
body: The Reds sent infielder Ivan Johnson outright to Triple-A Louisville, relays Charlie Goldsmith of Charlie’s Chalkboard. Cincinnati never officially designated Johnson for assignment but apparently placed him on waivers this week.

Johnson, 28 next week, was Cincinnati’s fourth-round pick back in 2019. The switch-hitter had some prospect buzz early in his time in the Reds’ system, with some scouts projecting him as a bat-first utility player. Johnson has posted solid offensive numbers in the minors but struggles with contact against higher level pitching. He also hasn’t really found a defensive home.

Cincinnati called Johnson up for the first time at the end of June. He was up and down on a couple occasions but never got much of a look. The Atlanta native went 1-16 with three walks and seven punchouts in his first 19 plate appearances. His lone knock was a single off Gavin Williams in late July. Johnson had a solid but not elite season with Louisville, hitting.247/.354/.424 with 11 longballs and 15 stolen bases over 273 trips to the plate.

This is Johnson’s first career outright assignment, so he can’t immediately elect free agency. That’s a mere formality, though, as he’ll hit the market at the beginning of the offseason as a seven-year minor league free agent. He’s likely looking at minor league offers, and Cincinnati could try to bring him back on a non-roster invite to Spring Training.

articles.title: Jameson Taillon To Undergo Flexor Surgery, Intends To Continue Career
body: Impending free agent starter Jameson Taillon tells Shi Davidi of Sportsnet that he’s scheduled for flexor surgery next week. The veteran right-hander acknowledged there’s a chance he’ll also require an internal brace repair of his UCL.

The surgery seems likely to cost Taillon most or all of the 2027 season. (It’s highly likely he’d miss the entire year if there’s a ligament repair.) Taillon stressed that he’s going this route because he intends to get fully healthy and continue his career. The former second overall pick turns 35 in November and would be eyeing a comeback for his age-36 campaign if he’s out until 2028.

It doesn’t come as a huge surprise, as Taillon revealed two weeks ago that he was undergoing multiple opinions on the elbow injury that sent him to the shelf on September 4. He tells Davidi that the soreness hasn’t really subsided within the past month. While Taillon weighed non-surgical treatment plans, he decided to go back under the knife and hope for a late-career act after the operation.

Taillon has already twice undergone full Tommy John reconstructions — as a prospect in 2014 and again in August’19 after he’d established himself as a big leaguer. It’s not uncommon for pitchers to require revisions or another full repair within five to seven years of a previous ligament surgery. It at least doesn’t appear Taillon will need a third full Tommy John reconstruction. Only three pitchers (Jason Isringhausen, Jonny Venters and Tejay Antone) are known to have returned to the big leagues after three Tommy John procedures. They’re all relievers.

articles.title: 2026-27 Club Option Preview: October Edition
body: The regular season is now done, which means it’s almost time for decisions to be made on contract options. MLBTR looked at the player options last month. Now let’s turn to the club options. For the sake of streamlining this post, mutual options have not been included, as it’s been over a decade since a mutual option has been picked up by both sides.

Jeff McNeil, 2B: $15.75MM club option (Mets responsible for $2MM buyout as part of December trade) The A’s picked up McNeil from the Mets in the offseason. The Mets were mostly looking to dump some salary, while the A’s were hoping to get a veteran utility guy for their young roster. For the most part, that didn’t work out for the A’s. McNeil had a poor season overall, though he was at least trending in the right direction.

On the whole, McNeil stepped to the plate 520 times with a.264/.313/.368 line and 83 wRC+. That splits up as a.226/.290/.302 line and 59 wRC+ in the first half, compared to a.310/.342/.451 slash and 114 wRC+ in the second half. That’s nice momentum but McNeil has still barely been replacement level this year and will turn 35 in April, so the A’s should walk away. Even if they want to bring McNeil back, they should be able to re-sign him for less than the option price.

articles.title: Blue Jays Notes: Clement, DH, Rotation
body: Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins spoke with the Toronto beat on Wednesday, addressing various aspects of the roster. Shi Davidi of Sportsnet was among those to relay the comments, which Jays fans are encouraged to give a full read.

Atkins was most notably noncommittal about the second base position, where Ernie Clement started 107 games this year. Atkins said Clement would need to “earn every bit of that” when asked if he’d be the starting second baseman in 2027. The GM left the door open to Clement winning the job, saying “when he’s been given an opportunity, he’s run with it.”

Clement had his best season last year and was a postseason hero during Toronto’s run to an AL pennant. He wasn’t nearly as impactful this season, hitting.259/.285/.364 across 621 plate appearances. Clement had an All-Star first half but was a liability down the stretch, batting.203/.235/.259 in the second half.

That leaves second base as an obvious area to address for an underperforming Toronto offense. The Jays scored the fewest runs in MLB and had a league-low 152 home runs. They were among the best teams in the league at putting the ball in play — only the Rays had a lower strikeout rate — but didn’t hit for power and had the AL’s lowest walk rate. The Jays rode a contact-heavy approach to success in 2025, but they became too one-dimensional this year.

articles.title: Joe Mantiply Elects Free Agency
body: Veteran left-hander Joe Mantiply is a free agent, per his MLB.com transactions page. The reliever was designated for assignment by the Blue Jays last week. Mantiply passed through waivers unclaimed. He’d been outrighted before, so he had the option to reject a minor league assignment and choose free agency.

Mantiply closed the 2025 campaign in the Blue Jays organization after getting cut by the Diamondbacks midway through last season. He entered free agency over the winter but re-signed with Toronto on a minor league deal. Mantiply debuted with the club in early April. He carried a strong 2.04 ERA into mid-May, but went down with a knee injury. Mantiply eventually needed arthroscopic surgery to address the issue.

After recovering from knee surgery, Mantiply struggled. He permitted five earned runs over eight appearances in September. The lefty was bumped off the roster during the final week of the regular season.

The 35-year-old Mantiply has never been a hard thrower, but his velocity ticked down even more this season. He sat at a career-low 88.2 mph with his sinker. Opponents hit.347 against the pitch, which Mantiply throws nearly half the time. His curveball and changeup averaged right around 80 mph. The arsenal helped Mantiply generate a strong 58.3% groundball rate. That came with a double-digit barrel rate and a 25% pulled air rate. Mantiply was likely fortunate to finish with a 3.00 ERA, as evidenced by his 5.40 xERA.

articles.title: 12 Players Elect Free Agency
body: Now that the season is over, we’ll start seeing several players choose to become minor league free agents. Major League free agents (i.e. players with six-plus years of big league service time) will hit the open market five days after the end of the World Series, but eligible minor leaguers can already start electing free agency.

To qualify, these players must have been all outrighted off their team’s 40-man rosters during the 2026 season without being added back. These players also must have multiple career outrights on their resume, and/or at least three years of Major League service time.

MLB Trade Rumors will offer periodic updates over the coming weeks about many other players hitting the market in this fashion. These free agent decisions are all listed on the official MLB.com or MILB.com transactions pages, for further reference.

articles.title: Tom Pohlad: Twins Will “Meaningfully Invest” In Payroll, Plan To Contend In 2027
body: 2026 marked the first season of Tom Pohlad as the Twins’ designated control person, with Pohlad becoming his family’s representative in league ownership matters and the franchise’s executive chair. Derek Falvey’s surprising departure as the president of baseball operations in January (and GM Jeremy Zoll becoming the new head of baseball ops) marked the first step in a new direction under Pohlad, who walked back some of the club’s rebuilding direction with a goal towards “playing meaningful baseball in September.”

The Twins were still above the.500 mark at the end of July, but a 21-30 record in the final two months of play dropped Minnesota to 77-85 — a seven-game improvement over 2025, but not a quantum leap ahead. Pohlad made it clear today that more is expected from the club next season, as Pohlad, Zoll, and manager Derek Shelton addressed the media during an end-of-year press conference. (Bobby Nightengale of the Minnesota Star Tribune, Betsy Helfand of the St. Paul Pioneer Press, Aaron Gleeman, and MLB.com’s Matthew Leach were among the reporters on hand.)

“I understand the patience in this market has run out, and I assure you we have a sense of urgency,” Pohlad said. “Our goal this offseason is to field a roster next spring where making the playoffs isn’t a hope; it’s the expectation that everybody in this room agrees is realistic.”

articles.title: Liam Hendriks Announces Retirement
body: In a very amusing and self-deprecating post on his Instagram page, veteran reliever Liam Hendriks has announced his retirement after 14 big league seasons. The 37-year-old Hendriks cited the fans, his family (“a huge thank you to my wife for always believing in me, which was honestly a terrifying display of delusion on her part “), past rivals like Salvador Perez (“who I am completely convinced [treated] my heater like a light afternoon snack “), his “miracle worker” of an agent, and many others who played a role in his career.

“As for what’s next: My immediate retirement plans include testing whether my elbow can survive holding onto the leash when my dog sees a rabbit, and choosing a new hobby where being single-handedly responsible for losing a game doesn’t lead to ESPN SportsCenter breaking down my psychological collapse in slow motion for the next 24 hours. Thanks for the ride. It’s been an absolute blast.”

Hendriks’ impressive resume is highlighted by back-to-back AL Reliever Of The Year awards in 2020 and 2021, and he also received down-ballot Cy Young Award votes in those two standout seasons. One of only a few dozen Australians to play in Major League Baseball, Hendriks is one of just four Aussies (along with Dave Nilsson, Grant Balfour, and Travis Bazzana) to make an All-Star Game, and Hendriks is the only one of that group to earn All-Star recognition multiple times, receiving three nods for the Midsummer Classic.

articles.title: Royals To Replace Hitting Coach Alec Zumwalt
body: The Royals are planning to replace hitting coach Alec Zumwalt, reports Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic. He’s being reassigned within the organization and not fired, however. Zumwalt will continue on in his role as the team’s senior director of hitting performance but apparently won’t be in uniform and working with the big league staff on a daily basis.

Zumwalt has spent more than a decade working with the Royals. The former Braves fourth-rounder (1999) joined the Royals as a scout in 2013 after his minor league playing days ended. Then-Royals GM Dayton Moore was plenty familiar with Zumwalt, having worked in the Braves’ scouting department and front office at the time Atlanta selected him in the draft.

Zumwalt climbed the organizational ladder in Kansas City, moving from advance scout to director of baseball operations and director of player development. The Royals named him the organization’s director of hitting performance following the 2021 season, and by May of 2022 he’d been shifted into the dugout in place of hitting coach Terry Bradshaw, who was let go after the team started the season mired in a dreadful offensive funk.

articles.title: Angels Notes: Mozeliak, Suzuki, Trout
body: The Angels just wrapped up their first 100-loss season and extended their league-worst playoff drought to 12 years, but fans are optimistic over a change in ownership. Arte Moreno, who purchased the Angels in 2003, recently agreed to sell a majority stake in the franchise to Stan Kroenke.

While the sale is not expected to fully close until the first quarter of 2027, the Angels have important offseason business to conduct in the meantime. It starts with figuring out who will run the Halos’ baseball operations. The team hired longtime Cardinals executive John Mozeliak to take over as interim general manager after the late-June firing of Perry Minasian. Mozeliak was handed the keys through the end of the year, but whether he’s in for the long haul is up in the air.

When discussing his status on Monday, Mozeliak said he had a meeting scheduled today with Kevin Demoff of Kroenke Sports & Entertainment (via Jeff Fletcher of the Orange County Register). It is unclear if that meeting has gotten underway yet, but it could give Mozeliak a better idea of whether he has a future with the franchise. Manager Kurt Suzuki is in a similar boat. If Mozeliak has his way, Suzuki will manage the team again in 2027. However, that isn’t Mozeliak’s call.
“I would like to see him be that, but ultimately that’s not my decision,” said Mozeliak (via Rhett Bollinger of MLB.com).

articles.title: AL West Notes: Daniels, Suzuki, Crawford, Spence
body: Jon Daniels has removed himself from consideration in the Athletics’ search for a new general manager, according to USA Today’s Bob Nightengale. Daniels has been working as a senior advisor in the Rays’ baseball ops department since November 2022, and prefers to stay put and spend more time with his family rather than jumping back into the grind of running a big league front office. From 2005-2022, Daniels led the Rangers’ front office first as the GM and then as the president of baseball operations.

This is the first time that Daniels has been connected at all to the A’s job, but the team is known to be exploring a wide range of candidates. Such names as former Nationals president of baseball ops Mike Rizzo, former Astros GM James Click, Red Sox assistant GMs Mike Groopman and Taylor Smith, and A’s assistant GM Billy Owens have been linked to the Athletics’ search to date. Nightengale reported two weeks ago that the A’s wanted to have a new front office leader hired before the end of the season, but while that day has now passed, one would presume the club would want to make its decision sooner rather than later.

articles.title: Kirby Yates Retires
body: Veteran right-hander Kirby Yates announced his retirement this afternoon following the Pirates’ 4-3 walk-off loss to the Tigers in Detroit. In a game that featured Justin Verlander’s final career start for the Tigers, the Pirates opted for a bullpen game, and manager Don Kelly gave Yates the nod as the opener. It was the first “start” of his big league career after 517 appearances as a reliever. Yates recorded five outs, including a strikeout of Dillon Dingler, before being lifted for Yohan Ramírez.

“It was good, but this was it …” Yates told reporters after the game (link via SportsNet Pittsburgh). “I don’t have anything left. Let’s put it that way. I’ve been running on fumes for a while. I think it’s just time. It’s felt like it’s been time for a little while now. I think I’ve given this game everything I have, and in return, it’s given me more than I can ever thank it for or imagine.”

Yates signed with the Rays in 2009 as an undrafted free agent. He reached the Majors in 2014 as a 27-year-old and delivered a decent 3.75 earned run average in 36 innings, working off a low-90s fastball and a low-80s slider to strike out 26.9% of opponents. Yates struggled to a 6.13 ERA over the next two years with the Rays and Yankees but found something of a groove with the Padres in 2017. In 61 appearances for the Friars, the righty struck out a dominant 38.5% of opponents against an 8.4% walk rate and a 3.72 ERA. Around that time, Yates began to move away from his slider in favor of a mid-80s splitter, which would later become his signature pitch.

articles.title: Pirates Not Expected To Make Leadership Changes For 2027
body: Pirates GM Ben Cherington discussed his own future along with many other topics as part of a season wrap-up interview with reporters (including the Pittsburgh Tribune-Review’s Kevin Gorman and MLB.com’s Aiden Stephansky) on Saturday. In regards to his status, Cherington said he expects to return for his eighth year in charge in the Bucs’ front office, as owner Bob Nutting hasn’t given Cherington any indication otherwise.

“Every conversation I’ve had with Bob is just about that. ‘How do we keep getting better?’ ‘How do we assess this season when we need to learn from it?’ The progress, the things that need to get better and what can we do about that going forward,” Cherington said. “Everything we’ve done, really over time, is building toward October, and every decision we’ve made — and certainly every decision we made over the last 12 months — was all aimed towards that. I don’t think that changes. That can’t change. We got to go into this offseason focused on that and beat the other teams.”

While only Nutting knows exactly how safe Cherington’s job truly is, the GM is under contract through the end of the 2027 campaign, and it would be a little unusual to see Cherington fired after the Pirates’ best season of his tenure. The 81-79 Pirates can clinch a winning record by beating the Tigers today or tomorrow, which would mark the franchise’s first time over the.500 mark since their 82-win season in 2018. Pittsburgh went 76-86 in both 2023 and 2024, which was the previous highwater mark of the seven-year Cherington rebuild era.

articles.title: Giants Claim Camilo Doval
body: The Giants announced that they have claimed right-hander Camilo Doval off waivers from the Pirates. Doval had been designated for assignment by Pittsburgh earlier this week. The Giants transferred righty Blade Tidwell to the 60-day injured list to open a 40-man spot for the move. Tidwell was recommended for UCL surgery this week, so he is certainly done for this year and likely all of next year as well.

It’s a fascinating reunion. Doval was the Giants’ closer not too long ago but some struggles, mostly with control, pushed him to the trade block. He was flipped to the Yankees at last year’s deadline, with the Giants netting prospect Jesús Rodríguez, Trystan Vrieling, Parks Harber, and Carlos De La Rosa in the swap. Doval struggled through a year in the Bronx before getting traded again, this time to the Pirates. Pittsburgh fell out of contention and put Doval on waivers this week to try to save a small amount of money, roughly $98K, per MLBTR contributor Ethan Hullihen.

The Giants helped the Pirates out by making this claim. For San Francisco, it has nothing to do with 2026. They are playing out the string on a lost season, currently sporting a 65-94 record. Even if Doval makes an appearance or two before the season is done, they will be meaningless games. Presumably, the Giants grabbed Doval because they either plan to tender him a contract for 2027 or try to trade him in the offseason.

articles.title: Rockies Outright Vimael Machín
body: The Rockies have sent infielder Vimael Machín outright to the Arizona Complex League, per his transactions tracker at MLB.com. He has the right to elect free agency but the log doesn’t indicate whether he will do so or not.

Machín was selected to the roster on September 5 when Willi Castro landed on the injured list. Ten days later, the club decided to recall Braxton Fulford. Machín was optioned as the corresponding move. In between those moves, Machín got into three games and made six plate appearances. He knocked three singles but also struck out twice. A few days later, when Jose Quintana was reinstated from the 60-day IL, Machín was designated for assignment.

It’s unsurprising that no one claimed Machín off waivers, as he’s a 32-year-old depth guy. This is now the fifth season he has taken part in but he has just 379 plate appearances with a tepid.209/.289/.269 line in those. He has experience at all four infield spots but the lack of offense makes it hard for him to get meaningful playing time.

Machín has been outrighted previously in his career. That gives him the right to reject this assignment and elect free agency. Even if he doesn’t exercise that right for some reason, he would qualify for minor league free agency at season’s end as a guy who has appeared in at least seven seasons on the farm.

articles.title: Offseason Outlook: Kansas City Royals
body: The Royals missed the playoffs for the fifth time in the past six seasons. After an 86-win season netted a Wild Card berth in 2024, they went 82-80 in 2025. This year’s group will win, at most, 73 games. The promising core of a few years ago has been marred by injuries and the aging of several key veterans. Kansas City now heads into the offseason looking for ways to surround their MVP-caliber shortstop with enough complementary pieces to contend. It’s going to be an uphill battle.

Kyle Freeland, Jose Quintana, Tomoyuki Sugano, Jordan Romano, Tyler Freeman (assuming his contract isn’t added back to the roster), Keegan Thompson (assuming his contract isn’t added back to the roster) It has been almost a year since the Rockies hired Paul DePodesta as president of baseball operations. The hope for many fans was that this would signal the start of a new way of doing business. For many prior years, the front office seemed to be loyal to its players to a fault, reluctant to trade them at peak value or when it made logical sense to do so.

articles.title: Rockies Reinstate Jose Quintana, Designate Vimael Machín For Assignment
body: The Rockies announced that they have reinstated left-hander Jose Quintana from the 60-day injured list and designated infielder Vimael Machín for assignment. They optioned righty Gabriel Hughes to Triple-A Albuquerque to make room for Quintana on their 28-man roster.

Quintana, who missed nearly four months with a left elbow sprain, will start against the Mariners on Saturday. The well-traveled 37-year-old and longtime innings eater inked a $6MM deal with the Rockies in the offseason, but he has made just nine starts. In his most recent outing, a May 24 loss to the Diamondbacks, he was crushed for six earned runs on six hits in 1 1/3 frames. Overall, Quintana has pitched to a 5.27 ERA with an unappealing 11% strikeout rate and a 9.4% walk rate in 41 frames. With another trip to free agency looming in the offseason, the one-time All-Star will try to end the season on a positive note.

Machín, 32, joined the Rockies on a minor league deal in December and received a promotion to the majors on Sept. 5. He appeared in three games and went 3 for 6, but the former Athletic and Oriole has hit a non-threatening.209/.289/.269 with two home runs in 379 major league plate appearances. While Machín has slashed a far better.288/.367/.438 with a dozen homers and seven steals in 499 PA in Albuquerque this season, his 94 wRC+ indicates his production has still been 6 percent worse than average in the Pacific Coast League.

articles.title: Royals Claim Spencer Bivens
body: The Royals have claimed right-hander Spencer Bivens off waivers from the Giants and optioned him to Triple-A, Kansas City announced. San Francisco designated Bivens for assignment earlier this week.

Bivens lost his roster spot on Wednesday because of another waiver claim. The Giants added right-hander Duncan Davitt off waivers from the Braves. Bivens has spent his entire pro career with San Francisco. He’s pitched in parts of three big-league seasons.

The 32-year-old Bivens took a winding road to the majors. After two years pitching at Division II Rogers State, he found his way into independent ball. The righty pitched in various outfits in 2020 and 2021. Bivens latched on with the Giants in 2022. He moved quickly through the system. A 2.92 ERA and eight saves at Triple-A in 2024 earned him his first big-league promotion.

Bivens has been an off-and-on member of San Francisco’s bullpen since his debut. His most extensive work came last season, when he appeared in 54 games. Bivens typically operated as a multi-inning reliever, but he also chipped in three saves and four holds. The veteran righty was limited to just four appearances this season. His most recent stint in the majors consisted of two games. Bivens gave up four earned runs in both outings.

articles.title: Rockies Outright Tyler Freeman
body: The Rockies have officially announced Willi Castro’s placement on the 10-day IL and Vimael Machin’s contract selection, which were both reported earlier today. To create space for Machin on the 40-man roster, the Rox outrighted Tyler Freeman to Triple-A. It hadn’t been publicly known that Freeman had been designated for assignment, but he has now cleared waivers.

Because Freeman has more than three years of MLB service time, he has the right to reject this outright assignment in favor of free agency. The Rockies hold two more years of arbitration control over Freeman’s services, but this outright is probably the precursor to a non-tender this winter, so Freeman might prefer to enter free agency now instead of waiting several more weeks or months to hit the open market.

Freeman has hit.247/.317/.314 with three home runs over 288 plate appearances this season, translating to a dismal 67 wRC+. The Rockies used Freeman primarily as a second baseman, right fielder, and DH, but his lack of offensive production reduced his playing time. Back problems probably had something to do with these struggles, as Freeman had a pair of fairly minimal IL stints due to back-related issues. Freeman was activated from the second of these IL stints on August 23 and then optioned to Triple-A Albuquerque.
